_meta.title: Emit Templates — every HTML output shape the converter produces
_meta.purpose: The single home of the converter's HTML forms: element families, callout classes, image/video/audio embeds, the red-flag form, the interactive placeholder, and the page-skeleton fragments keyed by Style_Anchor_Registry field VALUES. ContentConverter.js and SkeletonBuilder.js read THIS file. Changing what any output looks like is an edit here — never a code change.
_meta.grounding: Forms taken from the finished corpus (OSAH401, ANZH205, ARFUN01 …) and Style_Anchor_Registry_Examples.json. Where the corpus varies, the dominant/most-recent form is used and noted.
_meta.placeholders: {curly} tokens are filled by the engine. {content} is the gathered learner content; {classes} is a space-joined class list.
_meta.extension_rule: New style / class / menu shape / footer arrangement = a data edit here. If a change seems to need engine code, stop — design error.
_meta.comment_policy: Only TWO comment uses are permitted converter-wide: Mode P's commented image reference (below) and the ACK-TODO supplement (Acks_Formats.json). The acks lesson-label comments are mandated by the acks spec itself. No other comments are ever emitted.

red_flag.form: Red Flag: {text}

ledger_note_scheme.note: ROUND 219 (Chris, 2026-07-12 — the online HTML Convertor project's Change Ledger folded into PageForge V2; CL-0010 + CL-0013). The design team's SOURCE-SPECIFIC red-note prefix scheme replaces the round-57 CS:/RED FLAG: pair on ALL FUTURE conversions: a WRITER'S own note / CS instruction (kind 'cs') → 'Writers Note:'; a CONVERTER-detected issue (kind 'diagnostic', the default — ambiguity / missing info / unbuildable structure) → 'Red Flag:'; a DEFERRED piece of a known, correctly-built pattern (kind 'todo' — an asset/URL/setup the developer supplies in production; reserved for the doc-14 live-wiring rounds and matches Subject_Global_Parameters._meta.red_note_format byte-for-byte) → 'Designer/Developer To Do:'; a whitelisted Word comment → 'Note from {author}:' (Comment_Authors.render.form). ALL render red AND BOLD ('color: red; font-weight: bold;' — the bold weight is CL-0010's addition), always visible, never a hidden comment. The cv2-note / cv2-comment GATE MARKER classes are UNCHANGED, so every note stays invisible to every protected gate; the compare_structure/body_compare text-prefix exclusions were extended the same round (new prefixes ADDED alongside the legacy ones, so both corpus states pass). NO-REGRESSION MARKING: the human gold strips ALL developer notes, and these prefixes are design-authority decisions the gold predates — recorded in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions (overrides_gold:true) so no stocktake/audit ever chases the wording back toward the gold or the r57 forms. Env NOTESCHEME_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts every note byte-for-byte to the r57/r72 legacy forms (legacy_form / legacy_cs_form here + Comment_Authors.render.legacy_form).

omit_placeholders.note:
Round 89 (Chris, ENGI302-03) ADDS the [Lesson Overview] learning-intentions prompt 'Depending on the size and complexity of your module, it may or may not be relevant for you to add additional Learning Intentions and Success Criteria to frame each lesson.' — the SAME template-placeholder class as round 86 but living per-LESSON in [Lesson Overview]. Stored as the SHARED PREFIX 'depending on the size and complexity of your' because the Fundamentals subjects (HPFUN*/XFUN01) carry a variant ('…your FUNDAMENTAL, …frame THE LEARNING') vs the standard ('…your MODULE, …frame EACH LESSON'); the prefix folds both (and any future 'your course' variant). MEASURED: only those two continuations exist corpus-wide and the human ships NEITHER in any affected module — the distinctive opening is never a real CS note (the only human full-sentence occurrence is non-gated PES1001 where it was merged into a real

). Recurs 24 built dirs / 17 gated; Claude surfaced it on ~73 pages. Round 86 (Chris, CEDW501-00) — OMIT a writer instruction that is verbatim WT TEMPLATE-PLACEHOLDER text the writer never replaced. These are the template's default prompts ('Insert brief introductory text.' / 'Insert appropriate introductory video to pique student interest [max. 3 minutes].' / 'Start with a whakatauki' in [MODULE INTRODUCTION]; 'In this section outline any connections…' in [Connections]; 'Outline any relevant information relating to assessment…'). Leaving them means the writer supplied NO content, so the human OMITS them entirely — they are NOT surfaced as a CS note. The #redFlag emitter (kind 'cs' only) folds the note text (Utils.Fold: lowercase, accents stripped, dashes→hyphen, whitespace collapsed) and, when match=='prefix', drops it if the folded text EQUALS or STARTS WITH any phrase (so the '[max. 3 minutes].' tail and trailing whitespace variants match); no red-flag is counted. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_placeholder_recur.py): the phrases recur across 6–85 modules each (template boilerplate, never a unique writer note) and the human ships 0 of them (verified CEDW501/CEDT501/ENGI201). Diagnostics (kind 'diagnostic': 'Empty [tag]…', missing URL) are never omitted. Env PLACEHOLDER_OFF reverts to surfacing every placeholder as a CS note.

note_tidy._prefixes_note: Round 219 — the CL-0010/CL-0013 ledger prefixes ('Writers Note:' / 'Red Flag:' / 'Designer/Developer To Do:') joined the coalesce list; the legacy 'CS:' / 'RED FLAG:' stay so a NOTESCHEME_OFF (legacy-form) corpus still tidies identically. Matching is case-sensitive startswith, longest-first.
note_tidy.bare_cue_pattern: ^(dev|developer|dev team|cs|creative services|note to dev(eloper)?|note to cs|note for creative services)$
note_tidy._doc:
ROUND 203 (Chris, HPFUN902 — HTMLGen conversion fixes 4 + 5). Post-pass over the FULL assembled page (PageAssembler calls NotesAndComments.TidyDeveloperNotes after OmitPlaceholderResidue, before Indent). THREE behaviours, all on cv2-note

s, all gate-NEUTRAL (cv2-note is excluded from the skeleton, compare_structure, body_compare and the defect leak-scan — round 72): (5a MENU RELOCATE, env MENUNOTE_OFF) a developer comment rendered INSIDE the module menu (a cv2-note before the

boundary — the menu is #header-scoped) is HELD and re-emitted as the FIRST element inside the body, so the developer sees it (Chris: 'avoid leaving comments within a menu since the developer may not see this … generate them in the frontend within the next possible element outside the module menu and inside the normal module body'). MEASURED (outputs/_measure_menucomments.py): 80 pages / 76 modules render a menu note. (5b COALESCE + 4 BARE-CUE FOLD, env COALESCE_OFF) a RUN of consecutive cv2-notes (nothing but whitespace between) sharing the same prefix collapses to ONE note — the first line keeps 'CS:' (or 'RED FLAG:'), the following lines drop the prefix and join with
(Chris: 'if there are multiple comments … one after another … only the first line open with CS:, but not on the other lines straight after'). A note whose body is a bare/bracketed addressee cue ([Dev], [CS], Dev team, 'note to developer') with NO real content is DROPPED (folds forward — the run's prefix carries to the next real line; a standalone bare cue is dropped, issue 4 — WT line 165 '[Dev]' in its own coloured span produced a contentless 'CS: [Dev]' that stripAddresseeCue's delimiter requirement missed). MEASURED: 601 pages / 275 modules have a >=2 run (corpus-wide but gate-neutral); 13 bare-'[Dev]' notes (almost all HPFUN). The human developer DELETES these comments in the final gold (HPFUN902 gold ships 0 cv2-notes) — so the target here is Chris's stated developer-hand-off rule, not the gold; the round-43 'never silently strip a documented instruction' principle is preserved (the comment is retained, just relocated + tidied). Env NOTETIDY_OFF reverts the whole post-pass.
note_tidy.note: cv2-comment (whitelisted Word comments, round 72) are NOT coalesced or relocated by this pass — only cv2-note (the CS / RED FLAG retained writer instructions).

cs_relabel.note: Round 57 — split retained red notes by SOURCE. A writer→Creative-Services note (the round-43 retained instruction: the Instruction_Cues vocabulary + developer-directed questions, plus the undocumented container-positional note) renders with the CS: prefix via cs_form; a converter-emitted TECHNICAL diagnostic (the hardcoded #redFlag messages: empty/malformed tag, missing URL, orphan sub-tag, un-built widget, unmatched menu/container) keeps RED FLAG: via form. The #redFlag emitter picks cs_form only when called with kind='cs'. Greppability preserved per §4.1: 'RED FLAG:' now finds exactly the converter issues, 'CS:' finds the writer notes. Reverts to the round-43 all-RED-FLAG baseline when enabled:false OR env CSRELABEL_OFF is set (gate-safe A/B).

cs_dedupe.note: Round 70 — DEDUPE the doubled CS prefix (Chris, OSAI201-01: 'CS: CS Note: for the image…'). When cs_form is about to add the canonical 'CS:' prefix AND the writer's retained note ALREADY opens with a Creative-Services-family cue, that leading cue is folded away so the note reads 'CS: <body>' not 'CS: CS Note: <body>'. The engine builds one case-insensitive regex from cues (longest-first, \b-anchored so 'CSV'/'csc' are safe), an optional ' note'/' notes' suffix, and a trailing run of :,.–- delimiters. SCOPE: only the cs_form path — under CSRELABEL_OFF the prefix is 'RED FLAG:', where a leading 'CS Note:' is NOT a duplicate, so the cue is preserved. Measured class (outputs/_measure_csdupe.py): 101 occ / 51 pages / 24 modules; 0 of 966 RED FLAG diagnostics begin with a CS cue. NOTE:/answers:/alert-note/activity-note labels are deliberately NOT CS cues and are left intact. The DEV family + addressed 'note to/for <addressee>' forms are folded SEPARATELY by addressee_fold (round 71). Never strips a note down to empty (keeps the original if it would). Reverts to the round-57 doubled form when enabled:false OR env CSDEDUPE_OFF is set (gate-safe A/B; the note still starts 'CS:' so the compare_structure/full_compare 'cs ' exclusion is unchanged either way).

addressee_fold.note: Round 71 — extend the CS-prefix fold (Chris) to the remaining redundant ADDRESSEE leads, so a note whose audience the 'CS:' prefix already implies doesn't repeat it. Two branches, both requiring an explicit delimiter (every measured case has one): (1) a BARE dev-family cue — 'Dev:', 'Dev team –', 'Developer note:' (bare_cues + optional_suffix); (2) an ADDRESSED form — 'Note to developer:', 'Note to dev team:', 'Note to CS:', 'Note for Creative Services.' (addressed_by + optional 'the' + addressed_cues + optional_suffix). Delimiters folded: : , . – (en-dash) - (hyphen). bare_cues are DEV-ONLY so this never strips a bare CS cue — that stays cs_dedupe's job (round 70), independently reversible. \b-anchored so 'development'/'device' are safe. Measured (outputs/_measure_addrfold.py): 54 occ / 28 pages / 17 modules (MXFL401 14, TWHA90x, CEDT/CEDW501, EXBP901, …); residual CS-family 0 (round 70 holding). NOTE:/designer/'general note to the designers'/answers/image/video/source are NOT folded (not an audience the CS: prefix subsumes, or content). Never strips to empty. Reverts when enabled:false OR env ADDRFOLD_OFF is set (gate-safe A/B; the note still starts 'CS:' so the 'cs ' gate exclusion is unchanged).

Ground-truthed canonical form (Tag_Interpretation_Rules.md §4.1): always a block

dual_language._use_mtk_flag_doc: ROUND 186 (Chris, stocktake backlog 1 — the r167/r185 mtkFlag→reoMode DEMOTION). false (shipped) = the 'MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE' house header no longer puts a module in reoMode (374/390 WTs carry it — the house template NAME, not a bilingual marker; r167 measured 0 genuine bilingual modules rely on it alone). mtk_leak_guard._doc: ROUND 186 leak guard (the r167 #htmlLeaksResolvedTag precedent, generalised): on a demote-affected module (run.mtkFlag true but demoted), a NORMAL-path kept free-body table whose rendered HTML still shows a resolved [tag] falls back to the exact reoMode placeholder form (cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt) that hides it today — measured round-186: the ENTIRE +84-occ un-masked leak inventory is this one kept-table class (OS-family [Click drop], ENG-family [image], ENGS202/TWHA901 [body]). Env MTKGUARD_OFF disables just the guard.

reo_layout_table_grid._round167_note: ROUND 167 (Chris, ENGS201-01). In reoMode (a bilingual module OR any module the broad mtkFlag flags), a free-body table that ALL the bilingual handlers decline falls through to a cv2-interactive 'bilingual-unbuilt' placeholder that keeps the raw WT [tag] text BY DESIGN. That is right for an un-built widget/spec table, but a CLEAN STRUCTURAL LAYOUT table (a side-by-side image|body panel, every cell led by a structural [tag]) is NOT a widget — the human renders it as a row>col GRID, and the reoMode path was BYPASSING the layout-table grid that the normal (non-reo) path already runs. So ENGS201-01's 'Origin stories' image|body table shipped as the placeholder and LEAKED [body]/[image] as visible frontend text inside the box. FIX: before the placeholder, try TablesAndGrids.layoutTableGrid (the SAME detector the normal path uses — single-row or all-cells-tagged only, and it BAILS on any widget-member cell tag). A grid is emitted for a clean layout table; a widget/spec/data table still returns null and keeps the placeholder untouched, so no other reoMode table changes and no [tag] is newly exposed. env REOLTABLE_OFF reverts to the always-placeholder behaviour.

audio_image._status: PARKED (default-off) — round 135. The build is CORRECT (matches the human's `row>col paddingR>audioImage>audioImageOption>img` byte-for-byte; TRR102 builds 10 of the 30 clean 2-row grids) BUT it regresses the skeleton (A/B AUDIOIMG_OFF=1 TRR102 = MINUS 1.41): the human NESTS the audioImage grid inside the section's `col-md-8` / `div.activity` (with the lesson heading), while the build emits a BARE top-level `<div class="row">`. The rich structure in the WRONG nesting scores worse than the single cv2 WIDGET marker the skeleton aligned loosely. This is the SAME nesting wall as the boxes + over-capture guard: the bilingual page is richly NESTED (section -> activity -> widget) and any piece built in isolation regresses. The audioImage build (`ContentConverter.#bilingualAudioImage`) + flag stay here as the base; the REAL fix is a HOLISTIC bilingual structural build (row-group the section's heading + grid + widget under one col-md-8 / div.activity, the round-51 row-grouping for reoMode), then the widgets credit. TRR112-style grids (embedded in content tables, not separate 2-row tables) also need the prose+widget split first. env AUDIOIMG_OFF.

content_table_guard._round135b_note: ROUND 135 (Chris) — SHIPPED ON (default-on) as part of the keystone v2: WITH section_grouping it credits (the released content tables unfold reo/eng inside the human's div.activity nest, and the embedded-widget marker is re-emitted inside the box). Alone it was module-dependent / net-negative (TRR103 −0.92) — it must ship WITH the selective boxing + the interleave, which v2 does. env REOTABLE_OFF reverts it independently of REONEST_OFF. PRIOR (v1) finding: Isolated A/B (grouping OFF, guard toggled): the guard is MODULE-DEPENDENT — TRR102+TRR111 skeleton +0.56 / compare_structure +75, but TRR103 skeleton −0.92 and TRR113 −0.46 — net-negative on the class alone (confirms the original park). Unfolding a content table that embeds a widget reference only credits when the section is ALSO boxed in the human's selective `div.activity` nesting AND the reo/eng is interleaved per-paragraph; in isolation the extra unfolded (wrong-order) prose loses as many chains as it gains. Ships only WITH the corrected selective section_grouping + interleave fix. env REOTABLE_OFF.
content_table_guard._status: PARKED (default-off) — round 135. The guard correctly stops the scanner over-capturing a bilingual `English|Māori` content table as a widget (so the intro unfolds + the activity box wraps the REAL widget: TRR102 A/B with the boxes = skeleton +5.0, compare_structure +64). BUT measured net-NEGATIVE across the full Bilingual set (skeleton 26.6→25.9, A/B-clean): unfolding a content table that EMBEDS a widget LOSES the WIDGET marker the human builds on the box-less modules (TRR113), and a bare cv2 placeholder (the round-135 #bilingualTable append) does NOT recover the skeleton (a WIDGET needs the human's surrounding row>col structure, not just the marker). So the CLEAN fix is a real PROSE+WIDGET SPLIT — unfold the prose AND emit the widget in the human's structure (its own row>col / the audioImage grid / etc.), not a bare placeholder. The guard + `#bilingualContentTable` + the `#bilingualTable` placeholder + the `#bilingualSplit` consecutive-tag strip stay here (flag-gated, default-off) as the base for that round. Flip enabled:true WITH the split + REOACT to ship the boxes.
content_table_guard._round135_note: ROUND 135 (Chris, TRR102 — the activity-box prerequisite). The writers embed a widget reference (`[Interactive] [Flipcard]`/`[Carousel]`) INSIDE the intro `[Body]` cell of a bilingual `English|Māori` content table; `InteractiveScanner.#interactiveInTable` then OVER-CAPTURED the WHOLE content table (Activity NX: + [H2] heading + [Body] prose) as a flipCard widget (measured 64/140 bilingual scanner bundles). That broke two things: the reo/eng intro prose never rendered (it sat inside a cv2 flipCard placeholder), and the round-133 activity box wrapped the intro-flipCard + took the `Activity NX:` number, so the box landed on the WRONG content (A/B skeleton −1.58). FIX (env REOTABLE_OFF): in reoMode, `#interactiveInTable` is skipped for a table whose row-0 header is `English|Māori` (`#bilingualContentTable`, mirrors `#bilingualHeader`) — the table falls through to `#bilingualTable` (round-129) and unfolds as reo/eng. A real widget table ([Activity Embedded] [X] opener, flipCard [Item N] data, quiz) has NO English|Māori header → still captured. This UNBLOCKS the activity boxes (they then wrap the real widget) + fixes the intro rendering corpus-wide.

section_grouping._round135_finding:
SHIPPED v2 (default-on, round 135) — skeleton-POSITIVE; see Config.js round 135 + spec §9e. v1 (uniform boxing) regressed 152 cs; v2 fixes it with #bilingualRows per-paragraph reo/eng INTERLEAVE + Activity-NX:-label strip AND #bilingualSection SELECTIVE boxing (a real-widget section -> div.activity[number]; a prose/audioImage-grid section -> bare col-md-8). A/B REONEST_OFF=1 REOTABLE_OFF=1 TRR102 TRR111: skeleton SCAFFOLD +4.46/+1pg, cs exact 21 (content held), body 0, standard byte-identical. audio_image still parked (col-class). The v1 journey/finding follows: the mechanism WORKS (the `[H1] N.M` discriminator finds every section: TRR113 26/26; the scanner terminator releases each from its over-capturing bundle; the nesting renders as the human's `row > col-md-8 > div.activity > row > col-12`) BUT uniform boxing REGRESSES the gates: isolated A/B (guard held ON) = skeleton −0.36 / compare_structure exact −152 on TRR102+TRR111. ROOT CAUSE (measured, outputs/_measure_bilingual_nesting.py + the TRR102_1.0 diff): the human boxes SELECTIVELY — only ~55% of lesson rows are `div.activity` (true interactive activities), 22% are BARE `col-md-8` (prose/intro/audioImage-grid sections the human does NOT box), 13% callout, 9% side-col — so a uniform box mismatches the 22% bare sections; AND two pre-existing unfold defects degrade every box's chain match: the reo/eng order is all-reo-then-all-eng instead of the human's per-paragraph reo,eng,reo,eng (spec §9b balance), and the `Activity NX:`/`Ngohe NX:` label leaks as a body `

` (the human omits it / lifts it to the box's number= attr). THE NEXT-ROUND RECIPE: (1) fix the reo/eng per-paragraph interleave + suppress the `Activity NX:` label; (2) box SELECTIVELY — only a section whose content includes a real interactive widget bundle (wordSelect/dragDrop/quiz/flipCard/carousel), NOT a prose/audioImage-only section — with the human's exact `div.activity[ interactive]` class; (3) THEN flip section_grouping + content_table_guard together + re-A/B (they should credit once the box only lands where the human's does and the prose order matches). All the code (#bilingualSection / #bilingualRows / #bilingualSectionNum / the scanner #bilingualSectionOpener terminator) stays here as the base. env REONEST_OFF.
section_grouping._round135_note: ROUND 135 (Chris, the KEYSTONE — holistic bilingual SECTION nesting). The human wraps every Te Reo lesson SECTION in `#body > div.row > col-md-8 col-12 > div.activity > div.row > col-12 > {heading + reo/eng prose + audioImage grid + the widget}` — ONE nested box per `[H1] N.M` decimal section (measured 262 human activity boxes on lesson pages vs Claude 11; outputs/_measure_bilingual_nesting.py). Claude emitted each bilingual table as its own FLAT top-level row + cv2 placeholders, so every parked piece (audioImage / content_table_guard / reo_bundle_activity) landed at the wrong NESTING DEPTH and regressed in isolation (the nesting wall: boxes −1.58, over-capture −0.7, audioImage −1.41). FIX (reoMode-scoped, env REONEST_OFF): `ContentConverter.#bilingualSection` triggers on a `[H1] N.M` section-opener table, GATHERS the section's items (bilingual content tables -> reo/eng unfold via #bilingualRows; audioImage grids; a consumed widget bundle -> ONE cv2 marker with bundle._emitted suppressed; black prose) up to the next `[H1] N.M` opener / a non-section callout / page boundary, and wraps the FLAT inner content in the human's `row > col-md-8 > div.activity > row > col-12`. A section that contains a widget -> `div.activity interactive`; a prose-only section -> grouped under a bare `col-md-8` (the round-51 row-grouping mechanism, reoMode-scoped). Standard modules carry no reoMode -> byte-identical. This is the PREREQUISITE that makes the parked pieces (audio_image / content_table_guard / reo_bundle_activity) credit instead of regress; flip them on one at a time after the nest holds. Pairs with content_table_guard (so the prose unfolds rather than cv2-capturing). Tool outputs/_measure_bilingual_nesting.py.

lesson_heading._round137_note: ROUND 137 (Chris) — EXTEND the keystone box to the `[H2] Lesson N` lesson form (the convention-2 family TRR108/114/203/301; round 136 split their PAGES, this round NESTS the lesson activities the human boxes). The keystone (`_round135_note`) groups only a `[H1] N.M` decimal section; the `[H2] Lesson N` family rendered FLAT (~25% skeleton). `ContentConverter.#bilingualSection` now ALSO opens on a `[H2] (Lesson|Hei Mahi|Ngohe) N` first-content-row table (via `#bilingualLessonNum`, this pattern) when there is no `[H1] N.M`, with TWO behavioural differences vs the keystone: (1) the lesson TITLE renders as a BARE `row>col-md-8><h2 reo/eng>` OUTSIDE the box (the human keeps the lesson title at h2, ungrouped — measured the dominant title level across TRR108/114/203/301), the activity content gathers into the box from the row AFTER the title; (2) the box `number=` is RESEQUENCED to `{lessonNum}{letter}` with the letter A,B,C,D assigned sequentially within each lesson — the human DISCARDS the writer's irregular 1A/1E/1H letters (measured TRR203 WT 1A/1E/1H -> human 1A/1B/1C; TRR301 WT 1A/1E/1H/1I -> human 1A/1B/1C/1D). Everything else is REUSED: the gather stops at the next `[H2] Lesson N` (a new activity) AND at `#isCalloutTable`, so the `[Alert]`/`Finished` tail falls OUTSIDE the box automatically (measured 0/34 alerts inside human boxes across the family); SELECTIVE boxing keeps a shell lesson with no widget (TRR107, 0 human boxes) as a bare col-md-8. Disjoint from the `[H1] N.M` family by the marker + reoMode-gated -> the 197 standard modules byte-identical. env REOLESSON_OFF (independent of REONEST_OFF). Tool outputs/_measure_bilingual_lessonbox.py. NOTE (round 137 triangulation): the spec-§9f 'dipthong-tail page split' follow-up is NON-DERIVABLE — TRR114 pp4-5 / TRR107's later pages ('Oro tōpū', 'Kete Kupu', 'Silly Sentences') are 0-occurrence in the WT (developer-authored shells, spec §7); declined as Framework (C).

lesson_table_boundary._round136_note: ROUND 136 (Chris) — CONVENTION 2: a `[H2] Lesson N` / `[H2] Ngohe N` TABLE-ROW heading opens a lesson page when the lesson number INCREMENTS. The convention-1 round 134 only split on the `[LESSON N CONTENT]` tag; the TRR107/108/114/115/203/301/304 family carries NO such tag — it marks each lesson with a `[H2] Lesson N` table-row heading, REPEATED at the top of each sub-activity (TRR114: Lesson 1 ×3, 2 ×3, 3 ×3), so a naive split-on-every-marker over-paginates. The human splits ONLY on a NEW (higher) number (TRR114 → pages 1.0/2.0/3.0). `PageSplitter.Split` (reoMode-scoped) scans a table's first rows for `[H2] (Lesson|Ngohe) N` and opens page N.0 when N > the running lessonOrdinal. Self-discriminating (overview headings are Overview/Key Objectives/… never Lesson N) + reoMode-gated → standard untouched. The dipthong-tail lessons (no `[H2] Lesson N`, e.g. TRR114 pp 4-5) + PNR `Hei Mahi` are follow-ups. env REOPAGE2_OFF (independent of REOPAGE_OFF). Tool outputs/_measure_bilingual_pagesplit.py.

page_split._round134_note: ROUND 134 (Chris, TRR102 — the bilingual PAGE-SPLIT, convention 1). A reoTranslate module's WT marks each lesson with a `[LESSON N CONTENT]` marker that the normaliser resolves to a SECTION_MARKER (NOT a PAGE_BOUNDARY), so PageSplitter never opened a lesson page at it: the overview body is trimmed upstream → the stream STARTS at `[LESSON 1 CONTENT]` → the implicit overview swallowed lesson 1 and every later lesson shifted by one (lesson-N content on page N-1). FIX (reoMode-scoped, env REOPAGE_OFF): (1) a numbered `[LESSON N CONTENT]` opens lesson page N.0 (mirrors the `lesson` PAGE_BOUNDARY path); (2) a MID-doc `[Title Bar]` is kept on the current lesson page as its title, NOT treated as a sub-document twin (the round's relabel chaos — TRR102 lesson 4 uses `[Title Bar]` for its heading); (3) RR-4 KEEPS an empty overview (the bilingual menu page 0.0, body intentionally empty). Convention-1 family = TRR102/103/106/109/111/112/113. The `[H2] Lesson N`/`Hei Mahi N` TABLE-ROW convention (TRR107/108/114/115/203/301/304) + PNR `Hei Mahi` are follow-up rounds (table-row boundary detection). Measured human 86 pages vs Claude 45 (outputs/_measure_bilingual_pagesplit.py). reoMode = bilingual only (TRR/PNR prefix / reoTranslate body / mtkFlag), so the 197 standard modules are byte-identical.

dropdown_menu._doc: ROUND 212 (Chris, PNR101 empty overview). The NEW MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' bilingual Writers Template (the PNR101/102/104 family) opens with a [Content for DROP DOWN MENU] section: ONE English|Maori two-column table holding the whole module menu ([TITLE BAR] row, [H2][TABn] tab-label rows, [H1]/[H2] pane headings, [Body] content), closed by [END OF DROP-DOWN MENU] (PNR102 types it WITHOUT the hyphen), then a [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1] marker whose table is the overview body, then [LESSON N CONTENT] lessons. NONE of these markers was a recognised content-start, so DocxExtractor.TrimFrontMatter cut EVERYTHING before [LESSON 1 CONTENT] as front matter and the whole overview (menu + title + intro) silently vanished — the module shipped an empty -00 page. This config drives the five coupled pieces of the fix: (1) content-start recognition (Input_Doc_Rules content_start_fragments_dropdown); (2) PageSplitter keeps the [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] marker's content ON the overview page (module_content_pattern below — the human's 0.0 = menu + module content); (3) InteractiveScanner never opens a widget bundle for the opener (it parses as a 'dropdown' INTERACTIVE invocation — it is a menu marker, not a widget); (4) ContentConverter.#partitionItems routes the opener..closer region's table to the MENU side (flagged _reoDropdown); (5) MenuBuilder.#reoDropdownTabs composes the human's bilingual tabs menu (nav <span reo>/<span eng> labels; per-pane reo/eng element pairs; h4span section heads / h5 lead-ins; the Information pane splits at a 'Connections'-family heading into paddingR|paddingL columns — measured on all 3 golds). The module title comes from the front-matter metadata table's 'Module Name' row ('Nga tau: 1 | Numbers: 1' — pipe-split, payload order = reo first, the CEDW501 positional-slot precedent; see front_matter_metadata.table_row_fields). Measured corpus-wide over every parsed WT: the marker family = EXACTLY PNR101/102/104. Env REODROPMENU_OFF reverts ALL five pieces (the overview drops back to the empty page).
dropdown_menu._doc_module_content_all_tables: ROUND 220 (Chris, the PNR104-00 raw-dump screenshot). PageSplitter flags EVERY table in the [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] region (until the next structural red marker — [END OF PAGE]/[LESSON N CONTENT]) as _reoModuleContent, not just the FIRST. PNR104's writer split the module intro into TWO tables (whakatauki table with its own English|Maori header + a 'Module Introduction | Kowae Ako Whakataki' table); the r212 first-table-only walk left the second unflagged, bilingualTable declined it (no header), and the whole module introduction shipped as a raw cv2 bilingual-unbuilt dump — invisible to every gate (cv2 classes are gate-excluded by design). Measured over ALL 428 corpus WTs (outputs/_measure_reomodcontent.cjs): marker modules = exactly PNR101/102/104 (+ TRR304 whose opener-less form never enters this branch); multi-table region = EXACTLY PNR104. false (or env REOMODCONTENT_OFF) reverts to the first-table-only walk.

logical_to_element.rule: The writer's H-digit is a LOGICAL level resolved in context, never a fixed element (§5.1). In body context the digit shifts DOWN one level; page-title headings are built by the skeleton, not here; overview menu headings are CONSUMED into the menu (menu.tab_map below).
logical_to_element._relevel_headroom_note: ROUND 55. The body emission normally clamps to h5, but when #relevelHeadings is active it RANKS the page's distinct heading levels back into h3..max_level — so the emission is allowed ONE extra intermediate level (h6) for a writer [H5]. Without it [H4]->h5 and [H5]->h5 collapse before the re-leveller sees them, so a genuine 3-level [H3]/[H4]/[H5] page (e.g. OSAI401-04: human h3 'Data, data, data' > h4 'How AI uses data' > h5 'Data collection'…) loses its third level and the [H5] sub-items get pulled up to h4. With the headroom the re-leveller sees {h4,h5,h6}->{h3,h4,h5} and reproduces the human's hierarchy. The h6 is intermediate only — the re-leveller always normalises it into base..max_level; when re-levelling is disabled the ceiling stays h5 so no h6 reaches the output.
logical_to_element.lesson_first_h2: Becomes the page's body <h3> with any leading 'Lesson N' / 'Lesson N:' prefix stripped (the lesson number already lives in the header/module-code).
logical_to_element.no_span_rule: <span> wrappers appear ONLY inside header <h1> titles — never on body h2–h5.

OSAH); Claude keeps a whole-heading *italic* the writer typed (a section heading like '[H3] *What is online harassment or abuse?*' ->

…

). Measured LIVE outputs/_measure_heading_italic.py. Edit this string to restyle with no code change.

external_link_button_standalone.note:
ROUND 76 (Chris, OSBY201-03): a STANDALONE [external link] (NOT 'external link button') whose item content is ONLY a bare URL — no descriptive label text and no [LINK:] hyperlinked phrase — is the human's external-resource BUTTON, exactly like the round-56 [external link button] tag. #inline emits buttons['external link button'].form (
LABEL
) with the round-56 default label ('Go to website', or 'Go to video' for a video host) — the exact wording (e.g. 'Be internet awesome', 'Netsafe') is the human's editorial coinage, not in the WT. MEASURED (outputs/_measure_extlink_human.py): of the standalone [external link]+URL instances, the human renders the URL-only form as an externalButton (OSBY201/OSBY101 kind-kingdom, OSAH401 Netsafe/KeepItReal/BullyingFree, ENFUN01, ENGC201, OSGM101, …); the LABELLED / [LINK:]-phrase form stays an inline link (round 74 weave) — so the discriminator is 'item text is the bare URL alone'. Conservative: fires only on the external-link tag with empty label text + a URL. Env EXTBTN_OFF reverts to the round-74 bare-URL

URL

. ROUND 88 REFINEMENT: the 'labelled form stays inline' claim held only for a TRAILING tag; a LEADING [external link]+phrase is now a button — see external_link_button_labelled.

external_link_button_labelled.note:
ROUND 88 (Chris, ENGI302-02): a LEADING [external link] tag (governs the paragraph — '[external link] __The Story of Mauao__ [LINK:url]', the tag FIRST, the linked resource title as the whole rest) is the human's external-resource BUTTON, not the round-74 inline

weave. DISCRIMINATOR = tag POSITION (measured outputs/_measure_extlink_position.py): a LEADING [external link]+phrase -> externalButton (ENGI302 ×5 Mauao/Matriarch/Maui/Cried-Wolf/Aladdin, ENGI303/ENGJ201 Pixabay — 7/7 human buttons, 0 inline); a TRAILING [external link] (appended after a phrase in a bullet/sentence — OSBY201 '...Complete an online contact form [LINK] [external link]', OSAH401) stays the round-74 inline weave (button=0 corpus-wide), so this rule CANNOT disturb round 74/76. Trailing forms reach #inline's round-74 !text early-return; only a leading tag (the phrase in blackAfter) reaches this branch. Human class is 'button externalButton' (8) > 'externalButton' (2) — matches ENGI302; the round-56/76 standalone-bare-URL form keeps its own 'externalButton'. The href is the WT [LINK:] URL (the human re-hosts PDFs / coins copy-doc links — non-derivable editorial); the BUTTON STRUCTURE + label match. Guarded: primary.tag==='external link' (leading) + a short label (<=label_max_words, no end-punctuation) so a leading ext-link governing a prose sentence can never become a giant button. Env EXTBTNLABEL_OFF reverts to the inline

link.

all_external_links_videos.note:
ROUND 76 (Chris, OSBY201-03): a writer '[all external links]' instruction governing a 'Videos:' block converts the FOLLOWING [video] items in that section to external-link BUTTONS (the human renders 'Why be kind' / 'Upstander game' as
TITLE
, NOT embeds — the instruction declares these videos are external links). The button LABEL is derivable here: the [video] item's italic title (e.g. '*Why be kind*' → 'Why be kind'); the URL is the video link. A section pre-pass marks each governed [video] (governance resets at the next heading/page boundary); the [video] branch reads the flag. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_extlink_button.py): the '[all external links]' instruction appears in exactly ONE module (OSBY201) — so the rule is keyed on the INSTRUCTION (generalisable, not a module code) and cannot disturb any other page. Env ALLEXTVID_OFF reverts to standard video embeds.

hyperlink_weave.note:
Round 74 (Chris, OSBY201-02 issue 3) — a run HYPERLINKED in the Writers Template (a real w:hyperlink, captured by DocxExtractor as block.links {text,target}) is woven onto its DESCRIPTIVE phrase as phrase, the human convention. Measured: human body has 1011 descriptive-text phrase-links vs Claude 131 — an 880-link gap across 90 modules; the writer's [external link] tag is a 'opens externally' MODIFIER on the phrase, not its own element, so it no longer emits a separate bare-URL

when the block already carries a descriptive-phrase hyperlink (#inline suppress). Conservative: exact phrase text, first occurrence per line, skipped if already inside an or if the link text IS the URL (the bare-URL rule already linked those). Env LINKWEAVE_OFF reverts BOTH the weave and the [external link] suppress (back to plain phrase + separate bare URL).

info_trigger_inline.note: Round 75 (Chris, OSBY201-03 issue 2) — a SELF-CLOSED inline trigger marker ('anchor [audio trigger DEF]' / '[hover trigger DEF]', the DEFINITION carried INSIDE the marker's own red span so there is NO separate ']' closer) is woven onto its preceding anchor word as anchor (using the inline_format.info_trigger template), instead of breaking the paragraph and dropping the def. The DEF is recovered in ORIGINAL case from the marker text after 'trigger' (parse.remainders is lowercased/mangled). InteractiveScanner inserts the U+E000 sentinel right after the anchor; ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup builds the span. Conservative: fires ONLY on the self-closed form with a non-empty def AND a preceding anchor word; the SPLIT-bracket form ('[hover trigger DEF' + a separate ']' item, the 761-span ENGJ302/MXDI301 class) is a distinct, messier tokenisation handled by the existing hasCloser path and is NOT changed here (sized follow-up lever). Env INFOTRIG_OFF reverts to the paragraph-break behaviour.

split_bracket.leading_anchor_note: Round 86 (Chris, CEDW501-00) — the ANCHOR-BEFORE-BRACKET shape: after DocxExtractor merges the writer's adjacent red runs the marker span reads 'ANCHOR [hover|rollover|mouseover SEP DEF]' — the hovered WORD sits INSIDE the red span, before the bracket, so head_pattern (^\[) fails and the whole span leaked as a 'CS:' note (and broke the paragraph / fragmented a [whakataukī] box). WT: CEDW501 'He kākano ahau i ruia mai i 🔴Rangiātea [Hover: 🔴🔴Represents a place of origin… for all Māori.]🔴', and the body 'proud of your 🔴whānau🔴🔴 [Hover: People linked…]🔴'. FIX: when the merged span does NOT start with '[' but matches ' [hover…]', lift the anchor text out, append it to the preceding host with its LAST word woven as word (same U+E000 sentinel as round 75/82), and recover the DEF after the COLON inside the bracket ('Hover: DEF'). MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_anchorhover.py): 17 closed + 2 open occ / 11 modules; the COLON targets (CEDW501 ×3 whānau/iwi/Rangiātea, CEDT501 perspective/pātai/clarification, CEDR501 accurate, …) render the term as an infoTrigger in the HUMAN gold, so the weave MATCHES the human for the body cases and does what Chris asked for the whakataukī. The 'trigger'-keyword + widget guards still exclude MXDB301 '[Hover Triggers…]' / SSOG101. SCOPE/DEFERRED: only the COLON 'Hover:' form is woven here. The SPACED-DASH form ('Hover - DEF' / 'Hover – DEF', CEDT501 kaupapa/mana/erase) is LEFT to its pre-existing behaviour: when the dash marker is a SEPARATE red span (anchor not merged) it goes through the round-82 path where the round-84 A2 'def-in-next-item' can mis-grab a following bullet — a host-finder + dash-def follow-up, sized but not in this round (it is a pre-existing class, not introduced here). Env HOVERANCHOR_OFF reverts to the leaking-note behaviour (independent of HOVERSPLIT_OFF/HOVERDEF_OFF).
split_bracket.note: Round NN (Chris, AGH1004-01/-02) — TWO split/orphaned bracket shapes round 82 could not reach, both reversible via env HOVERSPLIT_OFF (independent of HOVERDEF_OFF). (A1) lead_orphan: the marker's opening '[' sits in the preceding BLACK run, so the resolved item text begins 'hover definition] DEF' with NO leading '[' and head_pattern (^\[) fails (AGH1004-01 '…specific areas or **regions** [🔴hover definition] a distinct…'). The '[' is restored before the head test (gated: a head keyword at the very start + a ']' present) and the orphaned '[' is stripped off the host so it never leaks as 'regions ['. Measured 8 occ / 6 modules (AGH1002/04/07/08…). (A2) unclosed_next_item: the marker carries NO usable def of its own — an UNCLOSED '[hover definition:' (no closing ']') OR a closed-but-empty '[hover definition]' — and its blackAfter is empty; the def is the FOLLOWING red/black item (DocxExtractor merges the writer's fragmented red runs into ONE item: 'DEF…]' with the paragraph continuation in ITS blackAfter), e.g. AGH1004-02 '…beautiful topographies 🔴[hover definition:🔴 🔴the shape and features…🔴 on planet Earth…'. That item is consumed as the def (a stray late ']' trimmed) and was previously mis-rendered as a 'CS:' note. Measured 101 occ / 28 modules (def-in-NEXT-RED-span). SAFETY: the def-in-BLACK form (no red def item; the next item is plain black text — 41 occ / 10 modules incl. AGH1007 'plant materia]') is NOT touched, left exactly as round 82 rendered it; the consumed next item must be a non-interactive instruction/noise/black span, never a real widget tag.
split_bracket._def_black_tail_doc: ROUND 222c (Chris, the ENGJ403 'pitch' hover screenshot). THE DEF-IN-OWN-BLACK-TAIL SHAPE — ENGJ403's standard hover idiom (12 occurrences measured in its WT, the module's only hover form): a red '[hover info ‘pitch’:' span with NO closing bracket, the DEFINITION as the span's own black tail, then a bare ']' red span whose black tail continues the sentence. (A2) requires an EMPTY own tail so this fell through — the marker leaked as a Writers Note and the paragraph fragmented. Now: def = the marker's own black tail; the ']' closer span is consumed and its tail rejoins the sentence; a QUOTED anchor in the head ('pitch') weaves the sentinel onto that word's LAST occurrence in the host prose (the round-146-deferred named-anchor class, now shipped for this form), falling back to the historical last-word append when absent/not found. Human gold ENGJ403 ships all of these as class=infoTrigger spans. Env HOVERTAIL_OFF reverts just this shape.

hover_definition_inline.note: Round 82 (Chris, ENGC101-01/-02) — a hover/rollover/mouseover DEFINITION marker whose def is NOT carried after a 'trigger' keyword (so round 75's info_trigger_inline does not weave it). TWO shapes, both currently broken: (A) COLON self-closed '[hover: DEF]' / '[hover definition: DEF]' / '[rollover definition: DEF]' / '[mouseover definition: DEF]' — the def is inside the bracket after the first colon; markers like '[Hover: …]' resolve to plain [body] (paragraph SPLIT) while '[hover definition: …]' resolve to infoTrigger but hit round 75's bare-marker guard (def DROPPED). (B) MARKER-THEN-DEF '[hover text] DEF' — the bracket closes and the def follows it inside the SAME red span (ENGC101 'Using **adjectives** [hover text] Describing words. can make…'). Both are woven onto the nearest preceding word as anchor in ONE paragraph (same U+E000 sentinel + ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup machinery as round 75). SCOPE/SAFETY: the head must start with hover/rollover/mouseover (head_pattern); a marker that resolves to a NON-infoTrigger interactive widget (shapeHover, a hover audio player, etc.) is skipped; a marker carrying 'trigger' (skip_if_tag_keyword) is left to round 75; a marker with NO recoverable def is left untouched (rendered as before, never a leaked literal). Env HOVERDEF_OFF reverts both shapes to the round-81 split/drop behaviour.

render_stitch.note:
Round 201 (Chris, queue-5 split-bracket infoTrigger) — RENDER-LEVEL re-stitch of any hover/rollover/definition marker that reached the FINAL visible text as a LITERAL. The scanner round-75/82/86 weave only reaches clean red TAG items; the leaking residue arrives as a BLACK item (HIS1002/HIS1005 'for TERM'), a 'definition'-head data-marker tag (ENGJ301), or a table cell (CEDO501). ListsAndRuns.hoverStitch runs at the TOP of inlineMarkup (every visible-text path:

/

  • /) AND on the FULL multi-line text in renderBlackText (cross-line 'for TERM'), inserting the U+E000…U+E001 sentinel that #inlineMarkup already converts to anchor. CONTAINMENT-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: cv2 placeholder dumps render RAW (never via inlineMarkup/renderBlackText — proven: their bare URLs stay unlinked), so the 389 markers trapped in un-built widgets are untouched. ANCHOR: a 'for/on TERM' marker weaves onto the LAST whole-word occurrence of TERM in the preceding text (the round-146 note's deferred named-anchor); otherwise the single word immediately before the marker. Reuses the round-146 hygiene (instruction-def + URL-tail decline) and the round-82 'trigger' exclusion (those are round 75's). A marker with no clean anchor/def is LEFT as the pre-existing literal — never a wrong weave, never a NEW leak. Measured visible footprint 39 occ / 19 modules (outputs/_measure_infosplit.py); the ~26 stitchable are ENGJ301/CEDR501/CEDO501/CEDK501/TWHA903/HIS1002/HIS1005/SSFUN01/SSFUN06/SSFUN07/ARFUN03/ARFUN05/HIS1004/PHE1007. Env INFOSPLIT_OFF reverts to the leaking literal.
render_stitch._head_words_note_r222c: ROUND 222c: 'hover info' (first, longest-wins) admits both the spaced '[hover info ‘X’:' AND the glued '[hoverinfo ‘X’:' cell forms (head_words internal spaces compile to [-\s]?) — the ENGJ403 4.0 act-structure table cells. The quoted-anchor weave in hoverStitch pairs with it.

hover_definition_inline._head_pattern_note_r222c: ROUND 222c (Chris, ENGJ403 hover screenshot): 'hover(?:\s*info(?:rmation)?)?' admits the GLUED '[hoverinfo ...' form (ENGJ403 types one) — the spaced '[hover info ...' already matched via the bare 'hover' + \b. Previous pattern: ^\[\s*(?:hover|roll\s*-?\s*over|rollover|mouse\s*-?\s*over|mouseover)\b

define_heads._doc: ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B3 — SCCH302-03 'boiling point'). The bare [define: DEF] head now weaves like [hover define:] (which already worked): head_pattern here REPLACES the base pattern (adding 'define' to the alternation) in the scanner weave, and stitch_heads joins the render-stitch head_words. Measured over ALL WTs: '[define' heads = 6 occ / 4 corpus modules (SCFUN01 x3 clean colon-defs, EXBP901/EXIP901 '[define on hover:', PES1007 '[define this:]' def-less -> guards decline, unchanged) + SCCH302. 'definition' was MEASURED and DECLINED for the scanner side: 247 [definition…] spans are data-marker SUBTAGS inside widget bundles (MXDB302 matching pairs, ANZH203, CEDT104 flipcard hovers) — weaving them would break widget capture; the render-stitch already carries 'definition' (round 201) for render-level literals. All existing instruction/URL/trigger guards apply unchanged. Env DEFINEHEAD_OFF reverts to the base head_pattern + head_words.

hover_weave_hygiene.note: Round 146 (Chris, queue 0a: the HIS1002-16 U+E001 sentinel leak) — HYGIENE guards shared by BOTH sentinel-weave paths (round-75 info_trigger_inline + round-82/86 hover_definition_inline). Measured corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_sentinel_hosts.cjs, full compare set + OSSC301): 295 weaves = 288 clean / 6 media-tail hosts / 1 instruction-def (media_tail_pattern = URL or media FILENAME tail: the 3 extra are MXFU201's '[hover] enlarge graph' hints anchored on 'png' — the human drops every one). (1) instruction_def_guard — a recovered 'def' matching instruction_cue_pattern is a writer NOTE, not a definition ('For each concept, please have the rollover definitions below. Ngā mihi' HIS1002-16; '…Please embed these images and have drop-down boxes…' AGH1004-01): DECLINE the weave so the marker falls to the round-43 CS-note handling — the human strips both. (2) url_host_skip — the anchor-host walk never selects a candidate whose trailing text is a bare URL (+']'/')' residue): the URL machinery reads straight through the private-use sentinel ('…Pounamu_0.jpg⟨IT0⟩For' became part of the URL, orphaning ⟨IT1⟩ into the output = THE defect-class-E leak; MXFU201-09 wove info onto the URL fragments 'png'/'qJIHqK'; HIS1001-07 silently lost its def). With only media adjacent the anchor is non-derivable → the existing no-anchor fallback (def dropped, marker consumed — matches the human at MXFU201, who drops the text entirely). The HIS1001 NAMED-anchor weave ('[Rollover for moratorium: …]' → the human's moratorium in the body paragraph) is the sized follow-up for the split-bracket infoTrigger round (queue 5) — anchor SELECTION belongs there, not here. Both guards only DECLINE mis-weaves; the 291 clean weaves are untouched by construction. Env HOVERHYG_OFF reverts all 4 sites to the round-145 behaviour.

video_embed_title_drop.note:
ROUND 80 (Chris, ENGC102): a [video] whose embed was built (a YouTube id OR a generic iframe URL) DROPS its OWN title line (the [video] element's blackAfter) from the body — that text is the video's NAME, which the AcksBuilder ships as the acknowledgement, so the human renders ONLY the embed. across 2042 human pages. .

media_url_paren_strip.note:
ROUND 80 (Chris, ENGC102): after a media-reference URL is stripped from a [video]/[audio]/[image] caption, the now-EMPTY '()' / '( )' wrapper and any orphan single ')' / '(' left behind are removed — the human never ships these (334 stray-paren occurrences across 97 Claude pages vs 0 across 2042 human pages, e.g. ENGC102 '

)

', XDLS908 'Stop sign ( )'). Conservative: only EMPTY parens and isolated single parens are removed; '(real text)' inside genuine prose is preserved (the regex requires whitespace/boundary on both sides of a lone paren). Shared by #media and #image via #stripMediaResidue. Env MEDIAPAREN_OFF reverts to leaving the paren residue.

media_timestamp_note.note: ROUND 87 (Chris, ENGI302-00): a RED parenthetical that is WHOLLY a clock timestamp / time-range — '(to 1:00)', '(0:10-1:48)', '(1:45-2:27)', with an optional timing lead/trail word (to/from/at/clip/…/onwards/only) — is a writer's MEDIA-USAGE instruction to Creative Services (how to trim the video/audio it sits beside), NOT noise. Without this, TagNormaliser classifies it 'noise' (it is <3 words, carries no instruction cue, has no bracket) and ContentConverter silently DROPS it (ENGI302-00 '(to 1:00)' after the intro-video URL). When the free text matches this pattern, the span is reclassified 'instruction' so the round-43/57 path retains it as a 'CS:' note immediately after the media element. TIGHT by construction: requires the parenthesis boundary AND a \d:\d\d / \d.\d\d time, so it can never grab labels like (front)/(Back)/(Gold)/(middle image)/(trigger engagement), nor money ($58.20) / decimals / time-of-day (10:00 AM) which are not parenthesised timestamps. Measured 41 occ / 11 modules would-be-DROPPED (the longer '… only' / 'clip …' forms are already retained as >=3-word instructions); outputs/_measure_round87.py. Env TIMESTAMPNOTE_OFF reverts to dropping it as noise.

caption_not_media.note: ROUND NN (Chris, ENGS302-00): a writer's CAPTION marker that embeds a media word — '[Insert caption with video]', '[caption with image]', '[Caption text for image]' — resolves to the embedded media tag (video/image) via the longest-suffix embedded match, so ContentConverter built/red-flagged a media element from a caption (ENGS302-00 'RED FLAG: [video] with no URL found' on '[Insert caption with video] Watch this clever Lord of the Rings…'). When a media-resolved tag's RAW text contains the word 'caption', it is a CAPTION: render its following text as ordinary body, never an embed/red-flag. The bare [Caption]/[Insert caption] (data-marker SUBTAG, image-caption widget) never reaches a media branch, so it is untouched. Measured: 34 caption tags / 6 modules; the 'caption + media word' mis-resolving subset is the target. Env CAPTIONMEDIA_OFF reverts to building the (red-flagged) media element.

media_url_in_text.note: ROUND NN (Chris, ENGS302-01): a [video]/[embed]/[imbed] tag whose URL the writer typed INSIDE the same red instruction span as the tag ('[Embed film] edit to start at 3 seconds https://youtu…' — the URL is part of it.text, not the black blackAfter nor a hyperlink nor a following black item) was not found by #gatherFollowing (which only scans blackAfter + following BLACK items) → 'RED FLAG: [embed] with no URL found'. The URL search now ALSO scans the element's own raw it.text as a last resort, so an in-span URL is recovered and the embed builds. Measured 20 occ / 4 modules (ENGS302, ENGJ402, XDLS502/901) currently red-flagged despite a URL being present in-span; the human builds the embed in every case. Env MEDIAURLTEXT_OFF reverts to the blackAfter/following-only search.
media_url_in_text.following_link_note: ROUND 247 (Chris, ENGS404-00). The new-era WT authors '[insert video]' on its own line with the video as a TITLE-ANCHORED hyperlink on the NEXT black line ('Pixar in a Box… - YouTube' — the URL lives in the docx hyperlink, not the visible text; the r240 D2 title-anchored class on the media path). The URL search now also reads the following-black range's first hyperlink TARGET (after block-link/gathered-text, before the own-raw-text last resort). The r80 video_embed_title_drop then drops the reference line once the embed builds, exactly as for a same-line reference. Env MEDIAFOLLOWLINK_OFF reverts.

embed_story_carousel.note: ROUND NN (Chris, BLL117-02): an [embed story] (also '[Embed pdf text of story]', '[Embed School Journal story]') is the writer asking to embed a decodable/journal STORY whose pages are an EXTERNAL link (SPELD/School Journal). The converter routed it to a bare <iframe> of that site — which renders as a broken grey box (most story sites block framing). The HUMAN builds a CAROUSEL of the story's page images (measured 63/64 [embed story] modules build a carousel), but those page images are sourced manually post-conversion and are NOT in the WT/Media List. So emit the human's carousel SCAFFOLD with ONE placeholder slide (the standard Mode-P/D image — the developer drops the real pages in, exactly like every other image). The carousel class collapses to the same WIDGET marker as the human's carousel in the scaffold gate. Keyed on the word 'story' in the tag remainder, EXCLUDING 'audio' (the 1 '[Embed audio recording of this story]' case is an audio, not a visual carousel). Human ref: 01-Finalized_Modules_/BLL117/BLL117-03.html (Activity 2B). Env EMBEDSTORY_OFF reverts to the bare iframe.
embed_story_carousel.trigger_note: Fire when the [embed] tag's bracket contains a trigger word ('story' OR 'book' — '[embed story]'/'[embed book]'/'[Embed pdf text of story]'/'[Embed School Journal story]') and NO exclude word ('audio' — the lone '[Embed audio recording of this story]' is an audio recording, not a visual carousel). Whole-word match so 'audiobook'/'booklet' don't trip it.

link_text_display._doc: ROUND 213 (Chris, the BLL241 supervisor-note screenshot). When a link points at one of the domains listed here, the FRONTEND TEXT of the link shows the domain's canonical display form while the href keeps the writer's FULL deep URL — e.g. a link to https://speldsa.org.au/pages/speld-sa-phonic-books renders as https://speldsa.org.au. MEASURED: the human golds do exactly this in the BODY on 67/68 speldsa sites (66 modules, nearly all BLL supervisor notes) while their ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS keep the full URL text — so the rewrite is applied by a full-page post-pass (ListsAndRuns.LinkTextDisplay, called from PageAssembler beside OmitPlaceholderResidue/TidyDeveloperNotes) that STOPS at the acks block. It only rewrites an anchor whose text is ITSELF a URL on the same domain (a writer's descriptive phrase link like 'SPELD SA website' is never touched), so it can never destroy meaningful text. Applies to EVERY module corpus-wide, every emitter (Chris's explicit instruction — 'whenever this type of link is used in ANY module'). Add a domain by adding a key; env LINKTEXT_OFF reverts to the raw full-URL text.

caption_text._doc:
ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B2 — SCCH302-02). A FREE-BODY [caption] (outside any interactive) is the writer's image caption; the human ships

…

(gold x545). 'caption' stays an alias of the data-marker SUBTAG, so inside widget bundles nothing changes (carousel/flipCard captions etc — measured 175 [caption] occ / 22 modules, nearly all widget members); this rule fires ONLY at the orphan-sub-tag branch (which by definition is outside every interactive), replacing the 'Orphan sub-tag [data marker]' red flag + plain

with the captionText paragraph. The match is the EXACT bare bracket ([caption] and nothing else in the span) so a caption marker carrying extra instruction text still surfaces as a flag. Env CAPTIONTEXT_OFF reverts.

image_attrs._round: 240 (Dev-Feedback R3, D1) — content-image alt text + loading="lazy"
image_attrs.note: Applied as a post-fill (MediaBuilder.FinishImg) on free-body + table-cell content images. alt authority: verified iStock API title (run.istockAcks, the *_istock-acks.txt map) > URL-slug Title-Case (the verified 98% slug-is-title rule) > empty. loading=lazy is a forward rule — gold era-mixed 24%; overrides-gold capture Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.r240_img_alt_lazy. Env IMGATTRS_OFF reverts both.
image_attrs.widget_internal_note: ROUND 242 (Dev-Feedback R5) — the r240 recorded RIDER taken: widget-INTERNAL images (InteractiveBuilder.#assetImage) join the same rule. Title authority = the VERIFIED map only (id read from the filename; no URL at that seam, so the slug fallback never fires) — corpus module folders carry no acks file, so the alt fill is corpus-INERT by construction; the only corpus-visible effect is loading=lazy completing flipCard's Mode-P visible template (a named forward-looking r240_img_alt_lazy delta; shapeHover's style-first Mode-P template untouched by the finisher's regex — recorded residue). Env WIDGETIMG_OFF reverts the rider ALONE (IMGATTRS_OFF still kills it too), so it decomposes independently of the r240 body-path rule.

image_reference_title_drop._round: 240 (Dev-Feedback R3, D3) — the image's own title-form reference line never renders
image_reference_title_drop.note:
The round-80 video-title-drop class extended to images: an OWN blackAfter line that fold-equals a non-URL hyperlink anchor of the same paragraph, or matches the iStock reference form, is the media REFERENCE, not a caption (gold ships 0 such

s; Claude shipped 145). Genuinely-following prose is kept. Env IMGREFTITLE_OFF. callouts.rule: One container algorithm serves every callout — only the class differs (a lookup, not logic). Modifier keywords append their class.
callouts.side_column_backward_pair_note: ROUND 123 (Chris, the round-122 logged follow-up). A side_column callout ([Side alert] → alertActivity) is the RIGHT sibling of the immediately-preceding col-md-8 main-content column, in ONE shared <div class="row"> — the human convention, measured 99/100 across the 43 [side alert] modules (`outputs/_measure_sidealert_pairing.py`; only BLL160 has 1 own-row, the 1% editorial exception). Round 122 freed the side alerts from widget absorption but rendered them in their OWN row, dipping the skeleton on own-row-vs-side-by-side placement. ContentConverter's callout emit site detects that rowFor("section") has just closed the preceding content row (parts ends with content_row_close = close col-md-8 + close row), un-closes it, appends #sideAlertCol as the right-sibling col, and re-closes the row. The col-md-8 default content col already matches the human; the EXACT side width (col-md-4 dominant 48 vs col-md-3 44) stays editorial. Falls back to the round-122 own-row form when there is no preceding content row (page-start / consecutive alerts). General + data-described: any future side_column callout pairs the same way. Env SIDEPAIR_OFF reverts to own-row (independent of SIDEALERT_OFF, which reverts the class entirely).
callouts.flowing_tags_note: ROUND 51: these callouts are NOT self-contained own-row boxes (unlike alert/important) — the human renders them as classed paragraphs that FLOW into the current section row (the page-start quote opens the row and the intro flows in). ContentConverter row-groups them as 'block' (flow) and skips the after-breakRow.

containment.rule: STRICT BY DEFAULT — a callout holds ONLY its own content run: the embedded payload plus the black text following its marker, up to the NEXT tag span (the project's core marker model, §1.1: 'the marker's content is the black text that follows it, up to the next marker'). The next [body]/[video]/[image]/heading tag is NEVER inside the callout. ONE exception: when the writer placed an explicit matching [end X] further ahead, the box deliberately spans — everything until that close stays inside.
containment.evidence:
Measured across all 2,045 human pages (12/06/26): .whakatauki direct children are ONLY

(median 2, n=181) — never the following body/video (the OSAI201 over-nesting bug). Large .alert boxes with media inside exist (median direct

0, div-heavy) and correspond to deliberately spanned boxes — the explicit-close pathway.
containment.span_note: While spanning to an explicit [end X], only a section marker or page boundary force-closes early (the writer's close is authoritative).
containment.wrap_note: STRUCTURED-CONTENT WRAP (autoClose mode 'span-wrap'): a content callout (wrap_content — alert/important) with NO black text of its own whose content is a following TABLE spans to CONTAIN it — the strict text-gather would otherwise leave it EMPTY (OSGM501: [Alert] + a 2-col image|text table, where Claude rendered an empty alert and lifted the table out). Unlike an explicit-[end X] span, a wrap is BOUNDED: it ALSO closes at the next heading (rendered level <= wrap_close_heading_max) so it can never over-capture. 18 modules have a callout-immediately-followed-by-table. Code: ContentConverter.#calloutWrapsStructured.

content_wrap.note:
Callouts whose by_tag def has wrap_content:true wrap their STRICT content run in this row>col-12, matching the human gold (measured 2026-06-15: alert content is in alert>row>col-12 ~78% of the time; inner col is col-12 in 94% of cases). whakataukī/quote keep their direct

s (no wrap).

strip_bold.note: ROUND 164 (backlog burn-down — the r161 catalogue 'bold STRIPPED in alert'). The human strips writer **bold** landing inside an alert-family box (class alert / alert solid / alert top / alertActivity) in these 16 subjects — measured LIVE on the r163 corpus (outputs/_measure_alertbold.py): human strips 1103/1153 = 0.96 in scope (per-subject 0.90-1.00; per-SUBCLASS 0.94-1.00, so no subclass sub-convention); the kept minority is span-level key-vocab editorial (HIS 'mana'/'apartheid' definition terms) with NO derivable discriminator -> NET-POSITIVE rendering-normalisation class. Claude kept 130 bold span-hits in scope (28 modules; HIS1003 49 + HIS1004 28 dominate). Fragment families ANZH(0.86)/ART(0.79)/BLL(0.77) OUT of scope; reo/bilingual KEEP bold (TRR strips 0.40) -> exclude_reo via MenuBuilder.isReoModule (r145 class, never mtkFlag). class_pattern tests the by_tag def's OWN open html — whakatauki/quote/wananga/supervisor-panel defs never match, so the strip cannot reach the separately-measured panel/table/widget catalogue buckets; nested tables/widgets render via other paths and are untouched by construction. Strips at the box's own lead/payload/content renders (#calloutOpen both modes + #sideAlertCol) via MenuBuilder.stripTextBold. A span-mode box's LATER main-loop items are a LOGGED residue. Env ALERTBOLD_OFF reverts to kept writer bold.

inline_continuation.note: ROUND 105 (Chris, OSAH501-01) — SAME-BLOCK button/link absorb. A STRICT wrap_content callout (alert/important) absorbs an [external link button]/[Button] (ELEMENT) or [external link] (INLINE) that sits in the SAME WT paragraph (shared source block) as the callout INTO its row>col-12 box, instead of letting it break out as a separate row below. The human renders such a same-sentence external button INSIDE the box (measured corpus-wide 2026-06-24, outputs/_measure_calloutbtn*.* : OSAH501/OSAH301/OSGM101/OSAH401/ANZH404/XGF9006/MXEO401 nest; 13 fire sites / ~9 modules). A button a PARAGRAPH later (different block) is UNTOUCHED — it stays its own row (the CED [alert.top] families, 36 diff-block cases). require_url:true gates absorption on a resolvable http(s) target (block link OR a URL in the item) so a misresolved writer instruction with the word 'button' but no link ('[please add a button to link to SSFUN07…]', SSFUN01) is NOT absorbed. The walk stops at the first different-block / non-absorbable / url-less item, so it can never over-capture. Env CALLOUTBTN_OFF reverts (button renders as a separate row below the box).

side alert._doc:
ROUND 121 (Chris, BLL210) — the writer's `[Side alert]` tip-box. The human renders it as a NARROW SIDE column holding a `
` (NOT the generic `[alert]` box: no `alert` class, no inner row>col-12 wrap, no h4 lead — the content is a direct `

`). Measured corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_sidealert.py`): 43 modules / 64 `[Side alert]` occ → 100 human `alertActivity` elements; Claude built 0 (it matched the bare `alert` substring and emitted a plain alert). `#calloutOpen` routes a def with `side_column` into `

{content}
` and SKIPS the alert wrap_content/lead. The EXACT side-column WIDTH (col-md-4 dominant 265 vs col-md-3 74) + the perfect SIDE-BY-SIDE pairing with the preceding main content (round-94 `pendingSideAlert` territory) are editorial/layout — this round gets the alertActivity CLASS + a side column right; the pairing is a sized follow-up. General + data-described: any future tag with its own output shape is added here the same way (Chris's 'consider other writer tags' directive). Env SIDEALERT_OFF reverts to the plain `[alert]` render.

proverb_normalise.note:
ROUND 225 (Chris, XDLS905/906 screenshots). The writer's proverb = bold reo + SOFT line break (w:br) + English; the extractor drops soft breaks so the two lines GLUE into one

('…ana”Through perseverance…'). Gold house form measured over ALL 215 human .whakatauki boxes: two+ separate PLAIN

(213/215), kept only 2/215, 5/215, wrapping curly/straight quotes 9/215 — the site CSS styles .whakatauki p, so kept double-styles. SPLITS re-derive the lost break from its visible boundary (leading **bold**/*italic* group abutting text · leading “quoted” phrase + prose · space-before pipe · full-tail '(translation)', parens dropped); STRIPS run segment-level via MenuBuilder.stripTextBold/Italic + edge-anchored quote strip. The no-marker language-boundary glue (CEDT501-12, CEDO105) is a measured DECLINE — no derivable split point. Engine: ContentConverter.#proverbSplit + #proverbStripSeg. Env PROVERBNORM_OFF reverts split AND strips. Tool outputs/_measure_whakatauki.py.

whakatauki.proverb_note:
A whakataukī holds ONLY the proverb (reo + english) — the leading SHORT line(s) on/after the marker. The COMMENTARY that follows (a long explanatory paragraph, no marker) is FREE body, not part of the callout. Measured: 137/147 human .whakatauki hold exactly 2

(the proverb), only 4 hold a long paragraph. ContentConverter.#gatherProverb stops at the first paragraph longer than proverb_max_chars (or after proverb_max_paragraphs) and leaves it un-consumed → rendered as body. split_payload_on_pipe splits reo|english on | / – / — (spaced). Fixes XGF9001 (the en-dash proverb + absorbed commentary).
whakatauki.icon_note: 2026-06-12 (round 5): icon img REMOVED — the signed-off OSAI201-00 gold file has a plain <div class="whakatauki"> and the archive has 0/181 with an icon. The earlier icon addition is superseded.
whakatauki.pipe_note:
Writers give the proverb as 'reo | english' on one line; the house form is two separate

s (179/181 in the corpus).

supervisor note.open: Supervisor note
supervisor note.note: The supervisor-note structure from the human gold standard (BLL146-0.0): a row-level super-content block. own_row = the template carries its OWN row/col wrappers, so the engine must NOT wrap it in the standard content row. ROUND 160: the flat open/close above are the LEGACY (round-159) form, kept verbatim for SUPINROW_OFF; the live form is inner_row below.

inner_row._note: ROUND 160 (Chris, BLL225-0.0). The human wraps the panel's two col-12s in an INNER row (super-content row > row > col-12 label + col-12 text) — measured 215/215 human non-activity sites vs Claude 0/214 (outputs/_measure_supervisor_nonactivity.py); the legacy template UNDER-COPIED its own gold source BLL146-0.0. Same class as the round-143.1 activity-panel inner row (the reveal JS keys on the nested structure). Env SUPINROW_OFF reverts to the flat legacy open/close.
inner_row.open: Supervisor note

pair_with_content._note: ROUND 160 (Chris, BLL225-0.0). BLL-family SIDE-BY-SIDE PAIRING: the human anchors a non-activity supervisor note to the section paragraph it annotates — ONE row.supervisor holding the note panel col FIRST + the content col (99/101 paired human sites are BLL; every other subject ships the standalone row — MXFL101 control has the IDENTICAL WT context and stays standalone; outputs/_measure_supervisor_nonactivity.py). Scope: subjects prefix match, BEFORE the page's first [Activity] opener (an in-activity note is round-143/round-160-C territory), companion = the next unconsumed [body] element. The section heading stays in its OWN row; the pre-pass swaps a note-BEFORE-heading ([supervisor note][Introduction][body], BLL225) past the heading so both writer orders ([Introduction][supervisor note][body], BLL111) reach the emit site identically. swap_heading_tags covers the mid-page [Introduction]→title-bar SECTION_MARKER alias; rendered [H1-3] headings (max_heading_level) also qualify. content_col_open_by_series: BLL2 pages carry paddingR (17/7 human), BLL1 plain (37/13). Env SUPPAIR_OFF reverts to the standalone round-159 form.

pair_with_heading._note: ROUND 162 (backlog burn-down — the r160 recorded partial). BLL1 h2-INSIDE variant: on the BLL1 single-file phonics parents (BLL130-160) each letter section opens [H1/H2] heading → [Supervisor note] → [Activity], with NO companion [body] — so pair_with_content declines. The human pairs the note with the HEADING itself: ONE row.supervisor = [panel col + col-md-8 col-12 paddingR holding ONLY the section heading] (measured 20/20 h2-inside human sites are BLL1 parents; outputs/_measure_supervisor_nonactivity.py). COUNTER-EVIDENCE bounds the scope: BLL210 (BLL2 parent) has 2 heading-preceded notes the human leaves STANDALONE → series list is BLL1 ONLY, not BLL-wide. The 2 BLL2 h2-inside sites (BLL246/254_2.0) are INSIDE activity boxes (SUPSCAN territory) — excluded, recorded residue. Fires only when the forward body-pair did NOT fire AND the just-emitted parts tail is a heading-only content row (row_open + <h1-3> + row_close, default col class) — the fold pops that row and re-emits the heading inside the pair's content col. Env SUPPAIRH2_OFF reverts to the standalone form (heading row + lone row.supervisor).

fold_page_label._note: ROUND 163 (backlog burn-down round 2 — the r162 logged residue). The [page N]-LABEL fold: on the BLL1 [page N]-delimited inquiry parents the writer opens a section `[page N]

supervisor note._long_payload_note:
ROUND 162 (backlog burn-down — the r160 BLL111 logged follow-up). A supervisor note whose WHOLE text the writer typed INSIDE the red span fails the ≤12-word lead rule and has no black follower → the panel rendered content-less + an 'Empty [supervisor note]' red flag; the human ships the prose as the panel

(with bare URLs woven). Measured 10 sites / 8 modules, ALL BLL, all genuine note prose (never instructions — instructionFragment keeps the CS-note path). Rendered via renderBlackText so links weave (BLL111-01). Env SUPPAYLOAD_OFF reverts to the dropped-payload + red-flag form.
supervisor note._strip_italic_note: ROUND 162 (backlog burn-down — r161 catalogue 'italic STRIPPED in panel'). The human strips writer *italic* landing INSIDE the supervisor super-content panel in the MXDI+XDLS families: 29/29 WT spans stripped (MXDI 11/11, XDLS 18/18), human panels carry ZERO <i>/<em> there; Claude kept 13 (MXDI103 pages 00/01/04/05). BLL is MIXED (0.64, book/story titles + letter-sound lines are KEPT) and reo/bilingual families keep reo italic → NOT in the list (r145 exclusion class). Applied to the panel's lead + gathered content at #calloutOpen via MenuBuilder.stripTextItalic (Font-Awesome <i class=fa> untouched). Env PANELITALIC_OFF reverts to keeping the writer italic.

modifier_classes._rule: Two-tier positional rule (§5.6): a positional phrase that maps to a documented class here is ACTIONED into the class; one that doesn't is rendered as a red flag at the box.
