lead_element: a short embedded title renders as this element inside the box (corpus: .alert leads are h4-dominant). Callouts without the key keep the bolded

lead.

drop_empty_span_wrap._doc: ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B1 part 2 — SCCH302-01). A span-mode callout ([alert]…[end alert]) opens its inner row>col-12 content wrapper eagerly; when the writer's whole content rode the span's own lead paragraph and the end tag follows immediately, the wrapper ships EMPTY. Measured: converted corpus 70 empty row>col-12 pairs / 60 pages / 28 modules; human gold 2 (one-off outliers) — the human never keeps the empty wrap. ON: the CONTAINER_CLOSE site detects the untouched wrap-open as the last emitted part and drops the pair. Env EMPTYWRAP_OFF reverts.

super_content._note:
ROUND 143 (Chris, BLL241-2 2A). A [Supervisor note] directly after an [Activity] opener has directive CONTAINER_OPEN, so container_auto_close.activity_close_before CLOSES the activity before it — the note is then emitted as its own row supervisor block and the activity's [body]/[image] spill into loose sibling rows BELOW the (now heading-only) box. The human instead NESTS the note as the activity's first child:
>
…note…
+
title+body
. FIX: the [Activity] opener looks ahead for an immediately-following supervisor note; when present #activityOpen adds the super-content-button activity class, emits the nested panel (below) FIRST, then opens a fresh row>col for the title+body — matching the human two-child box exactly. Measured 77 activities corpus-wide (supervisor-note-after-heading; outputs/_measure_activity_containment.py). The 70 plain-row + 53 interactive-next heading-only boxes are DIFFERENT triggers (separate follow-ups). Env SUPNOTE_OFF reverts to the round-142 auto-close + own-row form.
super_content._row_class_note: ROUND 143.2 (Chris — child-dictates-ancestor). The TOP content row wrapping a supervisor-note activity carries '.supervisor' (measured 104/104 human .supervisor rows contain a super-content note; outputs/_measure_child_ancestor_classes.py). The reveal JS keys off .row.supervisor — without it the note renders inline (visible) instead of the hidden icon-modal. The activity opener sets nextRowClass=row_class before its emit so body_region.content_row_open renders '<div class="row supervisor">'.
super_content.panel_open: Supervisor note
super_content._panel_note: ROUND 143.1 (Chris) — the human's super-content panel wraps its two col-12s in an INNER <div class="row"> (super-content row > row > col-12,col-12); the round-143 first cut omitted it, so the idoc_scripts reveal JS left the note VISIBLE inline instead of the hidden icon-triggered modal (BLL241-2 2A/2C). Matching the human structure byte-for-byte restores the modal (the working overview note uses the same super-content structure).

scan_within_activity._note: ROUND 160 (Chris, BLL225-2.0 2E). The writer also places the note MID-activity ([Activity][body][supervisor note][video][end activity]); the human STILL hoists it into the box panel as the FIRST child (BLL225-2.0 verified) — measured 50 mid-activity WT notes vs 69 directly-after (outputs/_measure_supervisor_boxgap.py; human ships 234 super-content activity boxes, Claude built 76 = the round-143 immediate trigger only; the ~115-box residue beyond all WT notes is EDITORIAL — human-added/duplicated notes, recorded C-decline). The opener lookahead now scans forward to the activity's natural boundary (mirroring container_auto_close.activity_close_before semantics: section heading after content / next activity / any auto-close directive or tag / closer / section marker), skipping bundle-consumed members (a note after an embedded interactive still belongs to the box). The found note is consumed IN PLACE (loop index unchanged — the content between opener and note must render); the main loop skips it on arrival via its consumedBy mark. Env SUPSCAN_OFF reverts to the round-143 immediate-only lookahead; SUPNOTE_OFF still reverts the whole super-content mechanism.

standalone_title_heading._round66_note:
ROUND 66 (Chris, BLL233-01). The text trailing an [Activity NX] tag is the activity TITLE; the human renders it as

as the box's first child (measured 86.6% of 6496 human activity boxes start with

, vs 0.2%

— outputs/_measure_activity_title.py). Claude's interactive-OWNED activity path already promotes the lead line to

(#activityOpen renderBlack=false, the addLead title logic). The STANDALONE path (renderBlack=true, a plain [Activity] with no captured widget — BLL233 1E) dumped the whole blackAfter via #renderBlackText as a plain

. Fix: when enabled, #activityOpen promotes the FIRST LINE of blackAfter to (the title) and renders the REST as body, mirroring the owned path exactly. Env ACTTITLE_OFF reverts to the all-

baseline.

number_from_tail._round83_note: ROUND 83 (Chris, ENGC101 deep-dive). Some writers type the activity number OUTSIDE the bracket — '[Activity] 3A' instead of '[Activity 3A]' (ANZH101/HIS family). it.parse.numbers is then EMPTY, so #activityOpen emitted a NUMBERLESS <div class="activity"> — the human gives it the number. MEASURED 180 bare-[Activity] openers corpus-wide whose lead text begins with an activity-number token (outputs/_measure_nested_bare_activity2.py SPLIT_INLINE = 180; tail forms: digit+letter 174, bare-digit-then-title 6, ZERO digit+lowercase-prose — outputs probe). FIX: TagNormaliser lifts a LEADING digit+letter id token from the span's free text (outside the bracket) into parse.numbers when an [Activity] CONTAINER_OPEN tag is present and no bracket number exists — so #activityOpen id, InteractiveScanner activityId, and the adjacent-merge carry all see it. Digit+LETTER only (174/180; the 6 bare-digit cases skipped so prose like '5 minutes' can never be read as a number). Env ACTNUMTAIL_OFF reverts to the numberless box. The human emits a numberless activity box only 0.65% of the time vs Claude's 24% (the discriminator).

bare_reemphasis_merge._round84_note:
ROUND 84 (Chris, ENGC101-02). A writer opens a NUMBERED activity then types a BARE [Activity] (no number) to re-emphasise where the interactive sits WITHIN it — ENGC101 2A: [Activity 2A] -> [H3] Identifying adjectives -> speech-bubble setup -> [Activity] 'Which words...Tick the describing words' -> the quiz. The human keeps ONE
with the bare [Activity]'s text as a

lead-in; Claude opened a SECOND, NUMBERLESS box (splitting 2A). MEASURED (outputs/_measure_nested_bare_activity2.py): the NESTED_PROSE class = 12 hits / 9 modules; in every module the human has ZERO numberless activity boxes. DISCRIMINATOR (merge vs renumber): the human MERGES only when the open numbered activity's OPENER had an EMPTY tail (ENGC101 [Activity 2A] -> title is a separate [H3]); when the opener carried its own title ([Activity 5C] Extra for Experts / [Activity 5E] Pick a task / [Activity 1D] Body rhythm) the bare activity is a NEW sibling the human RENUMBERS (Dropbox/Reflection/Pick-a-task) — so those are LEFT UNCHANGED (no merge). FIX: when a bare [Activity] opener (no number) arrives while the TOP activity is open, has content, and had an EMPTY opener tail (titledOpener=false), AND the bare lead is not an excluded standalone type (dropbox/reflection/journal/upload), flow its lead text into the open activity and suppress the new box. Engine: ContentConverter ConvertPage (guard before autoClose). Env REEMPH_OFF reverts to the split (two boxes).

mode_opener_merge._round202_note: ROUND 202 (Chris, classO ACTIVITY OVER-GENERATION — HIS1004 family). An un-numbered activity opener with NO content of its own — a LAYOUT/MODE annotation the writer types before the real numbered activity ([Activity individual] / [Activity embedded] / [Activity body] / [Activity box] / bare [Activity], remainder empty of a number) — is describing the SAME box as the numbered [Activity NX] that follows it, EVEN ACROSS the box's own title heading. WT shape (HIS1004): [Activity individual] -> [H3] Which rights were taken? -> [Activity 1A] -> press release + drag-drop. GOLD ships ONE <div class="activity" number="1A"> with the H3 as its title INSIDE; Claude split it — the mode opener made an EMPTY-ish box (the H3 as its only child, then auto-closed when the numbered opener's CONTAINER_OPEN directive arrived), then the numbered opener made a second box. MEASURED (outputs/_measure_activityboxes.py, ALL 392 paired modules): over-generation is concentrated in ~25 modules (corpus-wide Claude ships FEWER activity boxes than gold, 0.78x — this is NOT a corpus-wide over-box); the mode-word driven slice (HIS1004 38 empty-ish boxes / HIS1003 / HIS1006 / ANZH301 / ANZH304 / SSFUN02/05/06/08 / CEDR204 / …) is the biggest single mechanism. The round-84 consecutive-opener merge only skips BLANK lines between the two openers; this extends it to skip the box's own TITLE HEADING(s) (up to max_intervening_headings; the HIS1004 pattern is exactly one [H3]) and adopt the numbered opener's id, opening ONE box AT the mode opener's position so the heading lands inside. The numbered opener is marked consumedBy='activity-mode-merge' — it renders only its own lead into the open box, opens no second box, and does not auto-close. GENERAL (keys on 'un-numbered activity opener with empty content', NOT a per-module word list): XDLS903's [Activity] + black-text number '1A' is EXCLUDED because number_from_tail leaves the number in blackAfter (content present); a standalone mode opener with no numbered follower is left as its own box (a separate, measured follow-up — the standalone-embedded class). Engine: ContentConverter ConvertPage (activity CONTAINER_OPEN branch, after the round-84 immediate merge). Env ACTMODEMERGE_OFF reverts to the split (two boxes).

lesson_letter_number._round88_note: ROUND 88 (Chris, ENGI302 Lesson 2): the human numbers an activity box {lessonNumber}{positional-letter} — on lesson page N the K-th activity is N+chr(64+K) (ENGI302 lesson 2: [Activity 1/2/3/4] -> 2A/2B/2C/2D; the WT activity numbers RESET per lesson, the human prepends the lesson number + converts the ordinal to a letter). Claude emitted the BARE WT digit (number="1"/"2"/"3"/"4"). MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_activity_number_scheme.py over 1276 human pages): pageInt+positional 847, pageInt+letters 131, someInt+letter 73, bare-digit ≈ 0 — the human NEVER ships a bare digit, so Claude's bare number matches nothing and the renumber can only help-or-hold (the skeleton keeps number= AND class: ENGI302-02 1->2A and 4->2D EXACT-match the human's div.activity.interactive[number=2A] / div.activity[number=2D]). PREFIX = page.lessonNumber (PageSplitter's writer [LESSON N] / running lesson ordinal — robust to the 13/105 file-count misalignments, since it tracks the WT lesson structure the human uses, not Claude's -NN file index). LETTER = positional order of the activity within the lesson (A,B,C…), counted across sub-pages of the same lessonNumber (human sub-page letters CONTINUE 40 vs restart 11), reset per module. ONLY a BARE-DIGIT id is transformed — a round-83 tail-lifted letter id ('1A') is KEPT; overview pages (lessonNumber null) untouched; idx>=26 falls back to the bare digit. Env ACTLETTER_OFF reverts to the bare WT digit.
lesson_letter_number._integer_prefix_doc: ROUND 222b (Chris, the ENGJ403 '1.0A' screenshot). The {lessonNumber}{letter} renumber uses the INTEGER lesson part of a DOTTED page lesson number ('1.0'→'1', '5.1'→'5') as both the id prefix AND the letter-map key — the human ships '1A'/'5D', never '1.0A'/'5.1A' (measured: every gold in the affected class ENGJ403/CEDK501/CEDT501/MXDB301/MXEO301/MXFL302 is integer+letter), and integer map keys let a lesson split over sub-pages (2.0→2.1) CONTINUE its lettering (gold 2A then 2B/2C). The letter-LESS dotted-id gold convention (number='1.1') is writer-typed ids kept verbatim — it never enters this renumber. Env ACTLNINT_OFF reverts to the raw dotted prefix/key.

embedded_interactive_activity._round92_note: ROUND 92 (Chris, ENGS302-01). A writer tags an interactive AND its activity number in ONE bracket — '[Activity 1A drag and drop]' — so the span's primary directive is INTERACTIVE (drag and drop) while it ALSO carries the [activity] tag + the number. InteractiveScanner gives the bundle activityId='1A' but NO activityOwner (there is no separate [Activity] item to walk back to), so the converter's activity-wrapper path (gated on activityOwner) was SKIPPED and the dragAndDrop rendered as a BARE cv2-interactive placeholder with no <div class="activity"> around it. The human wraps it: <div class="activity interactive" number="1A"> (verified ENGS302-01 1A, ANZH205 '[Activity: Embedded – Vertical Drag and Drop]' -> 1A, AGH1004 drag-drop activities). FIX: when a bundle has an activityId from its OWN interactive tag's [activity] tag (no separate owner), open the activity wrapper around the placeholder (forceInteractive per the widget type, the round-58 .interactive rule); the title/instructions/data stay INSIDE the placeholder (un-built widget — gate-excluded skip_classes). MEASURED (outputs/_measure_round92.cjs): the numbered embedded form recurs across the corpus; the human ships a numbered activity box for it. Env EMBACT_OFF reverts to the bare placeholder (no activity wrapper).

reo_bundle_activity._status: STILL PARKED (default-off) — round 135. WITH the content_table_guard ON, the box correctly wraps the REAL widget (TRR102 A/B = skeleton +5.0, compare_structure +64) — the over-capture diagnosis was right. BUT the guard itself is net-negative across the full set (it loses the embedded widget on box-less modules; see content_table_guard._status), so BOTH stay parked until the PROSE+WIDGET SPLIT lands. Flip content_table_guard + this flag ON together (with the split). _status pre-guard below. The round-134 page-split fixed the page MISALIGNMENT, and the boxes now land on the RIGHT lesson pages with the right numbers (TRR102 0→13, on pages 1.0-5.0 matching the human). BUT a SECOND dependency surfaced: the InteractiveScanner OVER-CAPTURES the bilingual intro CONTENT table as a spurious flipCard, because the writer embeds `[Interactive] [Flipcard]` INSIDE the intro `[Body]` cell — so the box wraps the WHOLE intro (Activity NX: + [H2] heading + [Body], as a flipCard cv2) instead of the real widget, AND the row's number lands on that intro-flipCard, not the actual activity widget. A/B (_ab.py REOACT_OFF=1 TRR102) = skeleton −1.58 (over-captured box wraps the wrong content). So the OVER-CAPTURE must be fixed first (a reoMode #interactiveInTable guard: a bilingual English|Māori content table is NOT a widget just because a body cell mentions [Interactive] [X] — it should unfold via #bilingualTable). That fix also corrects the intro rendering. THEN flip enabled:true + re-A/B. env REOACT_OFF reverts to the bare placeholder.
reo_bundle_activity._round133_note: ROUND 133 (Chris, TRR102 — bilingual ACTIVITY scanner integration). In a reoTranslate module the activity NUMBER is a table ROW ('Activity 1A:' / 'Ngohe 1A:') inside the bilingual English|Māori content table, NOT an [Activity N] TAG, so the InteractiveScanner opener-lookback never found an owner and the widget bundle rendered as a bare cv2-interactive placeholder with no <div class="activity"> wrapper — the human wraps every activity widget: <div class="activity interactive" number="1A">. FIX (reoMode-scoped, reuses the EXISTING bundle wrapper machinery — no parallel path): a post-scan pass in InteractiveScanner tracks the most recent 'Activity NX:'/'Ngohe NX:' row and hands its number to the FIRST following widget bundle (one number -> one box, claimed-per-row so a second bundle before the next row stays inline), setting bundle.activityId + bundle.reoActivity. ContentConverter's bundle path then opens the activity wrapper via a synthetic owner (no lead — the bilingual intro heading/body renders as its own section OUTSIDE the box, matching the human; .interactive forced per the round-58 widget-type rule). MEASURED (outputs/_measure_bilingual_activity.py): the human ships ~252 div.activity across the 19 Bilingual modules; the 'Activity NX:'-row convention cleanly carries the number on TRR102 (20/20 human numbers matched) and the other 1A-row modules; the 1.1-positional modules (PNR/TRR103/.../no clean row) are a measured follow-up. SCOPE: reoMode only (standard modules carry the 'Activity NX:' text too — e.g. ENGS302 — but reoMode is false for them, so they are byte-identical). Env REOACT_OFF reverts to the round-132 bare placeholder (no wrapper, activityId unset).

standalone_widget_box._types_interactive_note: 'interactive' is the round-217 bare-[Interactive] generic invocation (Tag_Lexicon _meta.qualifier_alias_demote.standalone_becomes) — the scanner names the bundle after the tag, so it arrives here as type 'interactive', not 'unclassified'. Gold boxes the bare-invocation class 3/3 on AGH1001-01 and it is a task invocation by authoring intent.
standalone_widget_box._round217_note: ROUND 217 (Chris — the activity/interactive BOUNDARY audit, 2026-07-12). A TASK-type interactive the writer authored with NO [Activity] tag (AGH1001-01: '[Interactive] Drag and drop the products…' + data table) is STILL boxed by the human developer — an invented <div class="activity interactive" number="1B"> wrapping instruction + widget, numbered in the lesson's ordinary letter sequence (the gold library ships 6,863 activity boxes against only 5,663 writer [Activity*] tags — the human invents ~1,200; whole families e.g. MXDI/HIS author with ZERO [Activity] tags). MEASURED per Claude bundle type over every paired module (outputs/_measure_standalone_boxing.py — for each STANDALONE Claude widget, does the gold put that same content inside an activity box?): dragAndDrop 0.97 (73 decided) / unclassified 0.88 (163) / multiChoiceQuiz 0.89 (38) / radioQuiz 0.88 (8) / selfCheck 0.83 (6) → listed; the DISPLAY types (accordion 0.11 / carousel 0.11 / speechBubble 0.12 / clickDrop 0.12 / flipCard 0.12 / tabs 0.14 / modal 0.16 / hintSlider 0.12 / shapeHover 0.00 / glossary+timeline 0.00) stay bare BY CONSTRUCTION (not listed); the AMBIGUOUS band (dropDown 0.57 / selectionBox 0.78 / typing 0.60 / slider 0.43 / reorder 0.50, small n) is RECORDED as a follow-up needing a finer group-level discriminator — do NOT add these without re-measuring. The box takes the human's `activity interactive` form (force_interactive — the box exists BECAUSE of the widget) and the NEXT positional {lessonNumber}{letter} id (ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen positionalId=true — the human counts its invented boxes IN SEQUENCE with the tagged ones, which is why Claude's letters drifted on such pages: the A_WRONG class of the boundary audit). The gold's own box TITLE heading is human-authored (in no WT) — recorded C, never invented. reoMode excluded (bilingual bundles have reo_bundle_activity + their own placeholder surface). Matches on bundle.type ONLY (extraTypes-merged bundles fire via their primary type). Env toggle ACTWRAP_OFF reverts to the bare un-boxed placeholder/build.
standalone_widget_box._boundary_audit_note: The full audit that found this class: outputs/_measure_boundary_audit.py (per-block Claude-vs-gold containment diff over all paired pages: W_OVER/W_UNDER/A_OVER/A_SPILL/A_WRONG) + _measure_boundary_triggers.py (first spilled/absorbed item per box) + _measure_widget_boxing.py (gold-side census: task types ~1.00 boxed, display types 0.05-0.46) + _measure_standalone_boxing.py (the per-type standalone discriminator above). Remaining measured classes recorded in the round-217 changelog entry: A_OVER first-trigger [body]-after-widget ~187 groups; W_OVER runaway unclassified placeholders 1,118 blocks; the ambiguous-band types; supervisor-note A_OVER 53 (mostly the recorded r160 editorial residue).

prose_interactive_rows._round229_note: ROUND 229 (Chris — the Change Ledger CL-0030+CL-0048 activity pair kickoff). CL-0048/CL-0036 (constraint 63): inside an activity, prose sits in its OWN inner row and the interactive follows in a SEPARATE inner row at the wrapper width. MEASURED over every gold activity box (outputs/_activity_anatomy_core.py + _measure_activity_inner_rows.py, 7,539 gold boxes): the gold library largely PREDATES the rule — same_col (prose+widget in ONE inner col, Claude's pre-round form) is the gold-dominant anatomy at 75.4% of widget-carrying boxes and SOLIDIFIES (r182 >=0.60) at corpus level, so the UNIVERSAL flip is NOT live (captured overrides_gold in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.cl0048_prose_interactive_rows — the r219 CL-0007 pattern; doc-14's own Mode-B rule keeps gold/sibling structure authoritative for the built corpus). This registry holds the groups whose gold DOES solidify the SEPARATED form — where the flip is a fix-TOWARD-gold: generated by _measure_activity_inner_rows.py --gen (never hand-typed; gates sep_share>=0.60, n>=20 decided boxes, >=5 modules, widget col >=0.80 solid). ENFUN|Fundamentals: 77/96 = 0.802 separated (76 two_rows / 1 sibling_col), widget col 'col-md-12 col-12' 74/77 = 0.96; gold form byte-eyeballed (ENFUN02 1D): activity > row > col-12 [PROSE] /row + row > col-md-12 col-12 [WIDGET] /row. The prose col is NOT changed by this rule (gold prose col for a DEFAULT-width col-md-8 wrapper = col-12, 21/24 ENFUN + 205/236 corpus-wide two_rows — Claude's existing open already emits col-12; the gold prose col-md-8 minority rides WIDENED wrappers col-11/col-md-11, which Claude does not emit — the CL-0007 widths stay parked per round 219). Fires ONLY when the activity-owned bundle emitted PROSE first (title/lead/table — the actProse flag): a widget-only box keeps the single-col form (gold widget_only ships col-12). A box with prose AFTER the widget is the measured 4/77-gold / 3/76-Claude fringe — the split still applies and trailing prose lands in the widget row (recorded residue; gold's own 4 use a third row). Groups NOT earning a row keep same_col BY CONSTRUCTION: ENGFUN|Inquiry (5/5 sep but 1 module, below floors; Claude fires 0 there), PNR|Bilingual (7/10, 2 modules + the r220-recorded bilingual boundary territory), MXFL|Standard (0.384 — its gold separated share rides wrapper WIDENING Claude does not emit). ENFUN09 is the family's own gold deviant (6 same_col vs 2 sep — the r123 single-deviation class): family form ships uniformly, its ~6 boxes are the named net-positive collateral. Env toggle ACTROWS_OFF reverts to the single-col flow.

activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types_round64_note: ROUND 64 (Chris, ENGS401-01) — added the SELECTION/INPUT/ORDERING task types the round-50 list missed, measured by number-matched human convention (outputs/_measure_tasktype_convention.py): typing 96% (22/23), selectionBox 89% (8/9), dropDown 64% (21/33 — ≈ the existing selfCheck 69% threshold), clickingOrder 100% (3/3), crossword 100%. VERIFIED corpus-wide fix: ENGS401-04 4A (dropDown) and ENGS401-05 5A (carousel + typing, caught by the round-64 MULTI-TYPE marker scan that splits 'A + B' banners — the round-58 regex only read the FIRST type) now match the human's .interactive. NOTE ENGS401-01 (Chris's flagged page) is NOT fixed by this and is a SEPARATE deeper issue: its activity 1A is .interactive in the human because of a PROSE-authored emotion-selection ('select the emotion that best matches how you feel'); its [modal] tags are merely video pop-ups (display) and its carousel is display — so Claude correctly types both PLAIN. There is no task TAG to key off; a prose-selection classifier is the future pass, NOT a blanket rule. DELIBERATELY NOT added (the human keeps them PLAIN, number-matched): modal 12%, carousel 12%, accordion 21%, flipCard 23%, clickDrop 24%, tabs 15%, slider 33%, rotateBanner 17%, speechBubble 17% — a TRUE blanket 'any interactive -> .interactive' rule would flip ~2,000 of these against the human and regress the skeleton gate. Reversal: env ACTINT_OFF (the whole post-pass) or remove these entries.
activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types_note: An activity that OWNS a widget of one of these types gets the .interactive class (the 'circle' task indicator; plain .activity is the 'triangle'). The widget TYPE is the WT signal — measured per type across the 4,345 human files in 02-All_HTML_Files (reference/tests/interactive_col_sweep.py): these all carry .interactive in >=75% of in-activity instances (reorder 95, wordDrag 91, memoryGame 90, dropQuiz 87, radioQuiz 85, wordSelect 85, bingo 84, multiChoiceQuiz 79, dragAndDrop 77, selfCheck 76). DISPLAY widgets stay plain .activity (flipCard 32, carousel 25, accordion 17, clickDrop 14, speechBubble 9; typing 65 / slider 52 borderline → excluded). This REFINES the round-8 'don't force .interactive globally' (61% corpus-wide) into a per-type rule. Invisible to compare_structure (it records 'activity' for both).

strip_bold.note: ROUND 165 (backlog burn-down round 4 — the r161 catalogue 'bold STRIPPED in activity', tmpl:Fundamentals 0.913). The human strips writer **bold** landing in an ACTIVITY box's own body text (plain p/li black text) in the strong Fundamentals families — measured LIVE on the r164 corpus (outputs/_measure_actbold.py, alert-split): ARFUN 0.95 / ENFUN 0.91 / HPFUN 1.00 / MXFUN 0.97 / XFUN 1.00 = 846/892 = 0.949 combined (real non-alert activity regions). Fragments stay OUT: TEFUN 0.49 (genuinely MIXED) / SSFUN 0.75 / SCFUN n=7; non-Fundamentals templates 0.75-0.87 are out (the catalogue cell is Fundamentals-scoped); reo excluded via MenuBuilder.isReoModule (r145 class, never mtkFlag). The kept minority (46 span-hits, ARFUN04-clustered 'Instructions:'/'Goal:' leads + key vocab) has NO derivable discriminator — the colon-lead cut was cross-tabbed and does NOT separate (keep-rate 0.14 colon vs 0.02 plain INSIDE ARFUN04 itself) -> NET-POSITIVE class (paired fixable 65 vs collateral 18, NET +47, projected match 0.70->0.90). REGION discriminator = the LIVE container stack: the mapper strips ONLY while the stack TOP is an open ACTIVITY (mode 'activity') — a span callout on top (the r164 alert cell, which KEEPS bold in these non-r164 subjects), strict callouts, kept tables, widgets, headings and media all emit via other paths/stack states and are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. Claude pre-fix kept 125 in-scope span-hits = 87 <b> nodes / 10 modules (ARFUN04 98). Applied at ConvertPage's main-loop black-text emit sites via #activityBoldStripper + MenuBuilder.stripTextBold. Env ACTBOLD_OFF reverts to kept writer bold.

interactive_col_ceiling_note: BRIEF §3 FINDING (interactive_col_sweep.py over 4,345 human files): the top-most col-* ceiling for EVERY interactive type is overwhelmingly 'col-12 col-md-8' — the body_region.content_col_class_default the converter ALREADY emits. dragAndDrop: col-12.col-md-8 997 (55%) vs col-12.col-md-12 242 (13%); even .images dragAndDrops are 71% col-md-8 and .interactive activities 57% col-md-8. So a per-type WIDER ceiling (e.g. col-md-12 for dragAndDrop) is NOT corpus-supported and is NOT enforced — it would regress the col-md-8 majority. ENGS301-1.0's col-md-12 is a NON-DERIVABLE minority (per-instance layout choice, ~8% of image dragAndDrops); the converter's col-md-8 is the corpus-correct default. Findings: reference/WT_Triangulation_Findings.md + reference/tests/col_ceiling_findings.json.

mode_P.note: Mode P = visible placeholder + commented-out real reference (one of the only two permitted comment uses). The comment sits immediately after the visible placeholder.

filename_rules.label_rule: The Mode-P label is the media item number or 'image' — short, URL-safe.

image.uniform_rule: The chosen mode applies to EVERY image in the conversion run — no mixing (brief §8.1).

video.host_note: youtube-nocookie.com is the dominant corpus host (885 pages vs 473 plain youtube.com, measured 12/06/26).
video.timing_note: Writer timing notes (play from 0.18 to 5.30 …) render as red flags AT the embed — the visible note is the contract; translating to start/end params is optional and never replaces the note.

icon_rule._round200_note: ROUND 200 (Chris, backlog item 3 — the videoSection `icon` play-button styling). The human adds `icon` to a videoSection div as a per-SUBJECT/SERIES HOUSE STYLE, not a per-video choice — measured outputs/_measure_videoicon.cjs over ALL 392 paired gold modules: 82% of video-carrying modules are internally PURE (all-icon 182 / all-plain 126) vs 65 MIXED, and every per-video rule tested (first-video, in-carousel, in-activity, media-kind) lands ~56-59% on mixed modules = no per-video signal. The icon-vs-plain CHOICE SOLIDIFIES (r182 solidify: pooled video-share, a SERIES with n>=3 modules at share>=0.85, else a SUBJECT|TEMPLATE with n>=5 at share>=0.80) ONLY in these groups; the near-tie groups (1-10 Blended Literacy|Standard 51%, 1-10 English|Standard 53%, ConnectED|Inquiry 61%) do NOT solidify and stay PLAIN (default). MediaBuilder.media post-replaces the class token `videoSection ` -> `videoSection icon ` (the videoHost-replace precedent, MediaBuilder L111) when the run's module (from Module_Structure_Index.module_meta) has its series in icon_series OR its subject|template in icon_subject_template. Conservative ship (Chris-approved): 115 modules, projected +1163 net video-nodes matching gold, 94% correct in the shipped set; the 73 wrong are the documented net-positive collateral incl. 5 pure-plain modules (ANZH404, BLL171, BLL172, BLL174, EXPFUN06 — the r164 net-positive class). Widget-embedded videos (accordion/tab/carousel builders that call video.youtube directly) keep plain this round = recorded follow-up. env VIDEOICON_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts to all-plain, byte-identical to r199.

audio.note: Corpus form. The developer drops the real file into audio/ — a missing filename stays empty exactly as the corpus does, plus the writer's sourcing note as a red flag.

absorb_following_url._round88_note:
ROUND 88 (Chris, ENGI302-02): a plain [Button] (e.g. 'Go to journal') whose URL sits on the IMMEDIATELY-FOLLOWING standalone bare-URL paragraph is the human's LINKED button — the URL is loaded onto the button as its href, the bare-URL

is dropped (human '

Download journal
'; verified ENGI302/ENGJ202/SSOG301/MXDI301). Claude rendered '
Go to journal
' + a separate '

URL

'. FIX: #element button branch — when key==='button', the button has NO url of its own, and bodyItems[i+1] is a STANDALONE bare URL (whole content is one http(s) URL, not a tag/element, not consumed), absorb it as the href (buttons.button_linked.form) and mark it _consumed (the loop's round-72 skip drops it). The href VALUE is the WT URL (the human re-points to a fresh copy-doc / generic Drive link — non-derivable editorial); the STRUCTURE + label match. Tight: only the bare-URL-alone next item (same discriminator as round 76), never prose; skipped when the dropbox-orange override fires. Env BTNURL_OFF reverts to the un-linked button + separate bare-URL

.

button_download._round96_note:
ROUND 96 (Chris, ENGS302-01): a [button] whose RAW in-bracket text contains 'download' (e.g. '[Download learning journal button]') is the human's DOWNLOAD button —
{label}
(orange), NOT a plain
'Go to your journal'
. The label is the writer's in-bracket descriptive text with the trailing 'button(s)' word stripped ('Download learning journal'). SCOPED to an explicit 'download' in the tag text: the corpus-dominant downloadButton (32x 'Download journal', 'Response sheet', 'Explore an artwork') is rendered by the human from a BARE [Button]/[Add button] where the label + class are the developer's editorial choice (NON-derivable; measured outputs/_measure_dropbox.py: 59/77 downloadButtons sit in a PLAIN activity, so the parent 'dropbox' class is NOT download-button-triggered and is left alone). Env DLBTN_OFF.

external link button._round56_note:
Chris, OSAI201-02. The human's external-link button is
LABEL
 (class externalButton, NOT button — measured 830 human externalButtons). The writer often drops the marker INLINE in a body sentence ('Click here to play Quick Draw [external link button] https://… then come back and do the activity.'), so the text AFTER the URL is running prose, not the button label. ContentConverter.#element: for an external link button it extracts the URL, uses a SHORT (<=label_max_words, no end-punctuation) trailing phrase as the label else a derivable DEFAULT ('Go to website', or 'Go to video' for a video URL — the human's two dominant defaults), and RE-EMITS the remaining trailing prose as body so it is neither lost nor mislabelled. (The exact editorial label e.g. 'Quick, Draw!' is the game's proper name — not derivable from the WT; the default is the safe convention.)

dropbox_orange_house_style._round66_note: ROUND 66 (Chris, BLL233-01). The human renders a dropbox button as ORANGE <div class="buttonD"> in some modules and GREEN <div class="button"> in others. NOT a per-button call-to-action rule: the SAME label 'Upload to dropbox' is GREEN 496x AND ORANGE 378x corpus-wide. The colour is a PER-MODULE HOUSE STYLE (98.9% single-colour per module) that tracks the module CODE PREFIX (subject family): Blended Literacy (BLL) = orange (78/83 BLL modules; the other subjects AGH/ANZH/CED/ENG/MX/... = green). buttonD is EXCLUSIVELY dropbox text corpus-wide (388/388), so the rule fires ONLY when BOTH hold: the resolved plain [button] label matches label_match ('dropbox', case-insensitive) AND the module-code prefix is in module_prefixes. Engine: ContentConverter.#element button branch swaps button.form -> button_dropbox.form. Chris chose 'All BLL modules' (accepts ~5 BLL modules the human kept green: BLL171/240 mixed, BLL246/252/254 green). The <a href=...rcode=TCS-NNNNNN> dropbox link wrapper is a per-module D2L id absent from the WT+Media List (non-derivable) — match the COLOUR only, exactly as the current green buttons already omit the link. Env DROPBOXD_OFF reverts every dropbox button to green.

go_journal.label: Go to your journal
go_journal._doc_member_branch_yields_to_builder: ROUND 289 — the other end of the accordion's go-to-journal contract (interactive_builders.accordion.panel_delimiters.go_journal_member). #goJournalTail's MEMBER branch ships this heading for any bundle whose member walk captured a go-to-journal [button]; from round 289 the accordion BUILDER skips that member as panel content and emits the heading itself after the widget, so for a bundle that built, the member branch would emit a second identical heading. When the builder has emitted one it sets bundle._goJournalEmitted and this flag makes the member branch stand down — the round-273 'emit exactly once, wherever the item is reached' discipline. A bundle that did NOT build never sets the flag, so every hand-off box behaves exactly as it did at round 288. Env ACCGOJOURNAL_OFF reverts the builder side and with it this one, since the flag is then never set.
go_journal._doc_absorb_suppresses_own_render: ROUND 273 (Chris, the SCCH302-03 screenshot — 'the button is added twice'). THE DOUBLE-EMIT FIX. absorb_into_activity (r239) pulls a go-to-journal [button] that sits after a bundle-owned activity's widget INSIDE the still-open box and marks the item _consumed — but the main loop has no general _consumed guard for a TAG item, only the positional 'skip the items immediately after me' idiom, which cannot reach this button because the widget's own unconsumed end tag ([end click and drop]) sits in between. The button therefore also rendered on its own turn, producing a SECOND identical h4 in a bare row underneath the closed box. With this flag on, the absorb additionally marks the item _goJournalAbsorbed and the main loop skips it outright (skipping the ITEM, not just its emission, so no empty row/col is left behind). MEASURED on the shipped corpus: EXACTLY 5 pages / 5 modules carry the adjacent duplicate pair (CEDO102_0_0, ENGC102_3_0, MXFL103_1_5, SCCH301_3_0, SCPH301_6_0) plus the developer's SCCH302_3_0 — every one of them the same signature (correct h4 inside the activity, identical duplicate in a bare row directly after). Every other go-journal site is single and untouched BY CONSTRUCTION (the flag only ever fires on an item this absorb itself claimed). Env GOJOURNALDUP_OFF restores the duplicate; GOJOURNAL_OFF still reverts the whole r239 rule.
go_journal._doc:
ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B4 — SCCH302-03 activity 3D). A [button] whose EXPLICIT label folds to 'go to (your) journal' (or the alias-typed [go to journal]/[journal button] span — raw_match is anchored to the WHOLE folded span so a longer prose span can never false-fire; an alias span's real trailing prose is kept as body text after the heading, never stripped) ships the design team's templated

Go to your journal

INSIDE the open activity box, never a green
. MEASURED over ALL WTs: ~1,051 occ / 111 modules (728 black-label + 239 alias-typed + 84 in-span). The gold library is ERA-MIXED — h4.goJournal x568 / 57 modules vs
Go to journal x1,052 / 104 modules, MIXED within most subjects (no group discriminator) — the developer's feedback names the h4 as the design team's CURRENT convention, so this ships as a FORWARD-LOOKING overrides-gold rule (captured in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.r239_go_journal_h4; button-gold divergences at the Round-6 regen are INTENTIONAL named deltas, never chased). A button that carries/absorbs a URL keeps the existing button behaviour (gold h4 has no href); an EMPTY [button] whose label came only from journal_label_default is NOT retagged (conservative — bare buttons are also the source of gold's editorial downloadButtons). absorb_into_activity: a go-to-journal button sitting directly after a bundle-owned activity's widget is pulled INSIDE the still-open box before it closes (the r232 mtkQuizBundleTail placement class). Env GOJOURNAL_OFF reverts everything to the plain green button.

download_journal._doc: ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B5 — SCCH302-02 activity 2B). The writer's [button to download journal with standard instructions] ships the design team's templated download scaffold byte-verbatim from the developer's specification: the docs/{CODE} Journal.docx anchor + downloadButton + the empty hint + hintDropContent(oneDrive) divs, plus ONE red+bold Designer/Developer To Do note that the journal document itself must be created. Env DLJOURNAL_OFF reverts to the round-96 route (raw bracket text as the label).

manifest_unbuilt_only._note: ROUND 159 (Chris) — {CODE}_interactives.txt is the HAND-OFF WORKLIST: an interactive the converter already BUILT into the generated HTML is not work, so its entry is OMITTED and the per-entry list renumbers over the un-built only (measured at ship: 444 built entries dropped corpus-wide, 5,631 kept, all 387 txt files rewritten). The summary header KEEPS both counts (useful telemetry) with its NOTE lines rewritten to match; the per-entry 'Status:' line is DROPPED when this is on (every listed entry is un-built by construction — boilerplate). The txt is invisible to the HTML-only golden manifest and to every protected gate. Env MANIFESTALL_OFF (or enabled:false) restores the full round-138 list byte-identically.

manifest_faithful_content._note: ROUND 176 (Chris, ENGC101-02) — the 'Content:' block of {CODE}_interactives.txt must reproduce the writer's authored lines EXACTLY, so the developer knows precisely what belongs in the widget. The round-138 capture used each member's blackAfter, which DROPPED the red-highlighted words (the very adjectives the activity teaches — 'big, blue'/'stripey'/'cold'/'curious'/'excited') and STRIPPED the bracketed [Speech bubble] tags, leaving gap-riddled fragments ('There are two'/'fish and lots of'/'fish.'). ON: ManifestBuilder renders Content from the members' UNIQUE SOURCE BLOCKS (deduped, reading order), cleaning ONLY the 🔴[RED TEXT] sentinels + ** markers via #clean — so brackets + red words + full sentences survive. The txt is a developer-only working file (never ships) and is invisible to the HTML-only golden manifest + every protected gate. Env MANIFESTFAITHFUL_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts to the round-138 blackAfter capture byte-identically. SUPERSEDED at the entry level by manifest_raw_verbatim below (when that is ON, the raw renderer replaces this entry body); this stays the fallback when raw is OFF.

manifest_raw_verbatim._note: ROUND 205 (Chris) — for the UN-BUILT interactives, {CODE}_interactives.txt must carry the RAW parsed content VERBATIM, so the developer building the widget by hand sees exactly what the writer authored, unprocessed. The faithful mode (round 176) still ran each source block through #clean (stripping the 🔴[RED TEXT] sentinels + ** bold markers + collapsing whitespace) and rendered captured tables in a separate 'Data (Table N — Headers:/Row N:)' section. ON: each un-built entry keeps only its MINIMAL header (INTERACTIVE N of M, the extract REFERENCE CODE + hint when in extract mode, File, Placeholder marker, Activity, Type) and then a single 'Content:' block that walks the member SOURCE BLOCKS in reading order (deduped by block identity) and prints each block's raw text EXACTLY — sentinels, [tags], ** and all — with a captured TABLE rendered INLINE at its position as the ┌─── TABLE ───/│ cell ║ cell/└─── END TABLE ─── ASCII box (which is literally the table block's own raw serialised text). The Modifier / Tier / Data Pattern / Position / Activity Heading / Writer Instructions / Associated Media / Red Flags sections are DROPPED from the raw un-built entry (Chris: type + anchor + raw content only). BUILT entries are already omitted by manifest_unbuilt_only, so this only affects the hand-off worklist. The txt is a developer-only working file (never ships) and is invisible to the HTML-only content manifest + every protected gate (rounds 159/176). Env MANIFESTRAW_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts to the round-176 faithful/processed form byte-identically.

extract._note: ROUND 138 (Chris) — the Phase-1 INTERACTIVE HAND-OFF mode. When ConversionRun.interactiveMode === 'extract' (UI switch ON / env INTEXTRACT_ON, uniform across the whole run like imageMode), an UN-BUILT interactive is NOT rendered on the page: the dashed box above is replaced by a SINGLE loud, unique REFERENCE CODE marking its exact spot, and the captured content is handed off via {CODE}_interactives.txt (ManifestBuilder) headed by the SAME code. Default interactiveMode 'inline' never reads this block, so OFF output is byte-identical to before. SCOPE: un-built placeholder interactives only — built widgets stay rendered; the bilingual-unbuilt content-table placeholders are out of scope (a sized follow-up). REVERSAL: leave env INTEXTRACT_ON unset (UI default), or set enabled:false here.
extract._default_mode_note: ROUND 235 (Chris) — the hand-off is now the DEFAULT for every run: the UI switch is GONE (index.html section 3 removed) and both entries resolve interactiveMode from THIS key via ConversionRun.DefaultInteractiveMode (shared code — entry parity preserved). 'extract' + collapse.enabled:true = the shipped default (reference-code marker box + the raw content rendered COLLAPSED inside it, expandable). Env INTCOLLAPSE_OFF (or default_mode:'inline' + collapse.enabled:false) reverts the WHOLE round byte-for-byte to the r234 behaviour: inline dashed boxes by default, bare-marker extract only under legacy INTEXTRACT_ON.

collapse._note: ROUND 235 (Chris) — the COLLAPSIBLE hand-off box, now the default rendering for every un-built interactive: the loud rainbow reference-code marker keeps its exact search-by-code contract (class cv2-int-ref + data-cv2-index/data-cv2-ref + the {label} text), gains the class cv2-interactive on the SAME wrapper (so every gate exclusion — skeleton collapse, compare/body placeholder pruning, the defect leak scan, the EmojiStrip/LinkTextDisplay verbatim-zone walks — applies to the whole box exactly as it did to the old dashed box), and now CONTAINS the raw captured content (the exact inline-mode rendering: retained writer notes + the dashed box) inside a container that is COLLAPSED by default and expands/collapses with an animated (CSS grid-template-rows transition) click on the ▼/▲ arrow at the right end of the marker row. The Page Stitcher is unaffected: it replaces the whole balanced cv2-int-ref element by data-cv2-ref, so the hidden raw content is swapped out together with the marker when the finished widget is stitched in. Env INTCOLLAPSE_OFF (or enabled:false here, with default_mode:'inline') reverts to r234.

_interactive_builders_README: INTERACTIVE BUILDERS  — the data half of the 'easy widgets' auto-build.
WHAT THIS BLOCK IS:
Each key below is the name of an interactive WIDGET the converter now knows
how to BUILD for real (not just dump as an orange placeholder). The value is
the exact HTML the finished widget should be made of, with {curly} slots the
engine fills from the captured Writers-Template data.
WHO READS IT:
app/js/InteractiveBuilder.js. For every captured interactive it looks up
interactive_builders[<type>]. If a template is here AND enabled, it builds
the widget. If the type is missing, disabled, or the data does not fit the
shape cleanly, the builder backs off and the old orange placeholder is shown
instead — so a half-understood interactive is NEVER shipped wrong.
HOW TO EDIT (no JavaScript needed for wording / class / attribute changes):
• To change a widget's markup, edit its open / row / close strings here.
• To TURN A WIDGET OFF (go back to placeholder), set its enabled to false.
• {front} {back} etc. are the only moving parts — keep them spelled exactly.
• Whitespace/newlines inside the strings are cosmetic; the HTML formatter
re-indents the page afterwards, so write them however reads clearest.
HOW TO ADD A WHOLE NEW WIDGET (one data entry + one small code case):
1. Add a new key here with its open/row/close template (copy hintSlider).
2. Add a matching `case "<type>":` in InteractiveBuilder.js that maps the
captured table/members into the slots. That file explains exactly how.
Everything else (placeholder fallback, manifest, logging) is automatic.
SERIES-ANCHOR NOTE: widget MARKUP is corpus-wide and lives here. If one
subject/series ever needs a different shape for the SAME widget, that
belongs in the per-series anchor profile (see PHASE1_PART2_SPEC.md §A),
not as a code branch — same rule as every other style decision.

hint._note: ROUND 277 — the HINT ELEMENT. hint and hintSlider are DIFFERENT elements (measured over all 2,385 gold pages: hintSlider = div.hintSlider > hintRow > infoContainer > frontInfo|backInfo, 161 occ / 56 modules; hint = a title + a span.hint trigger + a sibling div.hintDropContent), and interactive_builders carried NO hint key at all — so Build returned null at its missing-template guard BEFORE dispatch and the writer's Need-help tip had never built, not once, on any of the 64 places a writer tagged one. The emitted form is the MEASURED plurality, 40 of 53 = 75.5% in the authoring modules (the SSOG span[style]+b and SSCI104 title-inside-the-drop minorities are recorded, not chased). Requires a tagged TITLE and real BODY, so an instruction masquerading as a title declines. Env HINTELEM_OFF.

mtk_quiz._doc:
ROUND 232 (Change Ledger CL-0038, 16 Jul — Chris). Any [MTKquiz]-family marker (any modifiers; the span-level retag in Tag_Lexicon._meta.mtk_quiz_retag does the matching) ends in the canonical button `
Go to quiz
` — href intentionally BLANK, the developer wires the D2L quicklink at publish time (gold's populated quickLink hrefs ARE that publish-time wiring, the CL-0044 class; the href divergence from gold is INTENTIONAL) — plus ONE Designer/Developer To Do note (kind 'todo', red_flag.todo_form, class cv2-note = gate-excluded) carrying the writer's raw quiz spec so the modifier prose ('supports engagement, audio, video, file sharing', 'should go to teacher dropbox' — which does NOT attach a dropbox wrapper) is never silently stripped. Writer quiz content stays rendered (constraint 1): the retag makes the marker an ELEMENT, so it never opens a capturing bundle. ADJACENT WRITER BUTTON ABSORB (the dedup rule — gold ships ONE button per quiz): a writer-typed quiz button in the marker's window — a [button] item labelled per button_label_pattern ('Go to quiz.'/'Quiz' — ARFUN02/ARFUN04/TEFUN02/TEFUN06-08) or a standalone [Go to quiz]-span bundle per marker_span_pattern (HPRE301) — is UPGRADED to the canonical anchored form and the marker's own button suppressed (its To Do note still emits). The window walks window_back/window_forward non-blank items, stopping at another mtk item, an [Activity] opener, or a section/page/closer boundary, so it can never leak across activities; a [go to quiz] span OUTSIDE any mtk window is untouched (the corpus-wide standalone class, ~40 modules, is a recorded follow-up — NOT this rule). A marker-claimed thin bundle (no content members) emits the button INSTEAD of its placeholder box; a fat one keeps its box (content never lost). Population: 33 spans / 21 modules (outputs/_detect_mtkquiz.cjs); 5 of them (SCFUN01, MXFUN02, SSOG103, SSOG301, EXPFUN07) have NO gold button — the rule is forward-looking and outranks gold there (named CHANGE-LEDGER OVERRIDE deltas, never chased). Env MTKQUIZ_OFF reverts the family byte-for-byte.
mtk_quiz.todo_note: Create this quiz in MTK and wire the button's D2L quicklink (the href is intentionally blank). Writer's quiz spec: {spec}

interactive_builders._principle: PRINCIPLE (anchor_compare two-layer test; reference/Principles_Audit_and_Reconciliation.md). Every builder here builds the widget the WRITER's tag specifies. The human developer's finished widget is the reference ONLY where the writer's tag corresponds to the human's element (Decision-Framework B). Where the human editorially SUBSTITUTED a different element (e.g. writer [flip card] -> human accordion; writer [carousel] left as static images), that substitution is NON-derivable (Decision-Framework A1): build the WRITER's tagged widget anyway and judge it on the widget VERIFIER (_verify_*.cjs, divergence/defect 0), NOT on skeleton-vs-the-human's-substitution. A skeleton dip vs a human substitution is the expected, documented cost (rounds 115/116), not a regression. Never half-build: build cleanly or keep the honest placeholder.

modal_sets._note_r292: ROUND 292 — five measured additions, each on its own env toggle. closer_pattern: a modal member whose bracket says close/end is a CLOSER and never opens a pop-out (41 such members corpus-wide; [Close Modal] was opening an empty set and sinking the whole widget — MODALCLOSER_OFF). stray_marker_tags: a content-less marker belonging to a NEIGHBOURING activity ([Tab 2], [trigger engagement]) is skipped like a [button] instead of bailing the walk — MEASURED LOSSLESS, all 26 occurrences sit at the very end of their bundle and carry no text at all (MODALSTRAY_OFF; 26 activities / 6 BLL modules, the joint-largest lever). prose_tags: an [external link] carrying a URL is pop-out CONTENT, not a foreign tag (MODALMEMVOCAB_OFF; 7 activities). opener_leading_numberless: in a NUMBERED bundle a leading text-less numberless marker is the widget's own opener, not pop-out 0 — it was creating a trigger-less first set that sank EXPFUN04/05 (MODALOPENER_OFF). bold_lead_label: a numbered set with no label takes the BOLD LEAD of its first line, the round-278/283/290/291 rule (MODALBOLDLEAD_OFF; CEDT208's four tapa cloths). media_tiles: the writer's lead table of [Insert media item N] references supplies the numbered sets' TRIGGER PICTURES from the Media List the run already parses — EXPFUN04's items 4/5/6 resolve to iStock-1156854907 / iStock-155353286 / iStock-1371047758, the three filenames its human developer used, and the emit is the human's own row of tile columns followed by the pop-outs. EVERY cell must resolve or none does, so a strip is never half pictures and half words (MODALTILES_OFF).
modal_sets._note: ROUND 280 — the general TKmodal set composer, tried LAST after the r216 image-pair form and the r73 document button, so all 88 pre-round builds are byte-identical by construction. Emits the corpus convention (div.button.TKmodalButton + its sibling div.TKmodal) from four delimiters: numbered [Modal N …] sub-tags, the SAME-BLOCK label line, a captured TABLE (one row = one modal), and the tag's own text. The text trigger is DOMINANT in the gold — 213 of 283 TKmodals = 75.3% across 52 modules — while the converter previously had no builder for it at all. min_modals 1 (a lone modal is the gold's plurality); label_max_words 9 is GOLD-BACKED (of 125 gold text triggers 96.8% are <=6 words and 100% <=9), so a longer writer line is not a trigger and the set declines rather than putting a paragraph on a button. A strict label/modal alternation keeps a multiple-choice quiz from becoming a row of buttons. Env MODALSETS_OFF.

modal.note: ROUND 73 (Chris, OSBY201-02 #13). A [modal] whose captured content is a SINGLE document/PDF URL is the human's external-resource BUTTON. The button WORDING is editorial (the WT gives only the URL), so {label} is a derived short writer link-phrase or default_label; the STRUCTURE (the <a><div.button>) is the derivable match. CONSERVATIVE (never half-build): builds ONLY on exactly one URL with no data table / rich members — anything richer keeps the orange placeholder. Env MODALBTN_OFF.

image_pairs.note: ROUND 216 (r214-a; Chris 2026-07-12: build the WRITER'S modal, not gold's flipCard substitution — the _principle rule). Repeating '[modal][image] <iStock URL>' + [body]/black content pairs (OSOH501-01's six ergonomics modals) build the corpus TKmodal convention: img.TKmodalButton trigger directly followed by its div.TKmodal (the CEDK401/ENGI301 sibling-pair form). size is editorial (WT gives none) -> corpus-dominant default_size M (measured 116 M / 81 L / 72 XL / 4 S). NEVER half-builds: non-image modal member, no/non-iStock URL, trigger caption residue, red text, table/nested/foreign member, content before the first trigger, or an EMPTY pair (the BLL image-enlarge dialect) all decline to the r73 path / placeholder. Measured outputs/_measure_modalpairs.cjs (369 modal bundles, all WTs): fires on EXACTLY 1 bundle corpus-wide (OSOH501-1.0 nested, 6 pairs); follow-up dialects recorded (EXPFUN tile-modals, MXDI '[Modal N Image]', BLL image-enlarge no-body). Env MODALIMG_OFF.

ROUND 69 (Chris). selfCheck QUESTION-LIST form (ref HPFUN401): a clean list of NUMBERED question lines -> per question a

+ a free-text

dragAndDrop.note:
ROUND 69 (Chris). dragAndDrop NARROW N:N TEXT-MATCHING form, layout=standard. Input is one 2-column data table [label | answer]; row order is the answer key. Builds the human's questionContainer (one .question per label) + ddContainer (a .drop per row + a .drag per row, option = 1-based row index), answers as

text. CONSERVATIVE: the human's LAYOUT choice (standard/column/FIB/scatter) and image-form alt text are NON-DERIVABLE editorial (NOT in the WT -- measured: bundle.modifier is the writer's freeform remainder, not layout=), so we fire ONLY on the safest sub-shape and keep the placeholder otherwise -- bail unless exactly one table, width 2, >= min_rows rows, every answer DISTINCT plain text (a repeated answer = categorisation, not matching -> bail), and no media / URL / red / extraType. layout defaults to standard. Env DRAGDROP_OFF.

glossary.note:
ROUND 56 (Chris, OSAI201-01). A [glossary] interactive is a flat list of 'Term – Meaning' lines (en/em-dash or spaced hyphen separated). InteractiveBuilder.#glossary parses each captured black line via split_pattern (term = before the first dash, meaning = after) and builds the human's Term/Meaning table:

Glossary

+ with a 'Term'|'Meaning' header (tr.title-g) and one row per entry. The outer row>col-md-8 wrapper is supplied by the body emitter, so only the inner div.glossary (which carries the wavy-border CSS) is built here. Declines (placeholder) if fewer than min_rows dash lines are found. The boundary bank now terminates the glossary at the next heading so a following [H3] is not swallowed.

labelled_pairs._note: ROUND 277 — the LABELLED-PAIR slider: a general composer run LAST, so all 22 pre-round slider builds are byte-identical by construction. ONE rule (a row is a FRONT then a BACK) covers every measured dialect: the front riding the opener, a [back]/[body] tag, a labelled red span, halves named in the bracket, a black bullet. min_rows 1 because 44.7% of the gold's 161 sliders are single-row. Trailing over-captured prose renders AFTER the widget (the r196 rule) so building never loses the writer's words. Env HINTPAIR_OFF.

_comment: hintSlider — a list of click-to-reveal rows. Captured as ONE 2-column table:
column 1 = the visible hint (front), column 2 = the reveal (back).
A leading 'hint | slide' (or 'front | back') header row is auto-skipped.
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI201 (hintCssFile="standard").
hintSlider._header_note: A first table row is treated as a column-label header (and dropped) when it is the writer's red instruction text, OR when every cell is one of these label words. Add words here if a writer uses different column labels.

panel_delimiters._note: ROUND 278 — the PANEL DELIMITER VOCABULARY, tried LAST after the strict paths and both modes of the r246 rich fallback, so it is strictly additive and the 253 pre-round builds are byte-identical by construction. Panels resolve from an ordered vocabulary, each derivation gold-verified: D1 [accordion N] widened to the word/ordinal spellings, a heading-less panel taking its head from its own first [H2]-[H6]; D2 a captured TABLE, ONE ROW = ONE PANEL (head = a short first cell, else the content cell's BOLD LEAD); D3 a repeating same-level heading; D4 repeating BOLD-LEAD black lines. min_panels 1 for the explicit D1 (56.5% of gold accordions have one panel) but 2 for the inferred D2/D3/D4, so one table row is never guessed into an accordion. Env ACCPANELS_OFF.

member_vocabulary._note: ROUND 289 (Chris — the interactive-coverage chain, round 1 of 8; the WHY_UNBUILT__accordion brief's reason A). THE ACCORDION'S OWN MEMBER VOCABULARY, supplied through the SAME caller-scoped `delims` mechanism tabs (r281), flipCard (r282) and clickDrop (r283) already use — so every other caller is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION and each family here reverses on its own data key. MEASURED FIRST, and the measurement CORRECTED the brief: the brief's ranking counted which item types APPEAR in a failing accordion (its `foreignTags()` lists every non-own tag whether or not the walk places it), not which one actually bails. Replaying the shipped walk's tag dispatch over all 122 reason-A records (0 truncated, 0 unexplained) gives the true FIRST BLOCKER: button 28 / data marker 17 / external link 15 / shape n 13 / table 7 / embed 6, then a tail of other-widget invocations. [body], [video] and [image] — the brief's items 1 and 2, ~118 of its claimed reach — have been placed inside a panel since round 278 and are NEVER blockers; CEDT208, the brief's own headline example, is blocked by its trailing [Button] Go to journal, not by its videos. prose_tags: an [external link]/[website]/[Link], a [Caption]/[label …]/[Insert toolbox item] data marker and an [embed]/[pdf] carrying black content render as panel prose (renderBlock links a bare URL, so the writer's link survives as a link); carrying NONE they surface as a red Writers Note rather than being silently skipped (text_tags_note_when_empty — the r214/r242 never-silently-dropped rule; false for every other caller, so tabs and clickDrop cannot move). note_tags: a bare [table]/[Insert Table] is an asset request for a table, and a [purple coloured box] shape marker is a design instruction — both are notes, never content. head_tags: a [heading] is a sub-heading at head_level. defer_pattern: a mid-sentence hover marker ([definition: horizontal axis] + the rest of the sentence in its trailing text, ENGJ301-4.0) STILL DECLINES — rendering only the trailing text would drop the defined term out of the writer's sentence, and weaving it is the r201 render-stitch which is deliberately switched off inside a widget. 8 members / 6 activities, recorded not shipped. REACH (measured, the same replay): the vocabulary + the go-journal rule clear the member walk on 71 of the 122 reason-A activities across 48 modules; the 51 that remain are dominated by another widget's invocation (~36 — a gathering class, not a builder one) and 10 non-journal buttons. Env ACCMEMBER_OFF.

go_journal_member._note: ROUND 289 — THE GO-TO-JOURNAL BUTTON, the accordion's single biggest blocker (21 of the 122 reason-A activities across 19 modules; 19 of them become fully clear once it is handled). The writer ends the accordion with '[Button] Go to journal' / '[Go to Journal]' and the walk had no role for it. THE SCANNER FENCE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: round 278's button_tail_terminates excludes a go-to-journal button because releasing it into the body stream produced the duplicate Chris reported at round 273 (caught live on HIS1006-12.0), so this rule changes nothing about CAPTURE — the button stays a member and the widget's boundary is untouched. Instead the member is SKIPPED as panel content (the gold puts a button inside a panel in 52 of 3,099 panels = 1.7%, so it does not belong there) and the accordion emits round 239's own templated <h4 class="goJournal"> AFTER the widget, which is where the human puts it. LOSSLESS BY MEASUREMENT, not by assumption: of the 24 currently-declining pages whose accordion carries one, 13 already show an h4.goJournal (round 239's #goJournalTail member branch, which fires for a bundle-owned activity) and 11 do NOT (no activity owns the bundle, so that branch never runs) — so simply skipping the member would have lost the button on 11 pages, and emitting it here covers both. The double-emit is prevented at the other end: the builder sets bundle._goJournalEmitted and #goJournalTail's member branch stands down (buttons.go_journal.member_branch_yields_to_builder). label_match/raw_match are READ FROM buttons.go_journal, never copied, so this rule and round 239's can never drift apart — the round-278 #isGoJournalButton discipline. Env ACCGOJOURNAL_OFF.

lead_before_first_panel._note: ROUND 289 — CONTENT BEFORE THE FIRST PANEL IS THE ACCORDION'S OWN LEAD (the brief's reason E: 11 activities across 8 modules — XDLS904 3, XDLS903 2, and one each in CEDT501, ENG1005, ENG1007, ENGI405, XDLS905, XGF9001). D1 declined outright the moment a substantive part arrived before the first [accordion N] marker, because attaching it to the first panel would put it in the wrong place. The clickDrop reading has rendered exactly this material ABOVE the widget since round 283, in the writer's own place, and this copies that behaviour: the lead parts are returned separately, rendered through the same renderBlock/asset machinery as a panel body, and emitted before <div class="accordion">. Nothing is invented and nothing is lost. GUARDED: only TEXT, IMG, VIDEO, EMBED and HEAD parts may lead (a table or a nested widget before the first panel still declines, since those are the shapes where the writer's intent is genuinely unclear), and a lead that renders to nothing is dropped. Env ACCLEADIN_OFF.

Template the writer types one [accordion N] tag per panel; the text AFTER the tag
on the same line is that panel's HEADING, and the paragraph(s) beneath it are the
panel BODY. The converter groups them into panels in document order.

heading ->

One <div class=accordion> wraps every (accHead + accContent) pair, in order.

than that — any other member ([image]/[video]/[button]/a data table), a panel

accordion._image_note:
Image-bearing accordion panels (OSGM501-02): the panel image renders FIRST inside accContent (img.img-fluid, iStock id -> images/iStock-.jpg, Mode P/D, alt non-derivable -> alt=''), then the body

_comment: ROUND 242 (Dev-Feedback R5, Family C1 — SCCH302's mixtures accordion). An
IMAGE-ARRANGEMENT LAYOUT MARKER: a red span the lexicon resolves to [image]
only EMBEDDED in prose ('[2 images next to each other]', '[insert images side
by side]'), with NO media URL of its own and NO trailing black content. It is
a writer LAYOUT INSTRUCTION about the images that follow, not an image
element — the accordion walks SKIP it as build content and a successful build
surfaces its text as the standard red note after the widget (the r214
instruction-member class; never silently stripped, never a build-breaker).
Both accordion walks previously BAILED the whole widget at this member, so
every output the rule can change was a declined placeholder — containment by
construction. MEASURED (outputs/_detect_r242_accunnum.cjs, all 429 WTs live):
the arrangement vocabulary = 21 occ / 13 modules (+ SCCH302); the un-numbered
repeated-label [accordion] form itself was ALREADY accepted (scanner same-type
absorb + the rich walk's bare-head panel delimiters) — this marker was the
ONLY blocker on the C1 class. Env ACCIMGMARK_OFF reverts (marker bails the
build again, the r241 placeholder state).
image_layout_marker.pattern: (?=[\s\S]*\bimages?\b)(?=[\s\S]*\b(?:side by side|next to each other|beside each other)\b)

head_from_first_line._note: ROUND 246 (Chris, ticket 2 of the basic-interactive builders round) — HEADING-LESS PANEL RECOVERY. A large writer family numbers the panels but puts NO text on the tag itself: '[accordion 1]' alone on its line, then the panel's own first line ('US 29302 (Version 3)') and the rest of the body under it. Every accordion authored that way bailed on the rich fallback's 'each panel needs a heading' rule, so the writer's tagged accordion shipped as a developer hand-off box. CHRIS'S DIRECTIVE (2026-08-03, the Decision Framework's A1 branch): 'if the writer has used the accordion tag, then I want you to attempt to generate an accordion despite what the human generated html files generate this as (since keep in mind they may have initially generated an accordion to start with, but after liaising with the writer of the module, they may have then changed the interactive)'. Measured for the record (outputs/_measure_r246_gold.py over 331 paired no-table declines): the gold ships an accordion at 156, another element at 102 and drops the text at 73 — which is why this build is judged on the accordion VERIFIER and the writer's tag, not on matching the human's substitution (Decision_Framework_Human_vs_Claude.md, GATE PRECEDENCE). THE RULE: a panel with no heading takes it from its OWN first text line, and that line is REMOVED from the body so it is never shown twice. Guarded — the donor part must be TEXT (never an image/video/nested part), must have at least one more line after the heading (a single-line part IS the body, not a title), the line must be at most max_words long and carry no red writer instruction, and a panel left with no body still bails. env ACCNOTBL_OFF reverts to the round-245 behaviour (the whole accordion falls back to the hand-off box).

_comment: ROUND 95 (Chris, OSAI501-03): the RICH-accordion FALLBACK. The two strict
paths above (#accordionTextOnly / #accordionWithImages) BAIL the WHOLE
accordion the moment a panel body is richer than heading + iStock image +
plain paragraphs. The human, however, routinely builds panels that ALSO
carry a [video] (YouTube), a BULLET list, and — in 5 corpus pages — a NESTED
shapeHover (OSAI501-03 'When AI is not appropriate'). This fallback fires
ONLY when the strict paths returned null, so every accordion that already
builds is BYTE-IDENTICAL (proven by ACCRICH_OFF). It groups members into
panels exactly like #accordionWithImages, then renders each panel body in
document order: [image]->img (iStock, reusing #assetImage), [video]->the
shared video.youtube embed, black/[body] text->renderBlock (the converter's
own #renderBlackText so bullets become <ul><li> identically to the rest of
the page), a NESTED sub-bundle marker->renderNested (the converter's honest
cv2-interactive placeholder). Conservative — still NULL (whole accordion ->
placeholder, never half-built) on: a data table, a non-iStock image, a
video with no resolvable id, a panel with no heading or no rendered body,
red writer-instruction text, or a member it cannot place. env ACCRICH_OFF.
rich_panels.nested_placeholder_note: The nested sub-bundle is rendered via the converter's renderNested callback (#interactivePlaceholder), so it carries class=cv2-interactive (gate-excluded per round 72) and gets its own data-cv2-index + manifest entry.
rich_panels._r214_note: ROUND 214 (Chris, OSOH501-01): sub_headings — a panel's own [H2]-[H6] renders faithfully inside accContent (panel 4's [H5] Manaaki/Tika/Whanaungatanga); skip_instruction_members — a writer CS/Dev note inside a panel no longer bails the build (it still surfaces as the standard red cv2-note after the built widget via bundle.instructions); skip_list_marker_lines — a docx numbered-list artifact line ('1.') renders nothing; nested_built_wrap — a nested sub-bundle that BUILT for real (the READYSAFE tabs) wraps in the human's in-panel row. env ACCRICH2_OFF reverts all four.

_note: ROUND 275 (Chris — 'the accordion builder gives up whenever the content is in a table:
190 failures, no successes'). A captured data TABLE inside an accordion panel is ordinary
panel CONTENT, and the human ships it exactly that way: measured over the whole gold
library, 325 accContent blocks across 99 modules contain a <table> (byte reference

EXPFUN02_0.0's 'Success Criteria Phase Two' panel —

lead

then the kept table).
The rich panel walk renders it through the converter's OWN kept-table emitter
(renderTable = TablesAndGrids.contentTable), so a panel table is identical to any
free-body table on the page — the same seam the rich TABS pane has used since round 195.
Before this rule all three accordion walks mishandled it: #accordionRich and
#accordionTextOnly bailed the whole widget at their catch-all, and #accordionWithImages
SILENTLY DROPPED it (a table item carries no .text, so it fell through the blank-line
guard and the accordion built with the writer's table missing) — a content-loss bug
repaired in the same round.
MEASURED (outputs/_measure_r275_blockers.cjs, all 449 corpus modules live): 190 accordion
declines carry a table; 85 of them already have a panel HEADING and are what this rule
reaches. RECORDED, NOT SHIPPED: the 105 BARE-OPENER bundles where the writer gave no
panel heading at all and the table's own ROWS are the panels — a different builder (the
accordion sibling of tabs' rich_panes.table_panes), spread over ~50 distinct table shapes
whose panel headings are frequently editorial and absent from the Writers Template
(ENFUN04's gold invents 'Step one/two/three'), so it needs its own measured round rather
than an invented heading.
NEVER HALF-BUILDS: no renderTable callback, no open panel, or an emitter returning nothing
all keep the honest hand-off box. env ACCTABLE_OFF reverts the whole rule (including the
#accordionWithImages silent drop, restored byte-for-byte).

rich._note: ROUND 276 — the RICH GENERAL COMPOSER, run LAST so the four existing branches keep their populations byte-for-byte (a fallback cannot break what already works). Flattens members AND every table cell into an ordered stream of PARTS and emits ONE `row speechBubble` per bubble, in the gold-measured plurality forms (1,218 gold rows / 143 modules: one bubble per row 80.4%, avatar rows layout=speech 97.6% + bubble-right 58.6%, image-less col-12 + bubble-basic bubble-top). Never half-builds: a foreign element with its own content, a captured non-bubble table, an un-nameable image, or a bubble with no text all decline. Env SBRICH_OFF.

_comment: speechBubble — a character image beside a STATIC speech/thought bubble of text.
CAPTURED AS: exactly ONE 1x2 table (one row, two cells) PLUS exactly one image URL in
the bundle's media. One cell is the writer's [image] tag + its iStock URL; the other is
the [speech bubble] tag + the bubble text. The cell ORDER decides which side the bubble is:
text cell first, image cell second  ->  bubble-LEFT  (text on the left, image on the right)
image cell first, text cell second  ->  bubble-RIGHT (image on the left, text on the right)
BUILT ONLY for the clean, single, STATIC (no-hover) bubble. The WHOLE widget falls back to
the orange placeholder (never half-built) the moment the capture is richer than that: a
'layout'/conversation modifier, 2+ images or 2+ rows/columns, a video URL instead of an
image, a non-iStock image we cannot name, a 'flipside'/front-back reveal, or ANY extra red
developer-instruction text in either cell (e.g. a 'CS: ...' note). Those stay visible flags,
faithful to the source — we never guess.
IMAGE honours the run's image Mode P/D exactly like every other image: Mode P shows a
placeholder + the commented-out real reference; Mode D emits the real . The iStock id
(the digits after 'gm' in the URL) becomes images/iStock-<id>.jpg, mirroring Emit_Templates.image.
Human reference (verbatim shape): 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI201/OSAI201-01.html (Aria, bubble-left).
TO RESTYLE (col widths, classes, the layout attribute) edit the strings below — no code change.
{text} = the bubble text; {image} = the rendered image; {layout} = layout_attr; {filename}/{label} = image slots.
speechBubble.image_only_media_note: ROUND 116 (Chris, OSAH501-03). The bubble TEXT may carry its OWN hyperlinks ([LINK: mailto:…]/[LINK: https://…]) which #harvestMedia collects into bundle.media alongside the one iStock image. Count the iStock IMAGES (the entries #istockFilename names) and require EXACTLY ONE; still bail on a video or a 2nd image. The non-image link URLs are the bubble's own links (the Lawdog Netsafe bullets). env SBLINKMEDIA_OFF reverts to the strict media.length===1 guard.

no_table_image._note:
R247 sibling: the IMAGE-LESS form lives in text_only below. ROUND 246 (Chris, ticket 1 of the basic-interactive builders round) — THE NO-TABLE AVATAR+BUBBLE FORM. The long-standing static speechBubble branch only recognises the writer's TABLE dialect (exactly one 1x2 table, image cell + text cell). A large family of writers instead types the whole thing as ONE PARAGRAPH: '[Image] avatar Tina smiling [LINK: https://…gm…] [speech bubble] RHS '. That has no table, so the bubble fell to the developer hand-off box while its avatar rendered loose above it. The scanner's same_block_image_absorb (Interactive_Boundary_ChildTag_Bank._meta.member_rule) recovers the paragraph-mate [image]; this template block is the shape the branch emits. MEASURED: the class is EXACTLY 55 bundles across TEDC401/TEDC402/SSCI104 and the human gold builds an avatar+bubble row at 55 of 55; within those golds the dominant column pair is 'col-md-2 offset-md-0 col-12 paddingR' | 'col-md-6 col-6' (118 of 147 speechBubble rows in the two TEDC modules) with class 'bubble-basic no-hover bubble-{side}' (55/55) inside 'row speechBubble' (55/55) and a single

(53/55). SIDE comes from the writer's ORDER exactly as the table branch derives it from cell order — image first (all 55) => the image column leads and the bubble is bubble-right, which matches the gold on 53 of 55 (the 2 lefts are editorial one-offs, the round-123 single-deviation class). The writer's own side WORD is deliberately NOT read: it is present on only 7 of the 55 and it is WRONG where it disagrees (TEDC401 #5 says 'RHS' where the gold ships bubble-left). env SBNOTBL_OFF reverts the whole ticket.
