ROUND 247 (Chris, ENGS404-00 '[insert thought bubble]') — THE TEXT-ONLY BUBBLE(S). A bubble the writer authors with NO character image and NO table ('[insert thought bubble] Where do we find stories? [insert thought bubble] Why are stories important?') had no builder branch at all — the r246 recorded image-less decline class, now built on Chris's directive that ALL basic interactives build (the A1 writer's-tag branch). MEASURED (outputs/_detect_r247.cjs, ALL corpus dirs): 229 bundles / 52 modules, 212 clean; the human library itself ships the text-only bubble form 385 times, and layout="thought" exists in the gold precisely for the thought wording (365 occ / 152 pages, XDLS901 the reference). Emit shape = the measured plurality (col-12; bubble-basic no-hover bubble-top — the side/colour scatter across the 385 is editorial C, this class string is the one data knob). One row per INTERACTIVE invocation member (the same-type merged '[thought bubble] … [thought bubble] …' paragraph ships one bubble each); >1

takes the r104 wrapper

; layout follows the writer's own word via thought_re. Never-half-build guards in InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubbleTextOnly. env SBTEXT_OFF reverts the whole branch.

conversation._note: CONVERSATION layout (round 48): the writer authors '[speech bubble] Conversation layout' + alternating Prompt/AI-response BLACK lines (each line a turn). The human renders div.row.speechBubble > col-md-12 > alternating div.bubble-right.no-hover (the user/prompt turn) / div.bubble-left.secondary.no-hover (the AI response). InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubbleConversation builds it from the bundle's black members: STRICT alternation starting RIGHT (matches the human's turn-taking; OSAI401-01 conv #1 Prompt1/resp/Prompt2/resp/Prompt3/resp and conv #2 Prompt4 + 'Click to see its response'), with a content override (a line starting with a response_prefix forces left, a prompt_prefix forces right). Conservative: builds ONLY when the bundle is a clean black-line conversation (modifier mentions 'conversation' OR >=min_turns lines start Prompt/AI response) with NO table and NO face/reveal members; anything richer keeps the placeholder. 5 modules use this form (ENGC401, ENGS401, OSAI401, OSBY301, OSBY401).

speechBubble._droppable_span_note: Red spans in a bubble cell whose content STARTS WITH one of these (at a word boundary) are DROPPED before the build, keeping the surrounding learner text — so a clean bubble is not blocked by a developer's 'CS: …' manual-edit instruction (OSAI201 #1 'CS: can a cross be put through the brain image') or a 'flipside:' reveal LABEL (OSAI201 #8 — the bubble text after it is the second part, rendered via the ' / ' multi-paragraph path). The widget's own [image]/[speech bubble] tag span is kept; any OTHER unrecognised 2nd red span still bails (conservative). Read by InteractiveBuilder.#stripDevSpans.
speechBubble._paragraph_note:
The writer's ' / ' inside a bubble is a PARAGRAPH break when every part is sentence/paragraph-like — at least paragraph_min_words words AND containing ending punctuation (.!?); then the parts render as multiple

(OSAI501-02 #7's GenAI bubble). A ' / ' list of SHORT labels (or any bulleted/numbered bubble — OSBY301's kaitiakitanga list) is left as the honest placeholder. Lower this only if a genuine multi-paragraph bubble has unusually short paragraphs.

cell_face_split._note: ROUND 290 — T0, ONE CARD PER CELL with the faces marked INSIDE it. Measured 24 activities / 16 modules: each cell is a whole card (ENGR102-3.0 '[H4] ai / [Image] Paint / [Body] paint / Back Try reading these words…', XGF9004-17.0 '[Front] … / [Back] …', CEDW501-5.0 '**Physical impacts** / [Reverse] …'). EVERY non-empty cell must split into a non-empty front and a non-empty back, so a table where only some cells carry a marker is a different shape and keeps its box. The marker may be a red span, a plain bracket, or the bare word, and may carry structural CO-TAGS ('[Back] [H3]') which are dropped. Env FLIPCELLFACES_OFF.

bold_lead_faces._note: ROUND 290 — the BOLD-LEAD front/back split, modelled byte-for-byte on TWHK901-0.0's human build: the bold opening phrase becomes the front <h5> with its colon dropped, and the WHOLE caption stays on the back unchanged. Fires ONLY when every resolved card has an EMPTY front and a bold-lead back, which is what makes it safe — a table where only some rows have a bold lead is a different shape and keeps its box. Measured 10 activities / 4 modules (TWHK901, AGH1006 x4, AGH1009, CEDK101). Env FLIPBOLDLEAD_OFF.

header_roles._note: ROUND 290 — a first row whose every non-empty cell NAMES a role ('Image | Title | Explanation', CEDO102-0.0) maps the remaining rows: one card per row, the Image cell the front picture, the Title cell the front heading and the Explanation cell the back. repeat_title_on_back follows CEDO102's own gold, which repeats the title as the back's heading. A role name must be the WHOLE cell, so a real card row can never be mistaken for a header. Also DROPS a role header the composer would otherwise read as a card (TWHK901's 'Images | Captions'). Env FLIPHEADROW_OFF.

general_cards._note: ROUND 282 — the general CARD composer, tried LAST so all 49 pre-round builds are byte-identical by construction. Cards resolve from an ordered delimiter vocabulary: T1 face-marker ROWS that repeat; T1b a face-marker COLUMN; T1c per-cell face markers riding with the content; T2 a TWO-ROW table with no markers, one card per COLUMN; T3 N x 2 rows; M1/M2 [Flip Card N] / [front]/[back] tags with a TEXT-ONLY front allowed; M3 face LABEL WORDS; M4 a bare MEDIA SERIES. A COMPLETED BACK ENDS A CARD, and content arriving while the FRONT is open is FRONT content. GOLD-BACKED: text-only cards are 43% of the library (a front is a HEADING alone 22.3% / a PARAGRAPH alone 20.7%), so an image is never required; min_cards 1 for an explicit delimiter but 2 for an inferred one; NO length cap on a front (a gold front runs past ten words 4.3% of the time); a label is NEVER invented. Env FLIPCARDS_OFF.

_comment: flipCard — a grid of cards, each a FRONT that flips to reveal a BACK.
CAPTURED AS: one 2-column table — column 1 is every card's FRONT, column 2 its BACK.
A leading column-label row (e.g. 'Image for one side | Text for flipped side', 'Front | Back')
is dropped (it matches the header keywords below, or is the writer's red instruction text).
Each CELL is rendered to one of two things:
• an IMAGE — when the cell carries an image reference (an iStock/.jpg URL, a [LINK: ...] to a
photo, or an [image] tag). It is emitted exactly like every other image, honouring Mode P/D
(Mode P = placeholder + commented real reference; Mode D = the real ).
• plain TEXT — the cell's black learner text (the writer's red label tags like [Front of card]/
[H4]/[Body] never reach the page). The writer's ' / ' (a slash with spaces) is the writer's

line-break and becomes
; **bold**/*italic* render normally.
BUILT ONLY when every cell is cleanly one of those two. The WHOLE widget falls back to the orange
placeholder (never half-built) if a TEXT cell still carries red developer-instruction text (a 'CS:'
note or an instruction we cannot safely drop — e.g. ENGI202's [Front of flip card] labelled cards),
if a cell is empty, has bullets, or the capture is wider than two columns / more than one table.
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/CEDO202 (text|image) and ENGJ302 (image|text).
{front}/{back} = the rendered cell; {text}/{filename}/{label} = the slots. Edit the strings to restyle.

general_panes._note_r293b_dupehead: ROUND 293b — a sub-heading repeating the panel's OWN title is a duplicate, not content (the accordion's `panel_delimiters.drop_duplicate_head`, env ACCDUPEHEAD_OFF, implemented in #accResolvePanels). Recorded here only as a pointer; the flag lives on the accordion. general_panes._note_r293: ROUND 293 measured the 79 declines against the SHIPPED dispatch and found the seven brief reasons collapse to THREE terminal causes, all in #tabsPanes — the brief's reasons B and F name #tabsRich, whose refusal has fallen through since round 281 and decides nothing. Gold re-measured over 317 body groups / 141 modules: labels <=6 words 99.15%, <=7 100%, PLAIN 1055/1055; a pane holds a picture 47% of the time and a video 14%; ZERO one-pane groups. The five rules below are each gold-verified on a page whose human build ships the same labels.

marker_bracket._note: R293 FIX 1 — A [Tab N] BRACKET RIDING ON ANOTHER TAG. Writers put the pane marker in the SAME red span as the thing that opens the pane: '[Tab 1] [H3] Read about it' (XGF9006-6.0), '[Tab 1] [H2] Building the basics' (XGF9003-0.0), '[Tab 1 - Maori] [Video 1]' (CEDW101-0.0). The span's PRIMARY tag is then h3/h2/video, so the delimiter test — which only looks when the primary is already 'tab n' — never saw it. This is round 291's delimiter_multi_bracket transposed: every bracket of the span is offered to the pattern in turn. GOLD: XGF9006 3/3 and XGF9003 3/3 exact, CEDW101 5 of its 6. The member's own content then becomes that pane's first content, so nothing is displaced.
marker_bracket._note_deny: A NAME IS NOT A TAG WORD. HPFUN301-0.0 writes '[Tab 1 - H3] How to stay confident' — the 'H3' is the writer telling the designer the HEADING LEVEL to use, not the tab's name, and reading it as the label shipped three tabs all called 'H3' over a build that was already correct. Caught by hashing every page of every tabs module in both toggle states (the round-292 byte-level check), not by the build census, which saw no change in the COUNT. When the captured label is a structural tag word the marker is treated as having no label, and the pane takes its name from its own first sub-heading exactly as before.

cell_inner_tags._note: R293 FIX 2 — A TABLE CELL CARRIES ITS OWN NAMING MARKER. The writer lays the whole set out as one table and tags each cell from the inside: '[Tab 1] Video / [insert video] …' (XMES103-3.0), '[H3] **File systems, folders and metadata**' over '[Body] …' (TEDC402-4.0), '[tab title: Level 1] …' (TEDC401-4.0). Round 291's T0 clickDrop reading transposed. GOLD: XMES103 2/2 and TEDC402 3/3 exact. A column whose header cell names no pane AND whose content cells are empty is not a pane and is dropped (TEDC402's [RHS] avatar column, which its gold also omits); a column that names a pane but has nothing behind it declines the whole build, per never-half-build.

marker_row._note: R293 FIX 3 — A WHOLLY-RED ROW IS EITHER A ROLE ROW OR THE LABEL ROW. Round 281 rightly refused a wholly-red row, because a flipCard table is laid out as entirely-red [front]/[drop] rows over the card faces — but OSAI201-3.0 IS that shape and its human developer built TABS from it, taking the four labels from the row BENEATH the 'front' marker row. So: a wholly-red row whose cells reduce to a ROLE WORD names the row beneath it (label row, then content rows); a wholly-red row whose cells reduce to real, distinct, short TEXT is the label row itself (TEDC401-1.0's 'Tab 1: Step 1'). Anything else still declines. GOLD: OSAI201 4/4 and TEDC401-1.0 4/4 exact.

label_prefix_strip._note: R293 FIX 4 — THE 'Tab N' PREFIX ON A LABEL CELL (the brief's #1-ranked change). The writer numbers the label so its order cannot be mistaken — 'Tab 1: Step 1' — and the human ships 'Step 1'. MEASURED REACH ON THE DECLINES: ONE activity, not the '8+ of 39, half of them in two modules' the brief claims; TEDC402's four are the cell_inner_tags shape above. The separator is OPTIONAL because the writer often leaves it out: OSSC401-3.0 writes a red '[Tab 1]' marker then black 'Ari's story', which the round-281 reading concatenated into the label 'Tab 1 Ari's story' while its gold ships 'Ari's story'. That is an EXISTING build corrected toward the gold, 4/4, and it is named in the round's changelog rather than hidden. A bare 'Tab 1' with nothing after it never matches, so a label cannot be emptied.

opener_label._note: R293 FIX 5 — THE OPENER REPEATS AND CARRIES THE LABEL. PHE1007-1.0 writes '[Tabs – tab one] Skeletal muscle', '[Tabs – tab two] Smooth muscle', '[Tabs – tab three] Cardiac muscle'. The opener tag is skipped as carrying no content of its own, so the label went with it. When the OPENER tag repeats with an ordinal or number in its bracket AND its own trailing text, each occurrence opens a pane named by that text. GOLD: PHE1007 3/3 exact.

lead_before_first_pane._note: R293 FIX 6 — CONTENT BEFORE THE FIRST DELIMITER IS THE WIDGET'S OWN LEAD, rendered above the tabs in the writer's place rather than disqualifying the whole reading. The rounds 283 (clickDrop) and 289 (accordion) rule, which tabs never got: the table reading demanded that EVERY other part be plain text, so a single [H3] riding along with the table refused the widget outright — which is what really blocks TEDC401-1.0, the brief's own headline example, before its 'Tab N:' prefix is ever reached. Only a heading or plain text may lead; anything richer still means the walk swept a section in.

_note: ROUND 275 (Chris — 'the carousel builder gives up whenever the writer included a video
link: sixty failures, no successes'). MEASURED first over all 449 corpus modules live
(outputs/_measure_r275_blockers.cjs): 194 carousel declines carry a [video]/[embed]
member and 125 of them carry NO other blocker at all. The dominant dialect is the BLL
phonics video list — the writer puts the video's TITLE on the [video] tag and the bare
URL on the FOLLOWING line, but colours that line RED, so it reaches the builder as a tag
member with no primary rather than the plain `black` line the round-247 lookahead was
written for. The URL was therefore never found, the video resolved no id, and the WHOLE
carousel bailed to a hand-off box.
follow_any_member: the recovery walks forward up to follow_window members of ANY type,
skipping blank filler, and takes the first line that IS a video URL (a line with prose
of its own is not a reference line and stops the walk). It stops at the first member
carrying a real primary tag, so a URL belonging to a different element can never be
stolen, and at a table/nested member. Reachable ONLY for a [video] with no URL of its
own — every such bundle declines today — so the rule is strictly ADDITIVE and cannot
change a carousel that already builds.
other_hosts: a URL the YouTube-id regex cannot read no longer bails the whole carousel.
A YouTube SHORTS url ships the round-266 media_table.shorts_embed 1x1 form (gold 57/57)
and any other embeddable url ships video.generic_iframe — mirroring exactly what the
free-body media emitter (MediaBuilder.media) already does for the same URL, so a video
inside a carousel and the same video in the body render by one convention.
drop_bare_url_lines: a slide line that is NOTHING BUT a bare video URL is that video's
REFERENCE, not learner prose — MEASURED: the gold library ships 1,618 carousel captions
and NOT ONE of them is a bare URL, the same convention MediaBuilder applies on the body
path (round 80, stripMediaResidue). Without it every URL line the tail lookahead did not
claim rendered as a visible link paragraph on the slide.
deny_extensions keeps the recovery from adopting a PDF/document/image/audio link as a
'video' (the [embed story] decodable-PDF family, 58 declines, is a DIFFERENT class and
is RECORDED not shipped: its slides are story pages that exist in no input).
env CARVIDEO_OFF reverts both halves; CARVIDTAIL_OFF still reverts the whole r247
lookahead including its original black-line form.

media_series._note: ROUND 247 (Chris, ENGS404) — the MEDIA-SERIES refinements. media_opens_slide (env CARMEDSLIDE_OFF): in a bundle with NO [Slide N] markers, each image/video member OPENS its own slide — the writer's back-to-back media list is one slide per item ('[image 1]..[image 4]' = 4 slides; 2 [video]s = 2 slides, which previously piled into ONE slide and failed min_slides); a heading/prose-opened slide still receives its FIRST media item, so the heading+image dialect is byte-unchanged. video_tail_url (env CARVIDTAIL_OFF): a [video]/[insert video] member with no URL of its own takes it from the immediately-following black link/title line (the r240 D2 title-anchored class inside a widget — MEASURED 137 members / 38 modules corpus-wide, NONE currently building, outputs/_detect_r247.cjs); the line is consumed as that video's reference. Pairs with the scanner's member_rule.media_series_break (env CARSERIES_OFF), which stops the run's capture at the first following non-media element.

rich_slides._note: ROUND 246 (Chris, ticket 3 of the basic-interactive builders round) — THE RICH SLIDE FALLBACK, the carousel's sibling of the round-214 rich_panels accordion fallback. CHRIS'S DIRECTIVE (2026-08-03, the Decision Framework's A1 branch): 'if the writer has specified a carousel, the best thing is to generate a carousel' — the human developer's finished page may show an accordion or plain body instead, but that substitution follows unrecorded verbal feedback after v1 was handed over, so it is NOT the target; the writer's tag is. Measured for the record (outputs/_measure_r246_gold.py over 554 paired no-table declines): the gold ships a carousel at 65, something else at 287 (134 of them accordions) and drops the text entirely at 202 — which is exactly why the build is judged on the carousel VERIFIER and the writer's tag, not on the human-match gates (Decision_Framework_Human_vs_Claude.md, GATE PRECEDENCE). The three existing branches each recognise ONE authoring dialect — a captured image/caption TABLE, image slides that ALL carry both an image and a caption, or a member run of BARE video URLs — and bail wholesale on anything else, which is why only 36 of 794 captured carousels built. This fallback runs LAST (every already-building carousel is byte-identical) and composes slides in document order from whatever the writer actually supplied: a [Slide N] marker or a heading opens a slide, and a slide may hold any mix of heading, iStock image, YouTube video and prose. NEVER HALF-BUILDS — it returns null (keeping the honest hand-off box) on a captured data table, an extra merged widget type, a nested sub-bundle, red writer-instruction text inside slide content, a non-derivable image or video URL, a member tag it does not recognise, an empty slide, or fewer than min_slides / more than max_slides slides. env CARNOTBL_OFF reverts to the round-245 behaviour.

general_items._note: ROUND 283 — the general ITEM composer, tried LAST so all 61 pre-round builds are byte-identical by construction. Items resolve from an ordered delimiter vocabulary: D1 labelled [click drop N] tags over the full member vocabulary; D2 a captured TABLE read five ways (T0 self-delimited CELLS, T1 a face-marker COLUMN, T2/T3 a peeled header then N x 2 rows, T4 one item per COLUMN, T5 one item per CELL); D3 a repeating same-level HEADING run. Two general rules carry it: content before the first button is the widget's own LEAD prose, rendered above the widget in the writer's place rather than thrown away, and a run of media immediately before a delimiter belongs to the item it opens. GOLD-BACKED (1,199 groups / 211 modules / 3,036 buttons): min_items 1 for an explicit delimiter (a one-item clickDrop is the gold's plurality at 43.5%) but min_inferred_items 2; label_max_words 8 (<=3 words 83.7%, <=8 99.2%); a label is NEVER invented, a bare URL is never a label, and a panel with no visible text is a half-build. Env CLICKDROPS_OFF.

dropDown — a select-the-answer quiz. ROUND 287 (Chris): the FIRST builder this
widget has ever had; before it, all 390 captured dropDown bundles declined at
Build's own missing-template guard, because there was no `dropDown` key here and
no case in the dispatch.
THE FAMILY FENCE (`opener_pattern` / `opener_deny_pattern`). Tag_Lexicon aliases
`dropbox`/`drop box` onto this same widget type, but a DROPBOX is the file-upload
area where a student submits a photo, a video or an audio recording — not a
dropdown at all. Measured over every Writers Template: 240 of the 393 captured
bundles are dropbox (87 modules) and 142 are a genuine dropdown (82 modules); the
human ships `class="activity dropbox"` (an activity MODIFIER) for the former and
`div.dropDown` for the latter. The builder therefore fires only where the writer's
own opener names a dropdown, so every dropbox bundle is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION.
Re-cutting the lexicon alias is a round of its own (it would move 240 bundles'
capture and hand-off labels across 87 modules) and is recorded, not done here.
THE ANSWER SIGNAL. The writer marks the correct option either by colouring it RED
or with an explicit [correct] tag placed immediately before it. Both reduce to a
MARK at a character position, so one derivation serves both. A dropdown whose
answer is not marked at all is NEVER guessed — it keeps its hand-off box.
OUTPUT SHAPE — measured over the human library (1877 dropDown units / 138
modules, body-scoped): answer="N" 1-based on 96.5% (multi-select 49, absent 17);
on 100%, reading 'Select one' on 96.9%; 2 options 441 /
3 options 952 / 4 options 285 (so min_options 2, and ≤10 covers 99.6%); the
container is div.dropQuiz (201) or div.dropQuiz autoCheck (105) whose first child
is div.row (111) or, in the paragraph form, div.dropParaContainer (79); the
question wrapper is a bare div.dropQuestion (795, the plurality — the Bootstrap
width variants are editorial and are not reproduced).
dropDown._r294_note: ROUND 294 (Chris): cell_parens — the round-287 D1 paragraph reading applied to a table CELL, one question per cell, emitting the SAME paragraph form the human ships for exactly these tables (MXFL302_05.1, BLL275_1_0, BLLR201_2_0 match it cell for cell). cell_correct_pattern names the explicit [correct]-family bracket inside a cell; note it has NO leading \b, because the writers type [Q1Correct] and \b does not fire between a digit and a letter. thousands_guard — a comma with digits IMMEDIATELY on both sides is a thousands separator, not an option break ('(1,400 km, 1,500 km)' is two options, not four); the discriminator is the absent space, so a real option break written ', ' is untouched. env DDCELLPARENS_OFF / DDNUMCOMMA_OFF.

level_attr_map._rule: Any other registry value renders as level="{value}".

template_attr_map._rule: template_phase registry value → template attribute, normalised via this map. Compound phase bands (e.g. '9-10/NCEA') map to the single template the human ships: the iDoc host (idoc_scripts.js) loads the stylesheet by this attribute, so an unmapped compound value renders the page UNSTYLED. '9-10/NCEA' → 'NCEA' is grounded on the human gold for all 3 modules carrying it (CEDK501, ENGS401, OSAH501).

template_phase_presets._doc: ROUND 221 (Chris, ENGJ403). THE TEMPLATE-ATTRIBUTE PRESET RULE: the <html template="…"> attribute must follow the preset module-LEVEL rule (code level digit 1→1-3, 2→4-6, 3→7-8, 4→9-10, 5→NCEA) and this rule SUPERSEDES sibling inheritance for THIS attribute only — ENGJ403 inherited template="4-6" from series sibling ENGJ402, whose own gold value is itself wrong (the human ENGJ403 ships 9-10). Everything else (menu conventions, groupKey, page model, chips…) keeps the sibling-emulation rule: rules.template_phase is NOT changed, only the emitted attribute. MEASURED over all 305 3-digit level-coded golds (232 already follow the preset): 'subjects' lists the families that solidly follow it (share ≥0.80, the r178 STRONG_SHARE floor) + ENGJ (Chris's named inherited-error chain); families whose code digit is NOT a curriculum level (BLL phonics series, HPFUN/fundamentals combo, the OS short-course numbering, XMES, MXEO, CEDK, OSGM, OSOH, OSSC) are EXCLUDED; 4-digit NCEA codes and FUN 2-digit codes never match code_pattern; a resolved 'combo' value is preserved (a combined-cohort template decision, not a level band — protects ENGJ201). Named preset-over-gold deltas at ship time: ENGJ301/302 4-6→7-8, ENGJ402 4-6→9-10, ENGS401 NCEA→9-10, CEDR401 7-8→9-10, MXFU201 7-8→4-6 (the lone within-family deviants = the same inherited/incorrect class per Chris's directive). Env TPLPRESET_OFF reverts to the pure sibling value.

unknown_subject_digit_fallback._doc: ROUND 238 (Dev-Feedback R1 Family A — module SCCH302). A subject NOT in the subjects preset list (a brand-new subject) that resolved NO template_phase at all used to ship an EMPTY template attribute — the iDoc host loads the stylesheet by this attribute, so the page rendered unstyled. When phaseForAttr is empty AND the code matches code_pattern AND its subject is unknown, the code's own level digit supplies the band via by_level_digit (SCCH302 → 3 → '7-8', the developer-confirmed value). PURE FALLBACK by construction: any module with a resolved template_phase — including every digit-is-not-a-level family (BLL/HPFUN/…), which all resolve real values — is untouched; a code not matching code_pattern (FUN-shaped, 4-digit) still ships empty because the FUN families' template values are MEASURED MIXED (10 combo vs 5 NCEA bases) and the rule refuses to guess. prefix_overrides (r224) + cohort_overrides (r231) still outrank it. Env toggle: TPLFALLBACK_OFF.

prefix_overrides._doc: ROUND 224 (Chris, 2026-07-14). EXPLICIT CODE-PREFIX TEMPLATE OVERRIDES — the design team's exception list for families whose code digit is NOT a curriculum level. A module whose code starts with a key here gets that template attribute UNCONDITIONALLY (outranks sibling inheritance AND the by_level_digit preset; preserve_values does not apply — an explicit prefix rule is absolute). LONGEST matching prefix wins; a null value means 'explicitly NO override' (a guard entry). THE BLL200 EXCEPTION: all BLL2xx modules are actually PHASE 1 → template="1-3", NOT the "4-6" their series digit or a mis-built sibling would suggest (5 gold modules — BLL250/261/264/265/275 — carried the wrong 4-6 and were corrected this round). BLLR2xx modules ARE phase 2 and keep "4-6": the BLLR guard entry is belt-and-braces ("BLLR201" cannot startsWith "BLL2" anyway — 4th char R vs 2 — but doc-14's r218 'BLLR is NOT BLL' startswith trap earns the explicit fence). Env TPLPREFIX_OFF reverts all prefix overrides (independent of TPLPRESET_OFF).

cohort_overrides._doc: ROUND 231 (Chris — Change Ledger CL-0033, 14 Jul). THE LANGUAGES COMBO RULE: every page of a Languages-cohort module ships template="combo" on <html> (the sub-type still comes from the <body> class). The prefixes are doc-14 §14.1's six languages × FUN + non-FUN code forms (data/Subject_Global_Parameters.json family '14.1 Languages P1-4' scope.cohort_prefixes — listed here VERBATIM so the engine never reads SGP at runtime; SGP stays shipped-inert, master_enabled:false). UNCONDITIONAL within the cohort: outranks sibling inheritance AND the by_level_digit preset (preserve_values does not apply — the r224 absolute-override semantics); applied AFTER prefix_overrides (no key overlap exists). Kept SEPARATE from prefix_overrides so each fix reverses independently (§2): LANGCOMBO_OFF reverts Languages alone, TPLPREFIX_OFF keeps reverting BLL2 alone. MEASURED round 231: the corpus holds ZERO Languages dirs (431 dir codes, 0 prefix hits, 0 short-prefix collisions — the r218 'BLLR is NOT BLL' startswith trap checked and clear, no non-Languages code starts CHI/FRE/SAM/GER/JAP/SPA), so this ships as an INERT forward-looking guarantee (the r224/r230 zero-blast class) — without it a fresh Languages code would ship the TEDC-style EMPTY attribute (no registry row, no sibling; the r221 pre-fix class — nothing today would ever RESOLVE combo for it). Env LANGCOMBO_OFF. ROUND 248 (Chris, 5 Aug 2026 — the final 20260511_Language_HTML + covering note): prefixes gain CHFUN + JPNFUN, the code forms ACTUALLY in circulation (CHFUN01-07 are live in the corpus and had been falling through to the r245 last_resort_default's combo with a loud warn; JPNFUN05 is named by the designer as the language-05 structural reference). Doc-14's draft spellings CHIFUN/JAPFUN stay in the list for safety; the list remains EXPLICIT full prefixes (the r245 rule — no 2-letter shortenings).
cohort_overrides._prefix_note: ROUND 245 (Chris — the FRNO901 developer test) added "FRNO". doc-14 §14.1 names the languages in three letters (FRE = French), but the module codes actually in circulation use a two-letter language + two-letter strand form (FRNO901 IS French). This stays an EXPLICIT prefix list rather than a two-letter pattern ON PURPOSE: FR/CH/SA/GE/JA/SP collide with nothing in today's 61 corpus subject prefixes (measured round 245) but would silently capture a future GEOG/CHEM-style subject. New real language code forms are added HERE as they appear; anything not listed falls to last_resort_default instead, which is the safe direction.

template_phase_presets._doc_last_resort_default: ROUND 245 (Chris — the FRNO901 developer test, the r238 Family-A class completed). FRNO901 is a brand-new subject: no registry row, no gold sibling, and its code digit 9 is not a curriculum level, so code_pattern never matches and the r238 unknown_subject_digit_fallback correctly declines to guess. Every OTHER universal field resolved fine through the r238 evidence floor (body_class, idoc_host, footer_class, menu types — all correct) but the template attribute shipped EMPTY, and the iDoc host loads the page stylesheet BY that attribute: the page renders unstyled. That is the same Prio-high failure the reference developer reported for SCCH302 at round 238, reached by a different route. THE RULE: after every other template rule has had its say (sibling inheritance → by_level_digit preset → unknown_subject_digit_fallback → prefix_overrides → cohort_overrides), a still-empty attribute takes `value` — a LAST RESORT, never a preference, and by construction unreachable for any module that resolved anything at all. VALUE = "combo" (Chris's decision, round 245): the combined-cohort template is designed to serve mixed levels so it degrades gracefully for an unknown module, it is the doc-14 answer for the Languages cohort this rule most often backstops, and it is the second most common value in the gold library (78 modules; "1-3" is commoner at 179 but is a junior band — a poor guess for an unknown senior module like FRNO901). Chris's framing: a default holds only until the developer builds the first proof, which then becomes the templated reference PageForge inherits from — so the run also carries a loud warn-level note naming the module and the assumed value. MEASURED ZERO-BLAST: not one page of the shipped corpus carries template="" (grep, all 01-Claude_Modules_ + all gold), and the corpus holds zero Languages dirs, so this round changes no existing byte — a pure forward guarantee, the r224/r231 class. Env TPLDEFAULT_OFF reverts to the empty attribute.

module_code_literal_guard._doc: ROUND 194 (Chris — the XFUN01 'XFUN02' chip). The style-anchor registry's free-text overview chip is mined from ONE group member's gold; when that chip was the member's OWN MODULE CODE the literal leaks to every sibling (measured 10 mined groups / 11 live wrong chips: XFUN01→XFUN02, MXFUN02/03→MXFUN01, ENGFUN02→ENGFUN03, XLP01-05→XPL06, XWHA01→XWHA02). A literal matching code_pattern is the convention 'the module's full code' → render run.moduleCode instead. Genuine free-text ('Module', 'Lesson 5') untouched. Gold evidence: every shown gold chip is the module's own code (ENGFUN02, XWHA01/02, XFUN02, MXFUN01); XFUN01's gold chip is commented OUT (content XFUN01); the XLP family golds swap XLP→XPL systematically = recorded non-derivable editorial (the guard fixes the digits, the letters stay LP). #header-scoped → gate-invisible. Env CHIPLIT_OFF.

family_title_default._doc: ROUND 203 (Chris, HPFUN902 — HTMLGen conversion fix 1). When a FUNDAMENTALS overview page renders NO title h1 (the writer left the [Title] payload EMPTY and no title was derivable), fall back to the SUBJECT-FAMILY display name — the general 'empty [Title] -> family default' rule the human developer follows (HPFUN902's WT [Title] is empty and 'Health & Physical Education Fundamentals' appears NOWHERE in the WT; it is the HPFUN subject-family name the human fills in, also on HPFUN301/401/903). MEASURED (outputs/_measure_familytitle.py, all 45 Fundamentals): exactly 4 modules render no title (ARFUN01, HPFUN203, HPFUN902, SSFUN02); of those only HPFUN's empty-title golds use the family name (HPFUN902 correct). HPFUN203's gold 'Maintaining Friendships' is module-specific + NOT in its WT (non-derivable, recorded C — this rule ships it the family name = a matching <h1> node, skeleton-positive, text a defensible generic fallback). ARFUN01's title IS in its WT as '[Insert title H1: ...]' (a 1-occurrence one-off, out of scope); SSFUN02's is non-derivable (C). So the map is scoped to HPFUN only (the one measured family whose empty-title fallback is the family name). Fires ONLY when titles is empty (a filled [Title] like HPFUN101 'About me' is untouched). #header-scoped -> skeleton-visible, gate-neutral to cs/body/defect. Env FAMILYTITLE_OFF.

lesson_title_h1._doc: CL-0042 / ROUND 230 (Chris — the OSSC pair). For the subject code prefixes in 'subjects' (the OSSC short-course family), a LESSON page ships EXACTLY ONE title h1 — its own lesson title (the r143 pre-activity harvest, 'Lesson N:' prefix stripped) — at EVERY level: the module's Te Reo title is never pushed as a second lesson h1, even where the registry's mined h1_count asks for 2 (OSSC3 lesson h1_count IS 2, mined from the OSSC301 gold, which repeats 'Ngā Tāware' on every lesson — the gold PREDATES the rule; that divergence is a recorded intentional override, never chased back in; see Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.cl0042_ossc_lesson_h1). OUTPUT-INERT today (the r224 prefix-override pattern — converts an accident into a guarantee): no OSSC module currently derives a Te Reo title at all (OSSC301's [TITLE BAR] '*OSSC301 Scams* ✅*Ngā Tāware*' never splits — the ✅ boundary is dropped upstream), and the live dual-title lesson emitters are XMES/CEDT/SSFUN only (outputs/_measure_ossc_lesson_h1.py Part B: 35 pages, 0 OSSC) — so the gate changes ZERO pages until the day a future title-split fix would otherwise have silently regressed OSSC. The overview page + the #module-code chip h1 are untouched (overview te-reo goes through the titleBar branch, not this one). Env OSSCH1_OFF reverts to the pre-230 push. lesson_te_reo_suppress._doc: ROUND 241 (Dev-Feedback R4, E2 — SCCH302; the recorded r199 follow-up, dev-confirmed 'delete it'). A LESSON page whose registry h1_count asks for 2 pushes the module's Te Reo title as a second h1 — but ONLY when the lesson has NO distinct title of its own (i.e. its title falls back to / fold-equals the module English title, the XMES102/103 gold form where the module pair repeats on every lesson). When the lesson carries a DISTINCT own title (fold-differs from the module English title), the module Te Reo h1 is SUPPRESSED — the gold form on every measured distinct-title lesson (XMES101 x8, CEDT207 x6, CEDT301 x6 ship ONE h1, the lesson's own; outputs measurement round 241: 35 dual-h1 Claude lesson pages = 25 suppress / 10 keep). Named collateral (recorded, net-positive r164 class): XMES103-01's writer left the placeholder 'Add lesson title' as the lesson title — it counts as distinct, so its Te Reo drops where gold ships the module pair (1 page vs 20 gold-verified fixes). Composes with (never replaces) the r230 lesson_title_h1 OSSC gate. Env toggle: LESSONTEREO_OFF (restores the unconditional push).

title_rules: h1_count drives how many title h1s appear (the #module-code h1 is NOT counted).
Overview: the [TITLE BAR] payload splits on '|' into English | Te Reo titles → one h1 each (count 2). Count 1 = English only; count 3 = an extra subtitle line when the writer provided one, else flag.
Lesson: the lesson's own title from [LESSON n] {title} (corpus practice); falls back to the module title when the writer gave none.
header.tooltip_rule: menu_button_tooltip yes → attribute present; no/none → absent.

title_split.rule: The [TITLE BAR] payload yields the header h1 titles. Chain: (1) strip a leading module-code token (writers often prepend it — OSAI201's payload starts 'OSAI …'); (2) split English|Te Reo on a pipe; else (3) on a line break; else (4) on a run of 2+ spaces (the OSAI201 separator); else (5) the BILINGUAL PARALLEL-PUNCT split below; else one title.
title_split.evidence:
Gold OSAI201-00: payload 'OSAI AI Digital Citizenship Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI' →

AI Digital Citizenship

+

Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI

.
title_split.placeholder_titles_note: A title-bar half equal to one of these (folded) is a writer PLACEHOLDER, not a real title — e.g. 'Te Reo' (literally 'the language') means 'Te Reo translation goes here'. The real translation is NOT in the WT (the human fills it in), so the converter drops the placeholder and emits a red flag instead of shipping it as an <h1>. Verified XGF9001 (WT 'My Inner Compass | Te Reo'; human shipped 'Te Takinga o taku wairua').

placeholder_title_rule.note: ROUND 76 (Chris, OSBY201): a writer who never replaces the template's italic 'MODULE TITLE TE REO' (or 'MODULE TITLE') placeholder has NOT provided that title — the real one is not in the WT, so it must NOT be shipped as an <h1>. extra_placeholders extends placeholder_titles (folded compare); a half matching ANY is DROPPED. all_placeholder_uses_course: when EVERY title-bar half is a placeholder, do NOT restore it — fall back to the front-matter Course as the SINGLE English title and emit NO Te Reo (matching the human, who ships only what's real). For a MIXED bar (one real + one placeholder, e.g. OSGM501 'GAMING SAFELY | MODULE TITLE TE REO'), the real half is kept as the English title and the dropped-placeholder flag stops PageAssembler from mis-promoting it to the Te Reo slot. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_placeholder_title.py): 18 WTs carry a placeholder half — 10 all-placeholder (OSBY101/201, CEDO202, CEDR201/301/302, CEDT201-204), 8 mixed (OSGM501, OSOH101/501, TEFUN02/05, XGF9001/9006, XLP05). The strings 'module title te reo'/'module title'/'te reo' are unambiguous template boilerplate — no real module is titled that, so the discriminator cannot touch a genuine bilingual title. Env TITLEPH_OFF reverts to the round-75 list (['te reo']) + never-zero restore + original Course backup (OSBY201 ships the doubled 'Module title te reo' second title).

title_split.bilingual_marker_split_slash_rule: ROUND 177 (Chris, ENGS401-00). THE ROOT-CAUSE GENERALISATION, not a one-off. The single-char soft separators now live in ONE ordered DATA list (char_separators) that the ONE splitter #bilingualCharSplit iterates — the FIRST that occurs exactly once and yields a macron-guarded bilingual pair wins. BEFORE this, the slash '/' was recognised only DEFENSIVELY (#titleHasOtherSep + #bilingualDashSplit BAIL when a slash is present) but NO splitter ever ACTED on it, so a slash-separated bilingual [TITLE BAR] ('Responding to Texts / Te whakautu i ngā kuputuhi') fell through to a single combined <h1> while the human ships two. Adding a future single-char title separator is now a DATA edit here — the defensive-vs-offensive asymmetry that caused this class cannot recur. Each entry: sep + its data on/off flag + its env A/B toggle + optional bail_other_sep (colon keeps its round-168 'any other separator ⇒ not mine' bail; slash deliberately does NOT set it, so ENGI201 'Connections – … / Nga Hononga – …' with internal spaced dashes still splits on the top-level slash). Slash is ordered first (outranks colon). MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_title_separators.py): slash splits 8 modules (ENGS401/CEDK101/ANZH203/ENGI201/MXFL202/MXFL301/SSFUN05/SSFUN08), 0 false-splits (the shared round-86 macron guard #bilingualTwoLangGuard never fires on a title the human keeps as one <h1>), and folding colon into the list is byte-identical (0 modules carry both '/' and ':'; the 3 colon+spaced-dash titles TWHA903/XMES102/XMES201 resolve to single either way via the boilerplate/macron guard). The macron-less-Te-Reo misses (SSFUN06 'Ethical Citizenship / Matatika Kirirarau', MXDB301) are the SAME documented guard limitation the dash/colon/case splitters already have — single today, single after, 0 regression, recorded C. Env TITLESLASH_OFF reverts SLASH only (faithful last-shipped = round 176); BILINGUALMARK_OFF still reverts colon+case.
title_split.strip_boundary_separators_rule: ROUND 177 (Chris, SSFUN05/08 'Visual Literacy /'). The COMPLETION of the slash-separator handling. When a writer types BOTH a soft separator AND a hard one — 'Visual Literacy /  Mātau Reo Ataata' (slash + TWO spaces) — the engine's hard-separator branch (pipe/newline/2-space) splits FIRST and consumes itself, leaving the soft separator ORPHANED on a half boundary ('Visual Literacy /'). After the split, each half has any leading/trailing char in this string (plus surrounding whitespace) trimmed. MEASURED provably human-matching: the human ships 0/405 title <h1> spans that start or end with a separator char (outputs/_measure_title_orphan_sep.py), so a boundary orphan is never legitimate. Scoped to '/' ONLY this round — the char this round handles (fixes SSFUN05, SSFUN08, ENGI401 'A Moment in Time /'). The ORPHAN-DASH class (XDLS909 'Living In Aotearoa –', BLL246 phonics) and the TRAILING-COLON class (PES1001 'Column Addition:', XLP02 '*:', XDLS909 'Activity 10B:') are SEPARATE pre-existing bugs (a different separator / a heading mis-captured as a title) with their own root causes — deliberately NOT swept in here; add their chars to this string only after measuring each class. The edge regex trims ONLY a leading/trailing separator (never one internal to a half), so it also cleans a SINGLE-title orphan (ENGI401 'A Moment in Time /', whose Te Reo half is an unfilled placeholder) while never disturbing a single-language title's intentional internal punctuation ('TV / Radio' keeps its slash). Env TITLESEPTRIM_OFF reverts (faithful last-shipped = round 176).
title_split.bilingual_marker_split_rule: ROUND 168 (Chris, screenshot review — OSAH301-0.0 'EN + Te Reo titles not separated'). Two more bilingual [TITLE BAR] boundaries the dash/punct splitters miss, BOTH behind the SAME round-86 macron guard (EXACTLY one half carries āēīōū, neither half placeholder boilerplate) so they cannot fire on a single-language or already-handled title. (a) COLON: a single ':' boundary — CEDO501 'TE WHAI MŌNI: YOUR MONEY', TWHK903 'Digital Citizenship: Tāurungi Matihiko'. (b) CASE-TRANSITION: an ALL-CAPS English half glued to a non-caps Te Reo half after the writer's ✅/emoji boundary was dropped upstream (DocxExtractor) collapsing to one space — OSAH301 'ONLINE ABUSE AND HARASSMENT Tūkinotanga ā-ipurangi…'; the maximal ALL-CAPS word prefix is the English, the non-caps remainder the Te Reo. The all-caps English self-heals through #normaliseTitleCase (the OSAH301 ALL-CAPS side-effect fixes itself once split). Both run AFTER punct/dash in the chain, so they only see what those rejected. Measured outputs/_measure_title_markersplit.py: 4 clean splits (OSAH301, CEDO105, CEDO501, TWHK903), 0 false positives. Env BILINGUALMARK_OFF reverts to one combined title.
title_split.bilingual_dash_split_rule: Step (6, after the punct split): when the payload has NO pipe / line-break / 2+space separator AND NO slash, split it on a SINGLE spaced dash ( – / — / - ) into TWO titles iff there is EXACTLY ONE such dash, BOTH halves are non-empty, EXACTLY ONE half carries a Te Reo macron (āēīōū), and NEITHER half contains template-placeholder boilerplate (module title / insert / awaiting / translation). The WT preserves order, and the human emits the halves in payload order (Te-Reo-first here, English-first for the pipe-split OSAI201), so parts[0]→english slot, parts[1]→teReo slot reproduces the human ordering. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_dashtitle.py over 147 readable title bars): 3 clean splits — CEDT501 'Kia Māia – Stand Up, Speak Out' and ENGR201 'The Inside Scoop – He Rangahau Pūrongo' EXACT-match the human's two <h1><span>, and CEDW501 'Te Tāute Tāngata – Knowing Yourself' matches the English exactly (the human's Te Reo 'Mōhou Anō' is an unrecorded editorial change, non-derivable). 0 false splits: ENGI201 (slash + multiple dashes) and XGF9003 (pipe) are excluded by the no-slash/no-pipe guard; XMES201 ('…MODULE TITLE TE REO: Aku mokai – …') by the placeholder-boilerplate guard. This SUPERSEDES the non_derivable_note's 'do not split on dash' for this tightly-guarded single-dash + macron + no-other-separator case ONLY; the 97 other two-title modules (slash/colon/bilingual-knowledge) remain non-derivable. Env DASHTITLE_OFF reverts to one combined title.
title_split.bilingual_punct_split_rule: Step (5): when the payload has NO pipe / line-break / 2+space separator, split it into TWO titles iff it is two phrases each ending in the SAME sentence-terminal punctuation (! !, . ., or ? ?) AND exactly ONE half carries a Te Reo macron (āēīōū) — the English!/Te-Reo! pattern. Measured across all 370 human title bars: 2 correct splits (ENGS301 'PICTURE THIS! WHAKAAHUATIA TĒNEI!', ENGC202 'Ready, Set, Instruct! Takatū, Whakaritea, Tohutohu!'), 0 false splits (no single-language title matches both guards). Set false to disable.
title_split.non_derivable_note: The macron-guarded splitters now cover every DERIVABLE separator present in the raw payload: pipe/line-break/2-space (unconditional), spaced-dash (round 86), colon + case-transition (round 168), and slash (round 177). What REMAINS non-derivable is a two-title module whose payload carries NO separator signal AND fails the macron guard — chiefly MACRON-LESS Te Reo (SSFUN06 'Ethical Citizenship / Matatika Kirirarau', MXDB301), where 'this half is Te Reo' cannot be told from the payload alone without a Te-Reo lexicon. The converter keeps those as one title — do not guess. Casing also stays the sentence-case default (round 10): the human's Title-Case rendering of an all-caps WT title is editorial and not derivable.

lone_title_maori_guard.note:
ROUND 80 (Chris, ENGC102): the Course-backup lone-title→Te Reo promotion (PageAssembler) ASSUMED any single [TITLE BAR] title differing from the front-matter Course is the Te Reo name (motivated by OSAI301 'Kirirarautanga matihiko AI'). That MISFIRES when the lone title is the ENGLISH module title and the Course is a broader subject: ENGC102 WT '*KEEPING IT REAL*' + Course 'Communication' shipped

Communication

(Course, wrong) + 'Keeping it real' shoved into the Te Reo slot; ENGS302 put the Māori Course 'Te Ara Hou' in the ENGLISH slot. GUARD: promote to Te Reo ONLY when the lone title is actually Te Reo — Te Reo Māori uses only a e h i k m n o p r t u w (+ macrons; ng/wh digraphs) and NEVER the letters in non_maori_letters, so a lone title carrying any of those is English and stays the English title with NO invented Te Reo (round-76 'only ship what's real'; the real Te Reo e.g. 'Kia mau ki te pono' is not in the WT). VALIDATED against the human gold (outputs/_probe_lonetitle.cjs): OSAI301 still promotes (Māori → Te Reo, English from Course); 0 of 40 single-title comparison-set modules regress (all 40 are English lone titles the human keeps as English). Env LONETITLE_OFF reverts to the always-promote behaviour.

module_prefix_split.note: ROUND 103 (Chris, BLL232). The BLL phonics [TITLE BAR] payload is 'Module N - <letter teams>' (e.g. 'Module 2 - oe, ow, ir, ur, ...'). The human SPLITS it: the leading 'Module N <sep>' prefix is stripped from the title h1 (so the title is just the letter-team remainder, wrapped in <span style="text-transform:lowercase;"> so the phonics render lowercase, not Title-Cased by the site CSS), and the OVERVIEW #module-code chip becomes 'Module {moduleNumber}'. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_module_prefix.py): 49 WT title bars carry this prefix — ALL BLL, 0 non-BLL (the discriminator is self-scoping). The human STRIPS the prefix in 49/49 (0 cases keep 'Module N' in the title h1 — over-fire-safe); applies the lowercase span in 44/44 parseable + the rest confirmed. The chip number tracks the MODULE CODE's last digit (44/46), NOT the writer's title-bar prefix (42/46) — where they differ (BLL142/147/154) the writer typo'd the prefix and the human used the code, so chip_from_code derives 'Module {last-digit-of-moduleCode}'. The 2 code-last-digit misses (BLL166 a human copy-paste 'Module 2' for code …166; one writer/dev inconsistency) and the 3 full-code chips (BLL176/177/252 ship 'BLL17x' not 'Module N') are NON-DERIVABLE editorial deviations — and ALL of this is in #header so it is INVISIBLE to every gate (skeleton text-strips + KEEP_ATTR excludes style; compare_structure/body_compare/defect-leak are #body-scoped). A visible-fidelity match. The strip is gated here (ContentConverter); the flag run.modulePrefix drives the chip + lowercase span in SkeletonBuilder. pattern group 1 = the title remainder. Env MODPREFIX_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts the whole behaviour (no strip → flag stays false → generic 'Module' chip + un-split, un-lowercased title).

phonics_overview_split.note: ROUND 125 (Chris, BLL210). The BLL phonics OVERVIEW (parent) [TITLE BAR] payload is 'LEARNING/TEACHING THE SOUNDS – <letter teams>' (e.g. 'LEARNING THE SOUNDS – y, long vowels, silent e') — the PARENT form, distinct from round 103's lesson 'Module N - ...'. Claude shipped the writer's ALL-CAPS lead verbatim ('LEARNING THE SOUNDS – ...') and left the letter-teams to be Title-Cased by the site CSS ('Y, Long Vowels'). The human de-capitalises the lead ('Learning the sounds', which the CSS capitalize then renders 'Learning The Sounds') and wraps ONLY the post-dash letter-teams in <span style="text-transform:lowercase;"> so they render lowercase ('y, long vowels, silent e'). #normaliseTitleCase already de-caps a WHOLLY-all-caps title (ENGC102 'KEEPING IT REAL' → 'Keeping it real') but SKIPS this one because the lowercase phonics tail makes the string not wholly upper. So this is a dedicated split: group 1 = the all-caps lead (de-capped via #normaliseTitleCase), group 2 = the separator, group 3 = the letter-teams (lowercase span). titleBar.phonicsLead/Sep/Tail drive title_h1_phonics in SkeletonBuilder; a phonics OVERVIEW whose #module-code chip is the bare non-numeric 'Module' literal (no round-103 prefix) shows the MODULE CODE instead (the human shows the code: BLL170/210/220/230/240 = 5 exact; BLL110-160 keep their own chip). Pattern is self-scoping (only the BLL phonics title phrase matches; 0 non-BLL). ALL #header → INVISIBLE to every gate (skeleton text-strips); a visible-fidelity match. Env PHONICSTITLE_OFF (or enabled:false) reverts to the un-split ALL-CAPS title + bare 'Module' chip. The writer's word (LEARNING vs TEACHING) is kept faithfully — the human's editorial TEACHING→Learning swap (BLL110/120) is non-derivable and not chased.

te_reo_line.note: ROUND 198 (Chris — the classT h1-COUNT slice, AGH1006/AGH1005). A Māori-language BLACK line directly following the [TITLE BAR] payload IS the module's Te Reo title (AGH1006 'Te whakatō tipu kākāriki: Te whakahaere hātepe ahumāra' — gold splits the colon pair into TWO h1s; AGH1005 same shape). Fires ONLY when the payload itself produced a single (English) title, the line is the FIRST non-empty item after the title bar, passes the round-80 Māori-alphabet letters test (never mtkFlag) and is title-sized (max_words). The line is CONSUMED (it stops rendering as body/menu text). pair_split: exactly one colon with both halves non-empty → two h1 lines (titleBar.teReoLines), the gold AGH1006 form; else the whole line is one Te Reo h1. Measured over ALL 430 module dirs through the live pipeline (outputs/_measure_titleh1.cjs): the Māori-adjacent-line population is EXACTLY AGH1005+AGH1006; over-fire surface ZERO (no module has such a line where gold ships no extra h1). Env TEREOLINE_OFF.

marker_glue_split.note: ROUND 199 (Chris — the classT h1-COUNT/text slice, XMES/TWHA family). The writer left the template's boilerplate prompt GLUED inside the [TITLE BAR] payload and typed the real Te Reo after it (XMES103 'My Family – Who I live with MODULE TITLE TE REO: Taku Whānau' → one combined <h1>; gold ships two: 'My Family – Who I live with' + 'Taku Whānau'). The round-76 whole-PART placeholder filter only drops a marker that is its OWN part (pipe/2-space separated, e.g. OSGM501 'GAMING SAFELY | MODULE TITLE TE REO'); a marker glued MID/SUFFIX to real text never reaches it and LEAKS. This rule EXPLODES each split part at its glued boilerplate marker (dropping the marker), reusing the standard English|Te-Reo assignment (the r86 two-h1 shape). GUARDS (both required, measured): (a) the whole payload must NOT START with a marker — a payload leading with the marker is Te-Reo-first (CEDT104 'MODULE TITLE: Waiata I te Neke | Waiata in Motion') where English-first cannot be guaranteed, so it is left to today's form (recorded residue; gold itself editorially reorders it); (b) a part that is WHOLLY a marker is LEFT to the round-76 placeholder filter, so its droppedPlaceholder flag + red flag are UNCHANGED and the OSGM501 whole-part class stays byte-identical. The markers are extra_placeholders (multi-word boilerplate); the bare 'te reo' from placeholder_titles is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — it is a real Te Reo word inside genuine titles (CEDW201 'Ko te reo atawhai me te reo manaaki', claude==gold), the false-positive surface. Markers are matched longest-first so 'module title te reo' wins over its substring 'module title'. MEASURED over ALL 430 module dirs (outputs/_measure_titlemarker.cjs): 34 payloads carry a marker; the GLUED-leak population fixed here is EXACTLY 12 modules (11 tracked — CEDK102, TWHA901-905, XLP01, XMES101/102/103/201 — plus the gold-only XMES202); the 18 whole-part / marker-prefix / Course-backup modules stay byte-identical; over-fire surface ZERO (no real title carries the boilerplate; TWHK907/OSOH501 golds ship it as a JUNK h1 which the fix correctly drops). Env TITLEMARKSPLIT_OFF.

split_payload_join.note: ROUND 198 (Chris — the classT h1-COUNT slice, TEFUN03/ANZH101). The writer authored ONE bilingual title line but SPLIT it across spans, so the round-76 black-preferred payload rule saw only half: (a) pipe_lead_black — the embedded RED title + a black payload STARTING with '|' ([TITLE BAR] 'Whakaaro Auaha' + '| Thinking creatively', TEFUN03) → payload = embedded + black; (b) pipe_sibling — a no-primary red instruction/noise span DIRECTLY after the title bar whose text starts with '|' ('| Tangata Whenua Pūrākau', ANZH101) → absorbed into the payload + consumed. The joined payload then splits on the pipe like any normal bilingual title. When a JOINED payload yields exactly 2 parts with exactly ONE Māori-lettered half, the English half is assigned first (gold ships EN-first on both; scoped to joined payloads only — the dash/char split paths keep payload order, CEDW501 gold ships Te Reo first there). Measured over ALL 430 WTs: pipe_lead_black = TEFUN03 + ANZH401 (ANZH401's pipe-half is placeholder boilerplate → dropped by the round-76 list, output byte-identical); pipe_sibling = ANZH101 + MXFL104 + OSOH301 (the DANGLING-pipe arm: the black payload ENDS with '|' and the adjacent span is the other half — 'ONLINE @HOME |' + red 'Ngā whakahaeretanga ā-ipurangi i te kāinga', gold ships both; measured exactly 1 corpus-wide) — the span's text AND its blackAfter are absorbed (MXFL104's bare red '|' separator span carries the Te Reo half in its OWN blackAfter, a mid-paragraph red span — live-probed; gold ships both languages as h1s and no body line). Env TITLESPANJOIN_OFF.

menu_empty_heading_rule.rule: A preconfigured menu/section heading with NO content before the next heading (or the menu end) is OMITTED — human developers almost never render an empty scaffolding heading. Measured across the corpus: 'What do I need to get started?' filled 127 vs empty-kept 3; Connections/Assessment/Planning your time NEVER empty. Applies to ALL menu archetypes.

menu.rule: menu_type registry value picks the shell. Overview pre-body headings route into the menu per tab_map (the CONSUMED outcome — they emit no body element). menu_type 'none' = no menu button and no menu content div at all.
menu._strip_italic_all_doc: ROUND 145 (Chris) — GENERAL menu-item italic strip. Measured corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_italic_transfer.py): the human strips <i>/<em> from module-menu items 99% (2173/2200; Standard 99% / Inquiry 93%), vs a mixed 43-66% (editorial) in body/activity/table and 0% (always KEPT) in acks — a clean role rule. The WT wraps menu learning-intentions/curriculum/descriptions in *italics*; the human menu carries none. ContentConverter.#buildMenu strips text-italic from ALL panes (tab1/tab2/content/left/right) via #stripTextItalic (removes <i>/<em>, keeps inner text; a Font-Awesome icon <i class="fa…"> is never touched — measured 0 icon <i> in any menu), generalising the round-81/109/142 ENG/banner curriculum-pane strips. EXCLUDES reo/bilingual modules (#isReoModule: TRR/PNR prefix / reoTranslate body_class / mtkFlag): there the human KEEPS italic on BOTH panes — the reo line AND its English translation (32 spans; TRR108 'He kaingākaunui…' + 'Mokopuna care about…', TRR301). Menu is #header-scoped (skeleton text-strips + KEEP_ATTR excludes it; cs/bc/defect are #body-scoped) → gate-neutral; ships on visible human match (round-81/142 precedent). Env MENUITALIC_OFF reverts to the round-142 family-only strip.
menu._none_family_fallthrough_doc: ROUND 107 (Chris — anchor_compare menu over-emit) — a Menu_Scaffold_Registry GROUP with NO measured evidence for the requested scope (e.g. a fundamentals family whose `overview` was never measured, n=0) but whose OTHER scope is a measured 'none' is a MENU-LESS family: the human ships no module-menu at all. Without this, #menuTypeFor falls the unmeasured scope through to the generic Style-Anchor default and FABRICATES a menu the human never built (TEFUN: lesson 'none' n=8, overview unmeasured → Claude bolted a 2–17 li menu onto the .phases overview the human leaves menu-less). The rule returns 'none' for that scope. Tight by construction — only fires when the SIBLING scope is an explicit 'none', so menu-BEARING fundamentals (ENFUN/HPFUN/MXFUN/XFUN lesson 'simplified') are untouched. Env MENUNONE_OFF reverts to the generic fallthrough.

lesson_repeats_overview._doc: ROUND 110 (Chris) — LESSON-MENU REPEAT. A small, measured set of modules repeat the OVERVIEW curriculum (Understand/Know/Do) menu VERBATIM on every lesson page's #module-menu-content (MXFL201_1.0 ≡ _0.0, 26 li). Claude built the curriculum only on the overview and left the lesson menus EMPTY. For a FLAGGED module, ContentConverter stashes the overview's built menu (run.overviewMenu) and reuses it wherever a lesson menu would be EMPTY. PER-MODULE by necessity, MEASURED non-derivable: MXFL201 repeats but MXFL204 — SAME subject×phase, SAME 'simplified' lesson menu-type, indistinguishable WT inputs — does NOT (its lesson menus are empty, already matching Claude); the discriminator is the human's per-module editorial choice (outputs/_measure_menu_population.py: the convert-time signal over-fires 69%). Tight + over-fire-proof: only the listed modules fire, and only where the lesson menu is ALREADY empty (never overrides a populated lesson menu, never fires on a menu_type 'none' page). Menu is #header-scoped → PRIMARY skeleton only. Env MENUREPEAT_OFF reverts.

lesson_content_in_menu._doc: ROUND 114 (Chris, OSAH501-03) — LESSON LEARNING-INTENTIONS → MENU. On a lesson page the [Lesson Overview] section's content IS the page menu: the intro line PLUS the [Lesson content] sub-region ('We are learning:' / 'I can:' lists). #partitionItems previously ended the lesson menu AT the [Lesson content] marker (lessonMenuEnd = contentIdx), so only the intro reached #module-menu-content and the WALT/I-can block leaked into #body. With this flag the [Lesson content] marker OPENS a menu sub-region instead of closing the menu: the menu runs from [Lesson Overview] to the first heading / title-bar (whether or not [Lesson content] is present), and the bare [Lesson content] marker item is skipped. MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_lessonmenu.py): 442 human lesson pages route WALT/I-can to the menu vs 5 to the body = 98.9%; the 5 body-exceptions (XGF9001) are menu-LESS pages (no #module-menu-content) so the fix — which only extends an EXISTING lesson menu — can NEVER touch them (REAL over-fire = 0). Guard: if extending past [Lesson content] finds NO heading, fall back to ending at the marker (never regress to an empty menu). Menu is #header-scoped → moves PRIMARY skeleton + body compare_structure (the body loses the leaked rows). Env LESSONINTENT_OFF reverts to ending the menu at the marker.

lesson_overview_bare_lead.note: ROUND 148 (Chris, review queue 1 part 2a — EXIP901/EXBP901/ENGS302). The BRACKET-LESS red 'Lesson overview' lead: the writer types the words as red TEXT with no square brackets, so no [Lesson Overview] tag resolves (TagNormaliser: class=noise, primary=null) and overviewIdx is never found — the lesson menu never fires and the whole WALT/intentions run stays #body, while the human routes it to #module-menu-content on EVERY such page (verified EXIP901_0.1-0.4, EXBP901_0.1-0.4, ENGS302_3.0; the writer even leaves the note 'In banner (as consistent with other products)'). MEASURED corpus-wide (outputs/_measure_bareoverview.py): exactly 3 modules / 11 bare spans; 0 black-text occurrences of the phrase anywhere in the corpus, so a RED-span-only predicate cannot over-fire by construction; every bracketed [Lesson Overview] (140 modules) resolves primary and is untouched. With this flag, when NO bracketed tag exists on the page, a red noise/instruction span whose ENTIRE folded text matches `pattern` is accepted as the overview MARKER (position only — the span itself renders nothing either way, so nothing is stripped that was previously shown). All downstream machinery (r114 lesson_content_in_menu, r147 section-stop, named-heading promotion) is marker-relative and reused unchanged. Env BARELEAD_OFF reverts to tag-only detection.

lesson_menu_section_stop.note: Round 147 (Chris, review queue 1 — menu under-populated 240pp/82m). SECTION-STOP lesson-menu capture, coupled with the same round's PAGE-ROLE-AWARE Menu_Scaffold_Registry re-mine (derive_menu_type.cjs; MENUREG_OFF). The r114 region (LO → first heading) absorbs everything in between, but the CED NCEA family writes [Lesson Overview] → [alert.top] printable-resources + [Button]s → [Lesson content] → WALT → [H2], and the human keeps the alert/buttons in #body with only the WALT in the menu (CEDO501 1.0–6.0). With this flag the menu absorbs two CONTIGUOUS TEXT sections — the [Lesson Overview] intro run + the [Lesson content] section — each running only over black text and menu_section_safe_tags; ANY other tag (alert, button, image, interactive, heading) ends its section and stays body. inquiry_tab_ends_overview_menu._doc: ROUND 119 (Chris, anchor_compare inquiry round — TWHA901/903/906). On a SINGLE-FILE inquiry LANDING the overview page holds BOTH the learning-design menu sections (Learning Intentions / Success Criteria / Planning / Connections / Assessment) AND the inquiry PANELS ([Tab 1: Introduction], [Tab 2], …). The CONTENT-BASED overview menu partition (menu.overview_section_labels) walks the items setting inMenu=true on a menu-label heading; the LAST menu section's inMenu=true then SWALLOWED the following [Tab 1]/[Tab 2] openers into #module-menu-content (they are not headings, so nothing flipped inMenu off) until the first non-menu inquiry heading ([H3] Agency) — so [Tab 1]/[Tab 2] never reached #body and got NO panel sentinel, collapsing Introduction+Agency(+Resilience) into one panel (TWHA901 built 9 of 11). SCOPED to the overviewMenuIdx content-fallback path (introIdx<0 && isOverview && menu!=='none'); a module with NO [Tab N] opener is byte-identical (the flag only fires where a tab-family tag exists, which is inquiry-only). closer_residue_strip._doc:
ROUND 111 (Chris, Task A — the [end X] leftover-leak). A writer CLOSER directive ([End page] / [End of important box] / [End interactive] / [End of task] / [End of alert box] / [End supervisor note] …) is a DIRECTIVE that renders NOTHING, but in a few downstream render contexts (a black or coalesced run, a flowing quote box) it survived into the BODY as a LONE

[tag]

. #stripCloserResidue removes such a

when the bracket (a) carries the standalone word end/ends AND (b) resolves via the REAL TagNormaliser to a CONTAINER_CLOSE or PAGE_BOUNDARY directive (class 'tag'). The 'end' word-guard is the precision floor — it EXCLUDES a mis-resolved heading like [Lesson Summary] (resolves to lesson/PAGE_BOUNDARY but has no 'end' → kept) and the [next page] page-break openers; the resolver-guard EXCLUDES content (e.g. [a mini-dictionary … near the end of a book] resolves to an OPENER 'important' → kept). A bracket carrying embedded CONTENT ([Lesson 2] THE WORLD COURT) is never a LONE

so it is untouched. IMPORTANT — the general [end X] closer CONVENTION itself was MEASURED already-built (97.9% / 3609 of 3687 occurrences already resolve to a closer via the prefix end/of// + the round-96 suffix X ends + the lexicon end-* aliases); this round ONLY suppresses the downstream LEAKED residue (kickoff algorithm step 4). Measured 21 occ / 6 modules (ENGFUN02 HIS1002 HIS1005 HIS1006 XDLS502 XGF9004); human ships 0. Env ENDCLOSER_OFF reverts (the lone

leaks again). Tools outputs/_measure_endclosers.cjs (resolution census), outputs/_measure_closer_pstrip.cjs (strip footprint).

fundamentals_panels._doc: ROUND 98 (Templates round B) — wrap the FUNDAMENTALS body into div.fundamentalsPanel phase="N" panels. The FIRST segment is the introduction panel (intro_class). AUTO-SCOPED to modules that carry [New tab] — the HPFUN family (7 mods); the SSFUN (activity-number-group delimiter, 4 mods) and XFUN ([H1] delimiter, 1 mod) families carry NO [New tab] so the pass is a NO-OP for them (byte-identical) — sized follow-up. at the top of #body. In fundamentals mode, when a single page carries >= min_delimiters standalone 'Phase N' black paragraphs AND no tag-based page/phase delimiter ([New tab]/[LESSON]/[Page N]), ContentConverter consumes each 'Phase N' line into a top-level {sentinel}; #fundamentalsPanels (phase_text branch) emits the div.phases nav (one

Phase N

per delimiter), wraps the pre-phase content in div.introduction, and wraps each phase segment in div.fundamentalsPanel phase=N (NO generated heading — the human keeps the phase's own [H3] 'Plan it!'/'Present it!'). The >=2-on-page + no-tag-delimiter gate scopes this to the clean TEFUN01-08 single-page 4-phase family and EXCLUDES MXFUN01 (a multi-file module whose Phase 1/2/4 sit on a deep page with [Page N]/[Lesson] openers). Measured outputs/_measure_phase_delimiter.py: fire set = TEFUN01-08 (4 delims -> 4 panels each); 0 non-fundamentals, 0 gated. Env FUNDPHASE_OFF reverts to the round-105 flat render (bare

Phase N

, no panels).

red_delimiter._doc: ROUND 189 (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 8 — D2 class P, the ENFUN slice; the r186 recorded follow-up). The ENFUN family delimits each phase with a standalone RED 'Phase N' span (no brackets: class noise, primary null, renders NOTHING) — the red twin of the TEFUN black line — so the r106 pre-pass never fired and the 8 ENFUN golds' chrome-and-panels form (.phases nav + introduction/tiles + 4 fundamentalsPanel) shipped FLAT. MEASURED over ALL 427 WTs through the live pipeline (outputs/_measure_funpanred.cjs): the class = EXACTLY 8 modules (ENFUN01-05/07/08/09, all ENFUN|combo single-file), every one nums [1,2,3,4] with the Phase-1 span PRE-alias (menu side); >=2-spans-outside-the-gate = ZERO; 24 longer prose mentions ('link to phase 2 fundamental', '[MXFUN102 content - Phase 1]') stay inert by the ENTIRE-folded-text predicate; MXFUN02's lone span is below min_delimiters (and unconsumed, so the scanner twin is a no-op there). THREE coupled acceptances, ONE toggle: (1) the ConvertPage pre-pass accepts the red span (type tag, no primary, class noise/instruction, whole folded text matching delimiter_pattern) as a phasebreak, blackAfter preserved (measured 0 carriers, belt-and-braces); (2) #partitionItems routes a PRE-alias matching span to bodyItems (it renders nothing in the menu — position-only, the r148 BARELEAD class; the r187 funLi menu region otherwise untouched); (3) InteractiveScanner #swallowMembers treats it as a HARD terminator (the red twin of terminators_absolute_text — measured: 3/4 spans on ENFUN01/07/09 were widget-swallowed without it, so those phases never opened). The r106/r113 emit path is UNCHANGED (nav 'Phase N' labels + introduction holding the phaseLink tiles + plain panels = the gold ENFUN live form, proven byte-shape on TEFUN02); gold's introduction PROSE is human-authored (in NO WT) = recorded C, as are the per-phase [Overview]+WALT repeat blocks gold drops/merges into the menu editorially (recorded follow-up, NOT this round). Gate everywhere: fundamentals body_class + page_model single-file + the flag (+ >=min_delimiters page-wide for the pre-pass/partition). Env FUNPANRED_OFF reverts all three.

bracketed_delimiter._doc: ROUND 191 (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 10 — D2 class P, the ARFUN slice; the r189 recorded follow-up). The ARFUN family delimits each fundamentals phase with BRACKETED red instruction spans — the THIRD delimiter dialect after TEFUN's black 'Phase N' (r106) and ENFUN's bare red 'Phase N' (r189) — wildly varied wording, spelled numbers AND digits: openers '[Phase one content begins]'/'[Start of phase two content]' (class instruction, primary null, folded keeps the brackets → they rendered as retained CS notes), closers '[End of Phase One]'/'[End of phase two content]' ('end other', CONTAINER_CLOSE) and '[End page and phase N content]' ('end page', PAGE_BOUNDARY — those never reach ConvertPage items). MEASURED over ALL 427 WTs through the live pipeline (outputs/_measure_funpanbracket.cjs): the class = EXACTLY 4 modules (ARFUN01/02/03/05, all ARFUN|combo fundamentals single-file; opener nums in order, 0 out-of-gate openers corpus-wide); ARFUN02's phase-4 boundary is CLOSER-ONLY ('[End of phase three content]' — the writer never wrote a phase-4 opener), so closers are break candidates too, gated by closer_requires_opener: 7 CLOSER-ONLY modules (ARFUN04 + TEFUN01/03/04/06/07/08 '[end phase N]') must stay untouched — TEFUN already panels via the r106 black dialect (unconditional closer acceptance would double-break it) and ARFUN04 (class O, 50-file gold, multi-file page model, 'beginning of/begin' opener dialect = near-misses) is its own round. Openers 1x widget-consumed on ARFUN01/03/05 (an engagement-quiz bundle swallows the next phase's opener) → the scanner hard-terminator twin covers the OPENER pattern only (closers measured never consumed, clCons=0 on all 11 closer-carrying modules). Adjacent closer+opener breaks and a trailing break are harmless by construction (the phase_text emit branch trims + filters empty segments). Both patterns are ENTIRE-folded-span with optional surrounding brackets; near-misses 11 spans / 3 modules stay inert; 0 modules carry both this and the black/red dialects. Env FUNPANBRACKET_OFF reverts all three acceptances; FUNDPHASE_OFF still reverts the whole phase-text machinery.

tag_anchored_delimiter._doc:
ROUND 192 (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 11 — D2 class P, the LAST two phase-text dialects). SCFUN01 and SSFUN03 anchor the phase word to a TAG's blackAfter instead of a standalone line/span — the FOURTH+FIFTH delimiter shapes after TEFUN black (r106), ENFUN bare-red (r189), ARFUN bracketed (r191): SCFUN01 '[TILE N] Phase N' (primary 'shape n' SUBTAG — the split-bracket '[TILE 1'+']' and ✅-emoji forms all self-heal to a clean parse, live-probed; ONE tile the writer typed in BLACK text, '[Tile 2] Phase 2', covered by black_line_pattern) and SSFUN03 '[Fundamental content] SSFUN03 **PHASE N**' (primary 'lesson content' SECTION_MARKER; the blackAfter carries the MODULE-CODE prefix + ** bold marks — the {code} placeholder in blackafter_pattern is replaced with the run's own module code, never hard-coded). eligible_tags maps each primary tag to its BREAK KIND — the branch whose emitted form matches the family gold: 'shape n' → 'phase_text' (ptsent; SCFUN01 gold panels open with the WT's own [h2], NO generated heading — the TEFUN form) and 'lesson content' → 'lesson' (lsent; the SSFUN family gold form = generated

Phase N

, measured SSFUN01/02/05/06 — SSFUN03's own h5 is a 1-of-6 within-family deviation, family form ships, the r188 gold-outlier class). The predicate: an UNCONSUMED tag item whose primary is in eligible_tags AND whose ENTIRE cleaned blackAfter (** stripped, symbol/emoji edges stripped, whitespace folded) matches blackafter_pattern — so residual prose can never be silently dropped (there is none by construction). MEASURED over ALL 427 WTs through the live pipeline (outputs/_measure_funpantag.cjs): the class = EXACTLY SCFUN01 (3 tag hits nums [1,3,4] + 1 black tile line) + SSFUN03 (4 hits nums [1,2,3,4]); 0 hits outside the gate; near-misses = EXPFUN02-05 '[Title] Phase N' (title bar NOT in eligible_tags — structurally excluded — and singletons below min_delimiters anyway); XFUN01's [H1] delimiters carry longer text and never match (verified absent from the probe); black tile lines corpus-wide = exactly SCFUN01's 1; 0 dialect overlap; ALL hits UNCONSUMED → NO scanner twin needed (unlike r189/r191 — recorded measurement, the census would surface a future consumed case). SCFUN01's phantom 2 panels (orphan [tab 1]/[tab 2] SUBTAGs in phase 4 hitting the r98 [New tab] push) are superseded: the ptsent branch strips stray CV2_FUNDPANEL sentinels (the r113 MXFUN02/03 strip); gold builds that pair as real tabs = class T, recorded, NOT this round. Env FUNPANTAG_OFF reverts the whole acceptance; FUNDPHASE_OFF still reverts the entire phase-text machinery.

accordion_delimiter._doc: ROUND 194 (Chris, STOCKTAKE session 13 — D2 class P, the LAST zero-panel module; the r193 recorded verdict's own round). XFUN01 authors its whole body as ONE [Accordion] widget of NINE numbered [Accordion 1..9] sections, and the human builds NO accordion — the fundamentals phases chrome instead (nav ×9 heading-labels + ONE noPhase row of 9 phaseLink tiles + 9 fundamentalsPanel, 1:1 BY NUMBER with the writer's sections; panel 8's head is the writer's [H4], so heading-counting misses it — the accordion NUMBER is the phase). A NEW mechanism class: every earlier dialect (r106 black / r189 red / r191 bracketed / r192 tag-anchored) accepts UNCONSUMED items, but these delimiters are widget INVOCATIONS the scanner consumes into bundles — so the fix is FOUR coupled pieces behind this one flag: (1) InteractiveScanner SUPPRESSION — on a gated page an accordion-primary INTERACTIVE invocation never opens a bundle (numbered/bare forms left unconsumed for the pre-pass; the writer's '[link to this section of the accordion menu]' cross-link falls to the link dissolve) + the numbered/bare forms are HARD member-walk terminators (no other bundle may swallow a phase boundary); (2) the ConvertPage pre-pass — folded ^\[accordion (\d+)\]$ → ONE {type:phasebreak} (ptsent kind: panels keep their own [H3]/[H4], the TEFUN no-generated-heading form), the bare [accordion] opener + the [End accordion section] closers (bracketed CONTAINER_CLOSE ×7 + ONE bracket-less instruction form, measured) → consumed no-ops, blackAfter preserved everywhere (measured 0 carriers); (3) the THIRD nav/tile dialect on the ptsent branch, driven by THIS registry row: label_mode heading (faithful first-heading nav labels — gold's 'Low tech'⊂'Low tech (no computer chip in sight)' abbreviations are the r188 recorded-editorial class) + ALL-phases ONE-ROW col-md-4 col-6 tiles in a 'row phaseContainer noPhase' container with alt='Phase N' (differs from BOTH r113 phaseNavTiles and r188 newTabNav; tile img = panel-first-img with intro fallback — the 9 gold iStock srcs are in NO WT, the r106 non-derivable tile-image class); (4) leftover handling — link_dissolve_pattern drops a '[link to … section]' cross-reference MARKER and re-exposes its blackAfter as prose (gold keeps the prose, drops/edits the links; the pre-round orphan-subtag RED FLAGs ×3 go), black_residue_pattern drops the L205 split-bracket black '[' leftover. THE FENCE: numbered [Accordion N] is the corpus-STANDARD accordion idiom — measured over ALL 427 WTs (outputs/_measure_funpanacc.cjs): 61 modules carry numbered accordions, 60 of them NON-fundamentals (golds build REAL accordions — untouched BY CONSTRUCTION: no registry row), near-gate (fundamentals+single-file, no row) = ZERO, the gated class = EXACTLY XFUN01 (9 numbered [1..9] + 1 bare + 1 link-INTERACTIVE + 8 closers + 10 link items + 1 black residue); XFUN02 is triple-fenced (0 numbered accordions, multi-file gold, lesson-structured). Registry lookup = the r166/r187/r188 shape (series → subject|template_phase via skeleton.template_attr_map). Recorded C within the module (r193): gold panel 5's rearranged Hoa-ako note + 'Be my hands' (WT Accordion 9 — the faithful ship keeps them in panel 9), the hmFQqjMF_f0 video + nznasca button in NO WT, the tile iStock images. Env FUNPANACC_OFF reverts all four pieces; FUNDPHASE_OFF still reverts the entire phase-text machinery.

per PANEL (intro included) and (b) a phaseLink tile grid for the CONTENT phases only (2..N — one tile per content panel, 11/12 golds; HPFUN401's missing 7th tile is the gold outlier), the tiles sitting INSIDE the intro panel after its content, chunked into .row.phaseContainer rows of tiles_per_row when the count exceeds tiles_split_over (gold: 4 tiles → one row ×4 golds; 5 → 3+2 HPFUN301; 6 → 3+3 HPFUN903; HPFUN101's single row of 5 + HPFUN102's justify-content-center wrapper are gold outliers — the family form ships).
