inquiry_tabs._doc: ROUND 100 (Templates round D) — the INQUIRY tabbed template (BLL [Tab N]-label-list family). A firing module has a 'side tabs' instruction + a `[Tab N] <label>` crumb-label list + ≥2 EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers. ContentConverter captures the labels, pushes a {sentinel} at each empty opener, suppresses the instruction + the label-list, and #inquiryPanels wraps the body into `div.crumbs` (an intro crumb + one per tab) + `div.inquiryPanel` (an intro panel + one per opener). SkeletonBuilder sets the `inquiry container-fluid` body class + the `footer-nav inquiry-nav` footer when content.inquiryActive. Discriminator is conservative (side-tabs instruction REQUIRED) so the `[tabs]`-widget `[Tab N]` modules (BLL232/236, OSAI501, MXDB202, PNR, XGF, ENGJ402…) do NOT fire. Env INQUIRYTABS_OFF reverts to the flat render (orphan `[Tab N]` flags and all).
inquiry_tabs._footer_nav_doc: ROUND 102 — the FIXED inquiry footer nav shell (the human ships an identical home/prev/next `ul.footer-nav.inquiry-nav` on every inquiry page). SkeletonBuilder emits it for a firing CED page (content.cedInquiry) ONLY when the registry produced NO footer links (single-file CED → footer_links 'none' → empty footer) — so a round-100 BLL module that already carries registry footer links is byte-unchanged. The hrefs render empty (single page), matching the human.
inquiry_tabs._body_class_requires_build_doc: ROUND 107 (Chris — anchor_compare template over-fire) — couples the `inquiry` body token to an actually-built inquiry page. The registry stamps `container-fluid inquiry` as a whole-SUBJECT default (ConnectED, Blended Literacy, *WHA), so every lesson page of those subjects inherited `inquiry` though the human ships it ONLY on the crumbs/inquiryPanel landing and leaves every lesson page plain `container-fluid`. Measured invariant (whole corpus): HUMAN inquiry-body⟺inquiry-build (55 build, only 7 body-without-build, 0 build-without-body); CLAUDE violated it on 77 pages. SkeletonBuilder strips the `inquiry` token when the page is NOT content.inquiryActive; fundamentals/mathJax/reoTranslate untouched; a page that DOES build inquiry keeps it via the inquiryActive override. Env INQBODY_OFF reverts to the raw registry token.

heading_label._guards_doc: ROUND 112 over-fire guards (measured `outputs/_probe_twha.cjs` + a full candidate sweep). (1) `min_true_openers` (2): `_emptyOpeners` counts the `[End tab]` CONTAINER_CLOSE closers, so the EX `[Section N]`/`[New side tab]` family (EXPFUN04: 1 true opener + 7 closers = `_emptyOpeners` 8) would fire and build a 1-panel page vs the human's 7 — require ≥2 TRUE openers (the real panel-split signal). (2) SINGLE-FILE scope (`run.resolvedRules.page_model !== 'multi-file'`): the heading-label landing is one page; the EX multi-file inquiry family is a DIFFERENT plan-deferred structure. NOTE — EXIP901/EXBP901 build inquiry panels via the PRE-EXISTING `_bllInquiry` side-tabs-instruction path (round 100), NOT this rule (confirmed HEADINGLABEL_OFF byte-identical). (3) The HPFUN fundamentals family meets the firing condition but is BYTE-IDENTICAL (the fundPanelMode SUBTAG branch pushes its own FUND_SENTINEL before the inquiry sentinel, and #inquiryPanels no-ops without an INQ_SENTINEL) — a harmless over-fire, proven by diff. Firing set: TWHA901/903/904/906/TWHK903 only. EXPFUN06 + canaries (CEDO501/ENGJ301/ENGJ302/PES1004/XGF9003) excluded.
heading_label._doc: ROUND 111 (Chris, Task B) — the TWHA/TWHK HEADING-LABEL inquiry sub-family. Unlike the BLL family (a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list + a 'side tabs' instruction) these carry EMPTY `[Tab N]` openers, NO labelled list, and NO 'side tabs' instruction — the crumb LABEL is each panel's FIRST heading (English part before ' | '). FIRE when `_labeledTabs === 0 AND _emptyOpeners >= min_openers`. ENGINE-MEASURED (outputs/_probe_twha.cjs) the threshold 6 cleanly separates the templates (TWHA901 _emptyOpeners=17 / TWHK903=17 / TWHA906=13 / TWHA903=8 — the count includes the `[End tab]` CONTAINER_CLOSE closers, which do NOT open panels) from EVERY over-fire danger (CEDO501 max 3, ENGJ301/PES1004 max 4, ENGJ302 max 3, XGF9003 always `_labeledTabs>=1`) — 0 false positives. BUILD = the UNIFIED page_split form (rel="1".."N", first showing): crumb-1 is the fixed 'Introduction', crumbs 2..N are the panels' first headings; panel-1 absorbs any pre-first-tab body content (usually empty — the overview is partitioned to the menu) so nothing is lost. The 11 TWHA901 openers reach page.items 1:1 with the human's 11 panels (headings Agency/Resilience/.../Curiosity == the human crumbs). TWHA902 already fires via the labelled path; EXPFUN06 (_emptyOpeners=4) is a deferred FN. Env HEADINGLABEL_OFF reverts to the flat render (orphan `[Tab N]` flags). Tool outputs/_probe_twha.cjs.

page_opener_fire._doc: ROUND 139 (Chris, BLL140/BLL220). WIDENS the round-100 `_bllInquiry` firing test to the `[page N]`-DELIMITED PANEL form. Round 100 fires when a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list (>=3) is followed by >=2 EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers. But BLL140/BLL220 author the crumb-list then open panel 1 on an empty `[Tab 1]` and panels 2..N on labelled `[page N]` markers (only ONE empty opener), so they fell BETWEEN path-1 (>=2 empty) and the heading-label path (0 labelled) and built ZERO panels/crumbs/nav. This flag makes `_bllInquiry` ALSO true when min_labeled orphan labelled `[Tab N]` (a real crumb-list) AND min_empty empty `[Tab N]` (the lead opener) AND min_page_openers top-level `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY markers (the panel delimiters) co-occur — then the EXISTING bll_page_split machinery opens the `[page N]` panels and the crumbs build, no new build code. The min_page_openers>=3 requirement is the over-fire discriminator: the widget-`[Tab N]` modules (MXDB202/XGF9003/MXFL301) carry orphan labelled tabs but 0 top-level `[page N]`, so they never fire. MEASURED 0 over-fire across all 73 `[Tab N]` modules; newly fires EXACTLY BLL140+BLL220 (both human-panelled). BLL240 (a multi-page inquiry variant, 0 page-openers on the landing) is a deferred follow-up. Env BLLPAGEOPENER_OFF reverts (independent of INQUIRYTABS_OFF); tool outputs/_measure_bllpage_widen.cjs.

bll_page_split._doc: ROUND 120 (Chris, BLL210). The BLL phonics inquiry family (round 100, _bllInquiry: a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list + EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers) authors each section as a HYBRID boundary — an empty `[Tab N]` AND a `[Page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY AND a `[H#]` label, e.g. `[Tab 4][Page 4][H2] a_e`. But SOME sections open on a `[Page N]` ALONE (no empty `[Tab N]` of their own — BLL210's Long vowels `[page 2]` + Silent e `[page 3]`). `_bllInquiry` split panels only on empty `[Tab N]` (line ~1016) + the round-101 consumed-opener recovery, NOT on `[page N]` (that was the cedInquiry-only path), so a `[page N]`-alone section MERGED into the previous panel and every subsequent crumb LABEL shifted (BLL210 built 7 of the human's 9 panels; o_e/u_e content landed under the e_e/i_e labels). FIX: in `_bllInquiry` (NOT cedInquiry — that family is mutually exclusive) a top-level `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY ALSO opens a panel (close any open activity first, like the round-101 idiom), DE-DUPLICATED so it never double-splits the `[Tab N][page N]` pairs: a `[page N]` is a no-op when the immediately-preceding body item is itself a tab-family opener or another page boundary (so the `[Tab 4][Page 4]` pair = ONE boundary, and a consumed-`[Tab N]`'s `[page N]` defers to the recovery). General + data-described; the firing discriminator is UNCHANGED (still _bllInquiry), so a module with no standalone `[page N]` is byte-identical. Env BLLPAGE_OFF reverts to the [Tab N]-only split (the round-100/101 under-built panels).

inquiry_tabs._recover_doc: ROUND 101 (Templates round D-followup) — INQUIRY consumed-opener RECOVERY. The empty `[Tab N]` PANEL OPENERS that follow a widget are frequently SWALLOWED by that widget's scanner capture (BLL150/160/170/210 — a trailing `[Tab N]` absorbed as the last member of the activity's final `modal`; TWHA902 — a `carousel`), so the panel never opened and the inquiry page under-built (2 panels vs the human's 6-9). In CONFIRMED inquiry mode (content.inquiryActive, computed post-scan so the discriminator is UNCHANGED — zero new over-fire), a NON-`[tabs]` bundle whose TRAILING members are empty `[Tab N]` closes any open activity and pushes one panel {sentinel} per swallowed opener — restoring the boundary the scanner ate WITHOUT un-consuming the tag (no leak) and WITHOUT a scanner change. Real `[tabs]` widgets are skipped (their `[Tab N]` are legitimate members; ENGJ301/XGF9003 untouched). A module that does NOT fire inquiry never reaches this path, so the lone non-inquiry module that absorbs an empty `[Tab N]` (ENGJ402, an accordion the writer mis-tagged) is byte-identical. Measured `outputs/_probe_tabconsume.cjs`: 6 modules absorb an empty `[Tab N]` into a non-tabs widget — 5 inquiry (recovered) + ENGJ402 (does not fire → untouched). Env INQRECOVER_OFF reverts to the round-100 under-built panels.

page_split._doc: ROUND 102 (Templates round D-followup) — the CED [Page N]-SPLIT inquiry sub-family (the ORPHAN crumb-list cut: CEDK101, CEDT404). Unlike the BLL family (round 100, panels open on EMPTY [Tab N]), these carry a PURE `[Tab N] <label>` crumb-list (EVERY tab labelled, ZERO empty openers) and split panels on in-stream `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY markers (single-file mode keeps them as section breaks — these CED levels are page_model:single-file). FIRE only when ALL hold: a consecutive labelled `[Tab N]` run >=3 that EQUALS the module's total `[Tab N]` count (a pure crumb-list), 0 empty openers anywhere, >=2 in-stream `[page N]` openers, AND panels(openers+1) == crumbs(labels). The >=2-in-stream-`[page N]` requirement EXCLUDES every real `[tabs]`-widget module (they carry 0 in-stream `[page N]`; over-fire watch-list proven zero in `outputs/_probe_cedpage.cjs`). ContentConverter captures + suppresses the label run (CEDK101's list sits in the MENU partition, CEDT404's in the BODY — the flag suppresses both), pushes a {sentinel} at each top-level `[page N]` (closing any open activity first), and #inquiryPanels (page_split mode) wraps the body into N UNIFIED crumbs (the first tab IS the intro — NO separate 'Introduction' crumb, distinct from BLL) + N inquiryPanels (first showing). The CONSUMED crumb-list sub-family (CEDO102/CEDT208/CEDW201/CEDW101 — labels eaten by the scanner, oL=0) needs consumed-label recovery (round-101 style) and is a documented follow-up. The crumb/panel index VALUE (0- vs 1-indexed) is editorial + skeleton-invisible (KEEP_ATTR excludes rel/crumb); 1-indexed here matches CEDT404 exactly and is functionally identical for CEDK101. Env CEDPAGE_OFF reverts to today's flat render.
page_split._consumed_crumb_list_doc: ROUND 108 (Chris — anchor_compare CED follow-up) — extends the round-102 CED page-split to the CONSUMED crumb-list cut. MEASURED (outputs/_probe_cedconsumed.cjs): in CEDO102/CEDW101/CEDT208/CEDW201 the `[Tab N]` crumb-list is eaten by a `[tabs]` WIDGET bundle (#0). The labels DO still reach #detectInquiryCed (it scans page.items, not just orphans), so the round-102 detector already SEES them — the real blockers are (a) the alignment formula assumed a leading intro panel ((openers+1)==labels), but the consumed family opens the first ('Introduction') panel ON the first `[page N]` (panels==openers==labels, CEDO102: 6/6/6), and (b) the consuming `[tabs]` widget would ALSO render. This flag accepts the openers==labels alignment AND, when the crumb-list is consumed, suppresses the consuming bundle so only the div.crumbs remains; #inquiryPanels drops the empty leading-intro panel (segs[0]=='' -> N sentinel panels, not N+1). SCOPED tight: only CEDO102 newly fires (clean: bundle ate ONLY the crumb-list, 6 free `[page N]` == 6 labels). CEDW101 (2 stray empty `[Tab N]` -> pure=false) and CEDT208/CEDW201 (panels split by a NON-`[page N]` signal: openers 2/1 != panels 4/5) do NOT fire -- deferred follow-ups, measured. Every real `[tabs]`-widget module still carries 0 in-stream `[page N]` -> no-fire. Env CEDCONSUMED_OFF reverts to the round-102 orphan-only ((openers+1)==labels, no suppression).

lesson_title_dedup._harvest_before_activity_only_note: ROUND 143 (Chris, BLL241-2). PageSplitter harvests a lesson page's header title from its first [H1-5] heading when the [LESSON] tag carried no title. When true, that harvest is restricted to a heading BEFORE the first [Activity] opener (a genuine lesson title) OR an explicit 'Lesson N:' heading — a heading buried AFTER an activity is widget/section content (BLL241-2 [H3] Fog, a clickDrop panel label; HIS1001 section headings), NOT the page title, so it is suppressed (the page keeps its bare label / module title instead of a wrong word). Measured 13/496 lesson sections affected, human titles none of them with the harvested heading. env LESSONTITLE_OFF reverts to first-heading-anywhere.

lesson_name_from_heading.note: ROUND NN (Chris, ENGS302-1.0): when a lesson page is opened by a '[LESSON] N' tag whose only payload is the digit, PageSplitter set page.pageTitle to that bare NUMBER ('1'), so the header <h1><span> showed '1' instead of the lesson NAME, and the existing post-pass that harvests the name from the first '[H2] Lesson N: Name' heading was skipped (it only ran when pageTitle was EMPTY). The post-pass now ALSO fills a pageTitle that is merely the bare lesson number (or label) — extracting the name from the first heading exactly as the empty case does (re-using PageSplitter's robust ^lesson N [:.\-–] strip after a leading-* strip, so italic/bold/plain + ':'/'.'/'-'/'–' variants all work). This cascades to the body de-dup: with the real name in #pageLessonTitle, the round-75 prefix-tolerant test now matches and the duplicate '[H2] Lesson 1: Plot Structure' body heading is consumed. SCOPE-SAFE: measured 0 of 555 human lesson pages title the header with a bare number, so overriding one only helps-or-holds; 63 Claude lesson pages currently show a bare-number title (the bug). Env LESSONNAME_OFF reverts to the bare-number title (and the un-de-duped body heading).

overview.note: ROUND 80 (Chris, ENGC102): the OVERVIEW page's first-body-heading de-dup was DISABLED (the page-lesson-title was forced to ''), so a [MODULE INTRODUCTION] [H1] that repeats the MODULE title leaked as a body <h3> (ENGC102 '[H1] Keeping it real' = the header title 'Keeping it real'). The overview HAS a title — the module English title in the header — so the de-dup now compares the overview's first body heading against that (#pageEnglishTitle), exactly as a lesson page de-dups against its lesson title. EXACT folded match only (measured: in 100% of cases where Claude leaked the dup, the human dropped it — never an over-strip). Env OVDEDUP_OFF reverts to the disabled-on-overview behaviour. NOTE: this needs the lone-title guard (lone_title_maori_guard) so #pageEnglishTitle is the real title, not a Course swap — ENGC102's header title was wrongly 'Communication' before round 80, which is also why the dup slipped through.

lesson_title_dedup.note: Round 75 (Chris, OSBY201-03 issue 1) — the FIRST body heading that repeats the lesson title (already promoted to the header <h1> by PageSplitter) is de-duped. When the writer wrapped that heading WHOLE in *italic* ('[H2] *Lesson 3: Be kind online*') the existing leading-'Lesson N:' strip (anchored on ^lesson) misses it (the string starts with '*'), the prefix survives, and the de-dup never matches 'Be kind online' in the header — leaving a DUPLICATE title in the body (310 corpus pages; the human keeps only 7). strip_lesson_prefix makes the de-dup COMPARE tolerant of a leading 'Lesson N:' on BOTH sides (rendering of any genuinely-kept heading is unchanged). Env LESSONPFX_OFF reverts to the exact-match compare.

activity_interactive_postpass._note: ROUND 58 — post-pass that adds .interactive to a free-body activity div whose depth-balanced span contains a cv2-interactive placeholder declaring an interactive-task widget type (the set in activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types). Closes the activity-missing-.interactive defect for activities whose interactive widget is a SEPARATE inner bundle (not the activity-owner bundle's own type), which the emit-time forceInt at #activityOpen (round 50) misses — e.g. BLL135-01/BLL216 dragAndDrop, BLL145/BLL155 selfCheck, CEDK102/CEDO105 multiChoiceQuiz. Derives from the SAME measured human convention as the round-50 emit rule (dragAndDrop 77% / selfCheck 76% / multiChoiceQuiz 79% .interactive across the 4,345 human files in 02-All_HTML_Files); triangulated on CEDO102/CEDK101/CEDW101 whose human overview carries class="activity interactive". Class-blind to compare_structure (records 'activity' for both) + body_compare; visible only to the structural-defect audit + skeleton (toward the human). Env ACTINT_OFF reverts.
activity_interactive_postpass.marker_format_note: the placeholder type marker 'INTERACTIVE (un-built) #N: TYPE' is a structural constant of interactive_placeholder; the DECISION CONTENT (which types count) is data here via interactive_widget_types.

heading_relevel._supervisor_skip_note:
ROUND 82 (Chris, ENGC101-02). The supervisor-note CALLOUT (elements.supervisor note template) carries a FIXED '

Supervisor note

' label inside its super-content-button box. That label is NOT a free-body section heading, but it sat in the re-level level POOL and PINNED the base rank at h3 — so the page's real writer [H3] section headings (digit + body_shift = h4) could not normalise back DOWN to h3 (ENGC101-02 had TWO supervisor notes, holding the base at h3, leaving 'Conversations'/'Speaking clearly'/'Listening'/'Practise…' stuck at h4 vs the human's h3). Treat the super-content-button box like a widget subtree: its heading is excluded from BOTH the pool and the rewrite (its own fixed h3 is unchanged). Env SUPHEAD_OFF reverts to including the supervisor-note label in the pool.
heading_relevel._activity_anchor_note: ROUND 55 (Chris, OSAI401-01). An activity-title heading is emitted at a FIXED level (h3 — the top content-section level); a free-body [H#] heading is the writer digit + body_shift (+1). So a writer [H3] SECTION heading that is a PEER of the page's activities renders one level too deep: the human renders OSAI401-01 [H3] 'Types of AI' at h3 (peer to the activity titles 'What can AI do'/'Match the AI Tool') and [H4] 'What is Generative AI…' at h4, but Claude — because the activity h3 occupied the base rank in the re-level pool — pushed them to h4/h5. #relevelHeadings now treats activity subtrees like widget subtrees (excluded from BOTH the level POOL and the rewrite), so the free-body [H#] outline ranks from base on its own and the activity titles keep their fixed h3 — the top [H#] then aligns with the activities, matching the human's flatter hierarchy. SELF-SCOPING: the rank map only changes when an activity is the SHALLOWEST anchor (if a real free-body h3 or [H2]→h3 is present it already holds the base, so the outline is unchanged — measured no-op on non-activity-anchored pages). Env RELEVELACT_OFF reverts to including activities in the pool.
heading_relevel.note: DOCUMENT-LEVEL heading re-levelling (round 45, measured): human developers IGNORE the writer's heading digit and re-base every page's body-heading outline to a consistent h3-top hierarchy (measured: 71% of human pages start their body at h3; body headings collapse to h3>h4>h5). The writer's [H?] digit is noise; the human's consistent OUTPUT convention is the signal. ContentConverter.#relevelHeadings runs a post-pass on the assembled #body: the page's DISTINCT free-body heading levels (sorted) map to base_level, base_level+1, … (clamped at max_level) — a rank normalisation. Headings INSIDE a widget subtree (skip_classes) are left untouched (protects the built-widget verifiers + their own heading conventions). Measured rank-based match: writer+1 46.2% -> 57.5% on text-matched body headings; gate-safe (heading level doesn't change the wrapper chain). enabled:false or env RELEVEL_OFF to A/B.
heading_relevel._fixed_level_note:
ROUND 245 (Chris — the SCCH302 developer error log). TEMPLATED CHROME headings the converter emits at a FIXED level with a fixed class must not join the re-level pool. `

Go to your journal

` (r239 B4) is the measured case: the human gold ships it at h4 568/568 = 100%, inside an activity box or standalone, but because it looked like an ordinary free-body heading it was re-ranked with the rest — Claude shipped 110 at h3 and 8 at h5 out of 835, and its presence in the pool also displaced the writer's real headings around it. A heading whose OWN class is listed here is excluded from BOTH the pool and the rewrite (the activity-anchor / supervisor-note exclusion treatment, keyed on the heading's own class rather than an ancestor div). Env FIXEDHEAD_OFF.

alert_table._side_pair_note:
ROUND 94 (Chris, ENGS302-01). The human pairs a RIGHT-positioned alert (col-md-4) in the SAME div.row as the FOLLOWING intro content's col-md-8, not in its own row (verified ENGS302_1.0:
{Welcome +

Under the Skin

+ watch + video}
{Vocab dump}
, then a fresh row at

Understanding the plot

). The round-92 own-row form left the alert structurally orphaned (the rounds 89/91 col-layout lever, deferred). FIX: when side_pair is on and the alert is positional (a real col, not default_col), ContentConverter DEFERS the alert as a pendingSideAlert (the side_col_open/close portion — col + alert box, NO outer row); the following intro content opens a col-md-8 row and FLOWS in (its film-title heading is gathered, not broken) until a media element (the intro video/image) completes the column, then the next row break closes the row with the alert appended as its col-md-4 right sibling. EXACT col-md-8 extent is editorial (lesson 2 pairs a different-sized section) — the SCAFFOLD (row > col-md-8 + col-md-4 > alert.top) matches; scoped to the positional-alert-in-table form (ENGS302 only, per round 92). Env ALERTPAIR_OFF reverts to the round-92 own-row alert.
alert_table._round92_note:
ROUND 92 (Chris, ENGS302-01). Writers AUTHOR a side alert box as a 1x1 TABLE whose single cell leads with the positional tag '[Alert box on right hand side]' (also '[Alert box to the right]', ENGS302 lesson 2) then [H3] title + [Text] + bullets. The cell went through #layoutTableGrid, which DROPPED the [alert] tag and rendered the title/bullets as PLAIN content in the page's default col — no alert box, no positioning. The human renders
{h3 + p + ul}
(verified ENGS302_1.0 lines 89-108). body_region.row_rule: ONE STRUCTURE PER ROW is the dominant gold-standard convention: measured across ALL 2,045 human pages (12/06/26), 51% of rows hold exactly one direct child, 14% two, 13% three. The engine therefore gives every root-level block its own row, with one grouping exception below. Inside an open container/activity, no row breaks ever happen.

row_breaks.flow_blocks_note: ROW GROUPING (round 51 — SHIPPED). Measured via reference/tests/_wt_human_align.py (Chris's WT<->human alignment): the human opens a new top-level div.row only at a HEADING (24%), an ACTIVITY (18%), the page-START/quote (14%) or a CALLOUT (2%), and FLOWS everything else (media, tables, widgets, lists, body) into the current section row. The old group_content rule wrongly gave every media/table/widget its OWN row (the 'rows ratio ~2.0' over-emission; the wall-to-wall +div.row in the OSAI401 skeleton diff). flow_blocks=true makes media/table/widget FLOW; only heading/activity/boxed-callout (kind 'section') break a row (ContentConverter rowFor + the 'section'/'block' call-sites). Also this round: emit() never opens an EMPTY row (a de-duped lesson-title heading returning [] used to leave an empty row>col); and FLOWING callouts (quote/thought) flow into the section row instead of a self-contained box (the page-start quote opens the row and the intro flows in). GATES (full regen): compare_structure 4244/80.0% exact + over-nesting 108 HELD; ROWS RATIO 2.0 -> 1.20 (the over-emission nearly eliminated); body 39/6/87/128 HELD; tags 100%; sentinels 4/7/5/7; 0 leaks; flipCard 14-baseline HELD. Skeleton SCAFFOLD match 45.7 -> 46.6% (the raw % is capped by non-derivable column widths; the width-normalised OSAI401 row structure is ~56%). env ROWGROUP_OFF for A/B.
row_breaks.group_content_note: GROUPED ROWS (scaffolding audit #3, measured 2026-06-15): text and lists FLOW into the current row; a heading starts a fresh row (the text after it flows in); a hard block (media/table/callout/widget/activity/page) takes its own row. Matches the human, where 86% of rows hold 2+ content children (h+p+p and p+p+p dominant) — the old per-block mode over-counted rows ~1.6x. Set false to restore the legacy one-block-per-row behaviour (heading_keeps_next_black_run).
row_breaks.heading_note: LEGACY (used only when group_content=false): a heading keeps its immediately-following text run in the same row. Everything else — each [body] block, video, image, table, callout, button, widget — stands alone.
row_breaks.after_note: Content following a closed callout/activity/widget always starts a fresh row (verified OSAI201_0.0, OSAH401_1.0).

activity_close_before._title_heading_note: An activity's OWN title heading must stay INSIDE the box, never auto-close it. title_heading_tags = heading tags that are ALWAYS the activity's title (an [activity heading] is never a section break). heading_closes_only_after_content: a PLAIN section heading (H2-H5 ≤ rendered_heading_max) is the activity's title when it is the FIRST thing after the [Activity N] opener (before any content) and so stays inside; only AFTER the activity has content is such a heading a section break that closes the activity. Without this, an activity whose title is a SEPARATE heading tag right after the opener (ENGC201-01 1B: '[Activity heading H3] Creating emotion avatars', and 246 such boxes across 59 modules) auto-closed EMPTY, spilling its heading/body/list/video OUTSIDE the box. Before this, a [H3] rendered h4 > 3 slipped past, so the activity 3B (S.A.F.E) swallowed the following [H3] 'The banter trap' + body + table until the next [Activity] tag. Measured 197-set (outputs/_probe_activity_heading.cjs): the FIRST top-level post-content heading after an [Activity] is [H3] x469 (77% with a new [Activity] following — a section break) vs [H4] x84 / [H5] x21 (sub-headings, kept inside). The title protection (heading_closes_only_after_content) still keeps a [H3] activity TITLE inside. Env ACTHEAD_OFF reverts to rendered_heading_max_legacy (3).

THE NEW-ERA WRITER LESSON NUMBERING: the newest WT era numbers lessons ALREADY DOTTED ([Lesson 0.0]/[Lesson 1.0]/[Lesson 2.1]) and closes in-lesson TILE structures with [end tile lesson navigate back to lesson N]. Three coupled PageSplitter rules, measured over all 428 WTs (outputs/_measure_wtlessonnums.cjs): (1) overview_zero_pattern — a [Lesson 0/0.0] while the OVERVIEW is open is the overview's own number (the module introduction), consumed, content stays on 0.0 (population EXACTLY ENGJ403; env ZEROLESSON_OFF); (2) dotted_label_verbatim — a dotted writer number is the page label VERBATIM ('2.1' not '2.1.0'; population ENGJ403 + CEDK501/CEDO501/CEDR501/CEDT501/CEDW501/XMES202, whose golds ship the same '2.1'-style pages; un-dotted '[Lesson 4]' keeps the historical '.0'; env DOTLESSON_OFF); (3) tile_closer_pattern — an 'end lesson' closer whose own text matches the tile pattern is an IN-PAGE structure closer, never a page boundary (population EXACTLY ENGJ403 ×2; env TILECLOSER_OFF).
page_split._doc_lesson_boundary_guard:
ROUND 245 (Chris — the ENGS404 developer test: 22 files for 12 lessons). TWO measured PageSplitter guards on what counts as a lesson page boundary. Detector outputs/_detect_r245_lessonsplit.cjs, run over ALL 429 corpus WTs + the 3 ZZ-HumanDev test modules (1549 lesson/page PAGE_BOUNDARY spans).

(1) duplicate_number_merge — THE DIVIDER-BANNER FORM. A WT house convention writes the lesson number TWICE: an all-caps banner on the divider page right after [End page] ('[LESSON 1.0]'), then the real titled opener ('[Lesson 1.0] Elements of narrative'), with ONLY the lesson-MENU region between them ([Lesson Overview] + the black We-are-learning / I-can run). The banner opened an empty file and the duplicate-label relabeller then cascaded EVERY later lesson number (ENGS404 shipped 22 pages incl. 9 header-only files). When a [Lesson N] marker's number equals the OPEN lesson page's number AND that page has received NO BODY content yet, the marker is merged into the open page (its title adopted if the page has none) instead of opening a new one. 'Body content' = a table or a tag whose directive is ELEMENT/INTERACTIVE/CONTAINER_OPEN/INLINE; the menu region's SECTION_MARKERs and black text do NOT count — that material belongs to the same lesson either way. MEASURED: 13 same-number pairs corpus-wide; the no-body rule fires on EXACTLY 9 (ENGS404 ×7 + HIS1005 ×2) and by construction EXCLUDES the 4 pairs where the writer genuinely reused a number across real content (CEDO501 bodyish=32, HES1005 bodyish=69, AGH1006 bodyish=20, HIS1007 bodyish=14). Corpus blast: HIS1005 only. Env LESSONDUP_OFF.

(2) instruction_guard — THE BURIED-MARKER FORM. A span becomes a lesson/page boundary merely because the word 'lesson'/'page' appears inside writer prose ('[insert lesson from ENO511 …]' → a page numbered 511; '[Designer note: Please insert old lesson from here…]'; '[Rollover for mana: … complete History fundamental lesson 7 …]'). NECESSARY CONDITION, and the containment statement: the primary must have matched how:'embedded' (the r174 clean_hows distinction) — the 1479 of 1549 boundaries that matched exact/denumbered/denumbered_head are untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION. Within that 70-span pool the marker is disregarded when EITHER the span is instruction-dominant by the EXISTING TagNormaliser.IsInstructionDominant predicate (all tags embedded + a recognised writer-instruction cue + >= min_words of prose — 8 spans / 7 modules), OR the bracket names a FOREIGN module code (foreign_code_pattern, any position, the run's own code excluded — the cross-module 'copy that lesson' reference form: '[insert lesson from ENO511 …]', '[Copy PHO1032 lesson 8]', '[PHO1011 lesson 5.1-5.3]'), OR the text BEFORE the marker word carries a hover/rollover marker word (deny_lead_pattern — '[Rollover for mana: … complete History fundamental lesson 7 …]' is a hover trigger whose DEFINITION mentions a lesson: vocabulary, not structure). FAIL-OPEN by design: an unrecognised embedded form keeps today's behaviour. Verified against the full 70-span pool: every genuine embedded marker survives ([Lesson summary] ×14, [lesson title] ×8, [Lesson Two] ×2, [Lesson six], [Final Page] ×2, [Next Page] ×4, [New Page …] ×2, [Intro page] ×2, [ILanding page], [Page N of diary] ×2, [page ends]); the r212 [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] and r226 [Sticky Nav Layout …] forms are consumed EARLIER in the same branch and never reach this guard. Named delta: HIS1001's '[Can you please make a map …]' page disappears — unambiguously not a boundary, though that module is already UNDER its gold page count for an unrelated reason. Env LESSONGUARD_OFF. DELIBERATELY NARROW (round-245 calibration): a broader leading-instruction-verb deny (insert/copy/create/from) was measured and REJECTED — it also removed ENGI405's '[insert zones writing wheel from this page' and ART1006's '[Create two new colour boxes … page called the', both of which happen to sit where the human developer DID break the page, so the count moved AWAY from gold (ENGI405 8->7 against a gold of 8). Those forms keep today's behaviour: fail-open is the safe direction, and the two rules kept here are the ones no reading of the writer's intent can dispute. Corpus effect measured module by module against the gold page count: PES1004 12->11 (gold 11, EXACT), PES1007 12->11 (gold 11, EXACT), CEDR501 12->11 (gold 10, toward), HIS1008 13->12 (gold 10, toward), HIS1001 no pagination change at all (content only), PES1008 toward, HIS1005 see duplicate_number_merge.

formatter._comment:
ROUND 243 (Dev-Feedback R6, E4): block-level line breaking. The emitters glue structural runs onto one line (
, ......); the human gold breaks every mixed div/table-structural glued boundary onto its own line (measured broken-share 0.88-1.00, _measure_r243_linebreaks.py) and keeps ONLY the empty-element one-liners glued (
0.018 broken, 0.010, 0.000). HtmlFormatter.Indent splits a zero-whitespace >< boundary when BOTH tags are in `tags`, EXCEPT an open tag immediately followed by its own close (the empty-element exception). Whitespace-only between tags, never inside a text node - semantically byte-inert; every protected gate parses via html.parser + \s+ normalisation. Env LINEBREAK_OFF reverts to the glued round-242 form.

reference_module._doc: ROUND 249 — the HTML Generator's REFERENCE-MODULE feature (Chris, 2026-08-05). The upload UI names the SUGGESTED reference module (advisory-only — PrecedenceResolver.SuggestReference over the library index; changes nothing), lets the person PICK a different library module (PrepareRun referenceCode -> the structural rules re-resolve as that module's), or — when no suitable module exists — UPLOAD the reference module's finished HTML pages (PrepareRun referenceHtmlFiles -> ReferenceMiner.Distil mines the Style-Anchor tracked fields, applies them live, and ships the distilled template as {code}_reference-template.json for Chris to add to the templated modules). The batch harness passes neither option, so every batch/corpus conversion is byte-identical to the pre-round engine BY CONSTRUCTION. Env REFMOD_OFF reverts the overrides + the distilled output; enabled:false does the same from data.

custom_template._doc: ROUND 263b (Gavin) — the 'Make your own template' choice: the person picks a subject + phase + template and ReferenceMiner.PickBySpec inherits the structure from the MOST TYPICAL library module of the narrowest matching pool. THE TEMPLATE IS NEVER RELAXED (each template is a separate beast — Fundamentals/Inquiry are one-page formats — so it dictates the content/lesson layout); when no module matches all three choices the pool widens by dropping phase first, then subject, always keeping the template. 'Most typical' = the pool member agreeing with the per-field majority of the Style-Anchor tracked fields on the most fields (ties → most recently built). Rides the parent enabled flag + REFMOD_OFF.

reference_module._mining_doc: ROUND 263 (module SCCH302 — the SCCH301 distil run): two miner corrections, both data-flagged above and reverted with the whole feature by REFMOD_OFF. chip_padded_detect — a zero-padded two-digit lesson chip ('01'..'09', the SCCH301 gold form) mines as 'padded-number' instead of being mis-read as 'decimal' (which renders '1.0'). tooltip_content_scan — the menu tooltip attribute is also read off the module-menu-content div (94 gold pages carry it there; 503 carry it on the button — the converter emits the button form either way, this only fixes the MINED yes/no).
